There are two ways to access Campaign registration. The correct starting point depends on whether you are completing registration for the first time or adding a Campaign to an existing approved Brand.

If you are completing A2P registration for the first time, you may continue into **Campaign Details** after completing the Brand Registration steps.

If your Brand is already approved and you want to create another Campaign, start from Trust Center.

Step 1

Navigate to Trust Center

Navigate to **Settings > Phone System > Trust Center**. In the A2P Messaging (SMS) card, click **Brand & Campaigns**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077175440/original/65YK636Ftk3aK0CqZDEyvuPQGxQI-TmoXQ.jpeg?1785347277)

Step 2

Create a Campaign

Open the **Campaigns** tab, then click **Create Campaign**. From the dropdown, select the Brand you want to create the Campaign for. After selecting the Brand, you will enter the Campaign setup flow described in this article.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077175463/original/28M7dnFv8xqPgr0RF_OtdUy3r_aIjUgg9Q.jpeg?1785347315)

## How to Register an A2P Campaign

After accessing Campaign registration, complete the Campaign setup steps below. Your Brand type, messaging volume, use case, and consent method determine the information required during registration.

Step 1

Select Your Messaging Volume

The first step in Campaign details is selecting your messaging volume. The available options depend on your Brand type.

**If you have a Tax ID**, choose the messaging volume option that best matches your business texting needs.

| Standard Brand Option | Best For | Key Information |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low Volume Standard Brand | Registered businesses with lower messaging volume and throughput needs. | Supports multiple phone numbers. Allows up to 6,000 SMS segments per day. Lower cost than High Volume.\* |
| High Volume Standard Brand | Registered businesses that send larger volumes of messages and require higher throughput. | Supports multiple phone numbers. Allows up to 600,000 SMS segments per day. Higher cost than Low Volume.\* |

\*For specific pricing information, see: [A2P 10DLC Messaging Fees: Registration, Monthly, and Carrier Costs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005200).

**If you do not have a Tax ID,** the only available option is Single-number registration. Only one number can be linked to this registration. You can change the number later.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077175477/original/x4Wm53WKpNPlzL3bH6UdU4_A47hJpOM-vw.jpeg?1785347341)

Step 2

Choose Chat Widget Setup or Manual Setup

Campaign registration opens in **Chat Widget Setup** by default after you complete Brand registration. Chat Widget Setup uses a HighLevel-generated opt-in widget and pre-fills Campaign information to simplify registration.

If your business collects SMS consent through another method, select **Switch to manual setup** from the Chat Widget Setup screen. Manual Setup lets you provide your existing consent method and Campaign information.

You can return to Chat Widget Setup from Manual Setup by selecting **Chat widget setup — recommended** in the Campaign details step panel.

If you are using **Chat Widget Setup**, continue to [**Step 3A: Complete Chat Widget Setup**](#Complete-Chat-Widget-Setup).

If you selected **Manual Setup**, continue to [**Step 3B: Complete Manual Setup**](#Complete-Manual-Setup).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077175598/original/HCMuD1klhuPmKQrixoclFaYCgi5Y6yOxKA.jpeg?1785347421)

Chat Widget Setup Path

### Complete Chat Widget Setup

Follow these steps when using the guided Chat Widget Setup path. For Manual Setup, skip to Step 3B below.

Step 3A: Chat Widget Setup

### Messaging Use Case, Widget Setup, and Compliance

Chat Widget Setup combines messaging-use-case selection, website information, widget installation, and consent configuration into a guided registration experience.

1. Messaging Use Case & Website Details

- **Messaging use case:**Choose the option that accurately represents your messaging program:
  - **Marketing / Promotional** for promotional messaging.
  - **Informational / Non-Marketing** for transactional or informational messaging.
  - **Mixed** when the same messaging program includes both promotional and informational communication.
- When **Mixed** is selected, HighLevel automatically sets the Campaign Use Case to **Low Volume Mixed**.
- **Your business website URL:** Enter the website where users will provide consent to receive messages. This should be a live, publicly accessible site that represents your business and matches the information provided in your Brand registration. The website should clearly display your business name and contact details.
- **Age-gated content checkbox:** Select this option only if your business sends age-restricted content.

**Using Mixed?** For additional details about the Mixed option, Low Volume Mixed assignment, and the generated dual-consent experience, see [Mixed Use-Case Support for Chat Widget Flow](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008722-mixed-use-case-support-for-chat-widget-flow).

2. Copy & Install the Widget Code

Copy the widget code provided in Chat Widget Setup and install it on your website. Click **Copy code**, then paste the snippet into the `<body>` or footer section of your website. If needed, use **Customize widget** to adjust supported appearance settings before installation.

Make sure the widget is fully installed and visible on your website before continuing.

3. Website Compliance Check

The Chat Widget should be the only form on the submitted page collecting SMS consent.

Do not place the widget on a submitted page that also contains another SMS opt-in form, such as a Contact Form, Lead Capture Form, or Appointment Form.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176179/original/l0EtHDpRUzgYT_-faVbO32WH70qMSWTHyw.png?1785347803)

### Switch to Manual Setup

If your business collects SMS consent through a method other than the Chat Widget, select **Switch to manual setup** below the Chat Widget Setup screen. Use Manual Setup when you need to provide a different approved consent method.

Compliance Tip

For more detailed guidance on compliance requirements and examples, see [A2P 10DLC Campaign Approval Best Practices](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001229784-a2p-10dlc-campaign-approval-best-practices).

Step 4A: User Consent

After completing Chat Widget Setup, HighLevel automatically fills in the inputs for Use Case Description, Sample Message #1, Sample Message #2, How do Contacts Opt-in to Messages, and the Opt-in Message.

If **Mixed** is selected, the generated Chat Widget includes two independent consent checkboxes: one for informational/transactional messaging and one for marketing/promotional messaging. Neither checkbox is pre-selected, and each consent choice includes its own locked disclosure content.

Review the generated information carefully to ensure it matches your business and messaging intent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176203/original/Mbdu75m3e4HMncMxe52LwrBbK7OUNNhZEw.jpeg?1785347850)

Step 5A: Business Website Compliance Checklist

The website compliance checklist helps confirm that the submitted business information, consent experience, and required website content are accessible before the Campaign moves to final review.

After reviewing all checklist items, select the blue **Review Application** button, then continue to Step 6.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176244/original/N_U6s4jOnshqz0G9DeahPaHXTwM-cwB9RA.jpeg?1785347879)

Manual Setup Path

### Complete Manual Setup

Use Manual Setup when your business collects consent through a method other than the HighLevel Chat Widget. From Chat Widget Setup, select **Switch to manual setup** to continue with the Manual Setup flow.

Complete the required Campaign details and consent information for your existing opt-in method.

For Chat Widget Setup, see Step 3A above.

**Tip:** To return to Chat Widget Setup, select **Chat widget setup — recommended** from the Campaign details step panel.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080122899/original/xl7K28ndrBcqa-L_uuzpN50QKcb-mHU5yA.png?1788531366)

Step 3B: Campaign Details

Manual Setup requires you to provide the Campaign information and consent details that would otherwise be generated through Chat Widget Setup. Keep every field aligned with the selected Campaign use case and the messaging program recipients will actually receive.

**Campaign Use Case:** Select the use case that best matches the type of messages your business will send. This should align with your business purpose, messages, and opt-in method. For detailed information, see [A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Cases](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000235).

**Website URL:** Enter a live, publicly accessible business website that represents your business and matches the information provided during Brand registration.

**Use Case Description:** Explain who sends the messages, who receives them, what messages are sent, and how contacts opt in. The description should match the selected use case and sample messages.

**Sample Messages:** Enter realistic examples of the SMS your business will send. Samples should identify the sender, align with the selected use case, and include applicable opt-out language. Do not include custom fields or values in sample messages.

**Additional Message Details:** Select applicable options such as links, phone numbers, age-gated content, or financial-related content. These selections may affect compliance requirements.

Helpful Tip

Click **See Example** in HighLevel for guidance on completing these fields.

For detailed requirements and examples, see [A2P 10DLC Campaign Approval Best Practices](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001229784-a2p-10dlc-campaign-approval-best-practices).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176288/original/w24DXJ8Im_oeKHP2TlnzaBdB0uJGbVJ9aQ.png?1785347911)

Important

If you have an EIN for your company but want to use a different brand name for your messages, you can add the sentence "We are doing DBA as [Business\_Name]" in the Campaign Use Case.

Make sure the rest of the submission, including the website, Privacy Policy, Terms & Conditions, and business name shown in opt-in form checkboxes, matches the declared [Legal Business Name] DBA [DBA Name]. You can register the same EIN for up to 10 brands.

Step 4B: User Consent

Manual Setup requires clear documentation of how contacts provide permission to receive SMS. The opt-in method, consent language, and supporting URLs should align with the Campaign use case and sample messages.

**Opt-In Method:** Select how contacts opt in to receive messages. Common options include website forms, paper forms, Facebook lead forms, QR codes, kiosks, or verbal consent.

**Opt-in Form URL:** Enter a publicly accessible URL that shows where users provide their phone number and opt in. If the method is not publicly visible, provide a hosted image or public link that clearly shows the opt-in flow.

**Description of Opt-In Flow:** Explain where contacts provide their phone number, what language they see, whether opt-in is optional, and what messages they agree to receive.

**Opt-in Message:** Enter the consent or confirmation language shown to users. It should align with the Campaign use case and include applicable program/company identification, message frequency, message and data rate disclosure, HELP instructions, and STOP instructions.

**Privacy Policy URL:** Provide a publicly accessible link to your Privacy Policy.

**Terms & Conditions URL:** Provide a publicly accessible link to your Terms & Conditions.

Helpful Tip

Click **See Example** in HighLevel for guidance on completing these fields.

For detailed requirements and examples, see [A2P 10DLC Campaign Approval Best Practices](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001229784-a2p-10dlc-campaign-approval-best-practices).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176309/original/-XXgaagGJdejovzrihZX7FQQtXwKJypITA.png?1785347944)

Step 5B: Business Website Compliance Checklist

Reviewing the website checklist before submission helps ensure reviewers can verify the business, consent method, and required legal information associated with the Campaign.

After reviewing all checklist items, select the blue **Review Application** button. Then continue to Step 6.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176318/original/PPKJfhjeuOdyZMMrZR-w7tgBGmveeW5ppQ.png?1785347965)

### Step 6: Run AI Compliance Review and Submit

The compliance review checks Campaign and website information for issues that should be corrected before submission. Passing these checks prepares the application for carrier review but does not guarantee final approval.

Click **Review Application** to run the AI compliance review.

If any checks fail, review the issue, fix the required item, and click **Review Again**. You cannot submit the Campaign until all required compliance checks pass. Once the checks pass, submit your Campaign for carrier review.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077176331/original/DUM4Cqnp3ci1lTVLEPJTQ5zjGZ0BIWM7hg.jpeg?1785347998)

## After Your A2P Campaign is Approved

An approved Campaign can only be used successfully when the applicable sending phone number is associated with that Campaign. Verifying the number-to-Campaign connection prevents an approved registration from appearing complete while SMS is still unable to use the A2P route.

To confirm your number is ready:

1. Go to **Settings > Phone System > Phone Numbers**.
2. Locate the phone number you want to use for messaging.
3. Confirm that the number displays the green **A2P Verified** label.
4. If the label is missing, link the number to the approved A2P Campaign.
5. Repeat this check whenever you purchase or add another applicable local number.

For step-by-step instructions, see [How to Link a Phone Number to an Approved A2P Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008316).

## Troubleshooting A2P After Submission

Campaign status helps identify whether you should wait for review, correct a rejection, or troubleshoot the phone number after approval. Use the status before creating another Campaign or making unrelated changes.

| Campaign Status | What It Means | What to Do Next | Resources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Pending** | Your Campaign is still being reviewed. | Wait for the review to finish. Do not create another Campaign or resubmit while the current Campaign is Pending. | — |
| **Rejected** | One or more issues were identified during review. | Open **View required fixes →** for every rejection reason and correct all applicable issues before taking the next action. | [A2P Campaign Rejections, Required Fixes & Vetting Errors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007572) |
| **Approved, but SMS still isn't working** | The Campaign is approved, but the sending number may not be linked correctly or the SMS failure may have another cause. | Verify the sending number is linked to the approved Campaign and displays **A2P Verified**. If it is already verified, troubleshoot the SMS error. | [Error 30034: How to Link a Phone Number to an Approved A2P Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008316) |

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens when I select Mixed in Chat Widget Setup?

HighLevel automatically sets the Campaign Use Case to **Low Volume Mixed**. The generated Chat Widget also includes separate consent checkboxes for informational/transactional and marketing/promotional messaging, and neither checkbox is pre-selected.

Q: How will Campaign vetting affect a newly submitted Campaign?

A newly submitted Campaign remains in a Pending state until the applicable vetting and approval process is complete. Compliant messaging can use the A2P route after the Campaign is fully approved and the applicable number is properly linked.

Q: What should I do if my Campaign is rejected?

Open **View required fixes** and review every rejection reason. Correct all applicable issues before taking the next action. If additional assistance is needed after reviewing the required fixes, contact Support.

Q: Is Toll-Free messaging an alternative to A2P 10DLC?

Yes. Toll-Free messaging uses a separate verification process and does not rely on A2P 10DLC Brand and Campaign registration.

Q: Does HighLevel add a markup to A2P fees?

No. A2P registration, vetting, monthly Campaign, and applicable carrier messaging fees are passed through without a HighLevel markup.

title_en: Zoom Integration for Users' Calendar Bookings
source_md:
**Note**: Dynamic Zoom links are only available with Personal , Round Robin and Collective Calendars.

Zoom is a communications platform that allows users to connect with video, audio, phone, and chat simultaneously! Integrating your Zoom account with group calendars is easy to set up and is a great way to take your productivity to the next level. By syncing your Zoom account with your calendar(s), you can quickly schedule appointments, send out reminders, and keep track of upcoming events - all in one place!

#### **Covered in this Article:**

#### [**What Is the Zoom Integration?**](#What-Is-the-Zoom-Integration?)

#### [Usage cases](#Usage-cases)

#### [Benefits of this feature:](#Benefits-of-this-feature%3A)

#### [**Integration Prerequisites**](#Integration-Prerequisites%C2%A0)

#### [Integrating the same Zoom Account with Multiple Users](#Integrating-the-same-Zoom-Account-with-Multiple-Users)

#### [**Step 1: Install the Zoom integration**](#Step-1%3A-Install-the-Zoom-integration)

#### [**Configure Zoom for Other Users as an Admin**](#Configure-Zoom-for-Other-Users-as-an-Admin)

#### [**Step 2: Set up appointment reminder workflow with Zoom location**](#Step-2%3A-Set-up-appointment-reminder-workflow-with-Zoom-location)

#### [**FAQs**](#FAQs)

- [I don't have a Profile tab on my sidebar.](#I-don't-have-a-Profile-tab-on-my-sidebar.)
- [Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Edited](#Handling-Meeting-Links-when-Meetings-are-Edited)
- [Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Deleted](#Handling-Meeting-Links-when-Meetings-are-Deleted)
- [Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Rescheduled to a different time](#Handling-Meeting-Links-when-Meetings-are-Rescheduled-to-a-different-time)
- [Handling Multiple Zoom Meetings at the Same Time Slot](#Handling-Multiple-Zoom-Meetings-at-the-Same-Time-Slot)
- [Existing Zoom Events Not Reflecting in the Calendar](#Existing-Zoom-Events-Not-Reflecting-in-the-Calendar)
- [Calendar Version Support](#Calendar-Version-Support)
- [How do I integrate my Zoom account with an unassigned calendar](#How-do-I-integrate-my-Zoom-account-with-an-unassigned-calendar)

---

## **What Is the Zoom Integration?**

**[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/nmgRNlT1aFo)**

The Zoom integration with this CRM allows users to schedule, start, and manage Zoom meetings directly from within the platform. This provides a seamless experience for users, removing the need to switch between different applications and platforms.

Once the Zoom integration is set up within the CRM, it is capable of dynamically generating unique Zoom meeting links for each new meeting that is scheduled. This process is automatic when the meeting location in the user availability and calendar settings is set to Zoom.

This unique meeting link generation is a significant feature as it provides added security and reduces the chance of unwanted interruptions during your meetings. Each participant gets a different link, making it harder for unauthorized persons to gain access.

For instance, if you're scheduling a meeting with a client, once you select Zoom as the meeting location, the CRM will automatically create a new Zoom meeting and embed the unique meeting link within the calendar event. The client will receive an invitation to the meeting with the unique Zoom link. This link is for that single meeting, providing convenience and security for all parties involved.

In addition, the Zoom integration enables you to keep track of all these meetings within the CRM. All scheduled Zoom meetings are automatically documented within the platform, making managing your appointments and keeping track of your engagements easier.

### **Usage cases**

**Team Meetings**: Make team collaboration easy with Zoom integration. A unique Zoom link is generated automatically each time a meeting is set, simplifying communication within your team.

**Client Consultations:**Streamline your client consultations with this integration. It automatically creates a unique Zoom link every time a client books a meeting, adding a layer of professionalism and ease to your interactions.

**Webinars:** Enhance your webinar experience with the Zoom integration. As a participant registers, a personalized Zoom link is automatically created, making webinar management seamless and efficient.

**Virtual Office Hours:**Teachers and professors can use the Zoom integration to manage office hours or extra help sessions efficiently. A unique Zoom meeting is created when students book a slot, eliminating scheduling hassles.

**Online Fitness Classes:**Fitness instructors can leverage this integration for effortless class management. Every time a client books a session, a unique Zoom link is sent out, providing a smooth virtual fitness experience.

**Virtual Real Estate Showings:** Transform your business with Zoom integration. As potential buyers schedule a showing, the system creates a unique Zoom meeting, bringing property viewing to their comfort zone.

**Telemedicine Appointments:** Make healthcare more accessible with Zoom integration. A unique Zoom meeting is created upon a patient booking an appointment, bringing healthcare services closer to home.

**Online Cooking Classes:** Start your cooking class experience with the Zoom integration. A personalized Zoom link is generated when a participant registers, bringing your culinary expertise to their kitchen.

### **Benefits of this feature:**

Here are some technical advantages of the Zoom integration feature:

**Automated Meeting Scheduling:**A unique Zoom link is generated automatically for each meeting once the integration is set up. This saves significant time on manual setup and prevents errors.

**Centralized Management:**The integration allows users to manage all aspects of meetings, including scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellations, directly from the CRM. This centralization improves efficiency and reduces the likelihood of miscommunication.

**Multi-User Accessibility:**Regardless of the number of participants, a unique Zoom link is automatically generated for each participant. This ensures security and improves the overall meeting experience.

**Calendar Syncing:** The integration allows Zoom meeting scheduling to be directly synced with the CRM calendar. This feature eliminates double booking and enhances time management.

**Real-time Updates:** Changes made in the CRM, such as rescheduling or cancellations, are reflected in real-time in the Zoom platform, thus reducing discrepancies and improving overall coordination.

**Enhanced Security:** Each meeting has a unique link, reducing the risk of uninvited guests joining a meeting.

**Automated Notifications:**The integration automatically sends participants notifications with meeting details and changes. This reduces the manual effort of sending out messages and improves meeting attendance.

**Data Tracking:** The integration allows for comprehensive tracking of meeting data, including attendance, meeting duration, and more. This can help in analyzing patterns and improving business processes.

---

## **Integration Prerequisites**

• Any User can start using Zoom Integration for Calendars

• Each User connects their own Zoom account to their Profile, and a unique link is generated with every booking on each Group Calendar(s) the User is assigned to

• Dynamic Zoom links are only available with Round Robin and Collective Calendars.

### **Integrating the same Zoom Account with Multiple Users**

Zoom integration is tied to unique User IDs in the backend, not email addresses. Zoom connections now support using the same Zoom account across multiple users and across multiple locations. To manage shared connections, use Calendars → Settings → Connections → Video Conferencing.

This can cause issues for users with different email addresses within the same agency or users needing to connect their Zoom accounts across multiple agencies.

In specific scenarios, if a user account is deleted and restored with the help of Support, it could result in two User IDs associated with the same email address. This could lead to further complications as the restored account couldn't reconnect to the original Zoom account due to the new User ID.

It's crucial to remember that User IDs and email addresses are treated as distinct identifiers within the system, underpinning the integration with Zoom. It's essential to consider your User ID as the unique identifier for the integration, not your email address.

This might seem complex, but understanding this distinction will help avoid potential integration issues and alleviate frustrations.

Let's use some examples for a better understanding.

Consider an agency, "ABC Marketing." They have three users:

User A with User ID "A001" and email "a@abcmarketing.com"

User B with User ID "B002" and email "b@abcmarketing.com"

User C with User ID "C003" and email "c@abcmarketing.com"

Users want to integrate their Zoom accounts with their respective profiles on the agency's platform.

User A connects their Zoom account successfully with the User ID "A001". Suppose, for some reason, User A's Profile is deleted and restored by the client contacting Support. Upon restoration, User A is assigned a new User ID, let's say "A004", while their email remains "a@abcmarketing.com."

Here's where the confusion can start. User A tries to reconnect their Zoom account. However, their Zoom account is still tied to the old User ID "A001". Therefore, when they attempt to connect using the new User ID "A004", the system blocks it. This is because, from the system's perspective, the Zoom account is already connected to a different User ID.

This is why it's crucial to remember that Zoom integration is linked to the User ID, not the email address. The system treats the User ID as the unique identifier when connecting to Zoom, even if the email address remains the same.

On another note, User A cannot integrate their Zoom account into User B's Profile either because the Zoom account is still tied to User ID "A001". So, even though they are within the same agency, they cannot share a Zoom account due to these unique User IDs.

Understanding this underlying mechanism should help avoid confusion and ease the integration process.

```
Please note: It is not recommended to connect different Zoom accounts to the same User across multiple sub-accounts or to use the same Zoom account across multiple users. 
```

## ---

## **Use one Zoom account across locations & users**

You can connect the same Zoom account in multiple locations and use it across multiple users.

- Same account across locations: You can connect the same Zoom account in multiple locations.
- Same account across users: Multiple users can connect and use the same Zoom account.
- Limit: A user can connect one Zoom account per location.

### **Dynamic links requirement**

Dynamic Zoom links are created only when the connected Zoom account is selected as the meeting location in the calendar.

### **Remove or switch the connected Zoom account**

You can remove or switch the connected Zoom account from:  
  
Connections → Video Conferencing

1. Go to Calendars → Settings → Connections → Video Conferencing.
2. Remove the existing Zoom connection or connect a different Zoom account.
3. Confirm the meeting location setting on any calendars that should generate dynamic Zoom links.

---

## **Step 1: Install the Zoom integration**

You can configure Zoom for your scheduled meetings in the following ways:

- **User Integrations**  
  - User Profile > Integrations > Zoom > Connect
  - In the dialog box, click **Connect to Zoom (If not already connected)**
  - Enter your Zoom login credentials, then click **Sign in**.
  - You'll be prompted to grant permission for *Zoom* to access your Zoom account. Click **Allow**.
  - You'll be redirected to the platform, where Zoom appears under User Profile Integrations.
- **Default Meeting Location**  
  - User Profile > Default Meeting Location > Zoom > Connect
  - In the dialog box, click **Connect to Zoom (If not already connected)**
  - Enter your Zoom login credentials, then click **Sign in**.
  - You'll be prompted to grant permission for *Zoom* to access your Zoom account. Click **Allow**.
  - You'll be redirected to the platform, where Zoom appears under User Profile Integrations.
  - You can then select 'Zoom' from the dropdown and hit 'Save' to prompt a dialog ascertaining whether or not existing meeting locations across all other calendars need to default to Zoom.
- **Calendar Settings**  
  - Settings > Calendar Settings > User [x] > Meeting Location
  - In the dialog box, click **Connect to Zoom (If not already connected)**
  - Enter your Zoom login credentials, then click **Sign in**.
  - You'll be prompted to grant permission for *Zoom* to access your Zoom account. Click **Allow**.
  - You'll be redirected to the platform, where Zoom appears under User Profile Integrations.
  - You can then select 'Zoom' from the dropdown to have the meetings include Zoom links with every booking.

```
Please note: You must be logged in as the user to do the profile setting integration options. If you are unable to find the Profile setting option within the sub account-level settings, you must edit the user's role from the agency-level Team setting to assign the user to the specific location(s). 
```

---

## **Configure Zoom for Other Users as an Admin**

If the Zoom integration has already been installed in your account by the respective User, you can choose that as a Default Meeting Location for the User under Team Management.

```
Please note: Each User has to be currently log into their account to integrate Zoom. Agency admins can now use the "Login As User" Feature to complete this process for any user in the agency.
```

---

## **Step 2: Set up appointment reminder workflow with Zoom location**

[The Workflow Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001179678-workflow-builder-overview) is a potent tool with many uses. Still, for this use case, it provides easy access to automate internal and external reminders of upcoming appointments, including the dynamic Zoom link. You can craft your workflow by combining the following triggers and actions or use one of the available templated Recipes.  by

- Click on "**Add New Workflow Trigger**"  
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206660/original/S3Jj3DZ7tw5oVVrf675riHl1iYjyzSLZsA.png?1685555017)

- Select "**Appointment Status**" as the trigger and add the following filters:  
    
  - Event Type: Is this a one-time appointment, a recurring appointment, or would you like it to fire for either
  - Appointment Status: The calendar setting for auto-confirming appointments would ensure all appointments trigger this filter
  - In Calendar: Optional if narrowing down specific calendars and specific users.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206662/original/yPxrWPmscg8nb2ajniYeIIK41mZBuhgzNQ.png?1685555017)

- Click on "**Add your first Action.**"

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206661/original/UKPzULnHxI0XGo-sHcaDI4wjAnTXDNAEFQ.png?1685555017)

- The first action needed is a one-minute time delay "**Wait**"step to ensure the meeting location value is updated.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206664/original/iGbrgntY2P6mG-d7jRX-OOtWDozGO88BpQ.png?1685555018)

- The following action steps would begin your appointment booked confirmation notifications: "**Send Email/SMS**" would notify the contact on their listed primary email and phone number. Be sure to include the custom value {{appointment.meeting\_location}} in your messages to provide them with the dynamic zoom link.Zoom  
    
  For a link to custom values/merge fields available, please [CLICK HERE](https://gohighlevelassist.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/48001078171-custom-values-merge-fields).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206666/original/n3MremtNoREea-aDu7-xIMMGxJS8Pxlo3g.png?1685555020)

- Optionally, you can include email, sms, and in-app appointment reminders to the assigned User or any external contact using the "**Internal Notification"** action.

```
Best Practice: If sending internal notification email, use do-not-reply@agency.com or notifications@agency.com to ensure no confusion with contact initiated conversations.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206665/original/IzaXTOV1gVRvWBNGhf3wL1g1fRhL_0kHYw.png?1685555020)

- The last step is defining the cadence of notifications using the "**Event/Appointment Time**" wait for action in unison with the previous **Send Email/SMS** and **Internal Notification actions**.   
    
  - Specify how long you want to send the next reminder before the event. In this example, it will wait for 24 hours before the following action (send email/sms or internal notification) will fire.
  - meeting  
      
    - Move to the next step: fire the next action and follow the workflow linearly.
    - Move to a specific step: this will move the lead to a particular action in the workflow.
    - Skip all outbound communication actions until the next wait step: Will not send any email/sms and moves the lead through the workflow linearly until the next wait step.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206669/original/HpmFx3C2NsvtOxSYnc1ydHloPe5Gyx_iIA.png?1685555020)

---

## **FAQs**

### **I don't have a Profile tab on my sidebar.**

If you do not see the "**Profile**" tab on your sidebar, you are not a user/employee within that respective sub-account/location. Please add yourself to that sub-account as a user by clicking **My Staff > + Add Employee > Add Employee >Save.**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206667/original/Nzf6NA_NPQE2hJ4Tx1ZhVUIwnKewEeCvVg.png?1685555020)

If you want to add your agency user profile to this sub-account as an employee, please head back to your **Agency View > Agency Settings >** Click on the**"Team"**tab**>**Search for User **>**Click on**"User Roles" >** Click **"Add to Sub-account" > Select which subaccount you want to add them to**.

**Tip:** To switch between an agency and sub-account Profile, you can use the "[login-as feature](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001223053)" available for agency admins.

### **Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Edited**

If your meeting date and time are the same, the Zoom meeting link generated prior continues to function as intended.

### **Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Deleted**

If your meeting is canceled or deleted, the Zoom meeting link will be dropped permanently unless there is another meeting for the same time slot using the same meeting link.

### **Handling Meeting Links when Meetings are Rescheduled to a different time**

If your meeting is rescheduled, a new meeting link will be generated unless there is another appointment in the same time slot, in which case, the link generated prior would be re-used.

### **Handling Multiple Zoom Meetings at the Same Time Slot**

If the Calendar Settings allow for multiple appointments per slot, then the same meeting link would be re-used across all the meetings.

```
Please note: Currently, a single user may only use up to 100 requests per day (UTC) to create, update, or delete meetings. This 24-hour period resets at 00:00 UTC, not the user or account’s local timezone.
```

### **Existing Zoom Events Not Reflecting in the Calendar**

Currently, Zoom Integration neither pulls in events from Zoom nor uses pre-generated meeting links on meetings created directly via Zoom.

### **Calendar Version Support**

Currently, the dynamic Zoom Integration only works with Group Calendars.

### **How do I integrate my Zoom account with an unassigned calendar**

Unassigned booking calendars can use static or pre-generated Zoom meeting links by manually adding the static link to the meeting location setting under Team and Event Setup.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000206668/original/-jTZ-dQlZq3LjkIa24xsFk24aelYjLVvYg.png?1685555020)

title_en: Bot Goals Overview - Conversation AI
source_md:
Bot Goals help define how your Conversation AI agent communicates, what it should accomplish, which actions it can take, and how you can test its responses before launch. The **Bot Goals** tab includes the agent’s prompt, available bot actions, and a real-time test panel so you can refine the customer experience in one place.

This article provides an overview of the main areas inside Bot Goals. For detailed setup steps for individual actions, use the related articles linked at the end.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Bot Goals in Conversation AI?](#What-are-Bot-Goals-in-Conversation-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Bot Goals](#Key-Benefits-of-Bot-Goals)
- [How To Access Bot Goals](#How-To-Access-Bot-Goals)
- [Prompt](#Prompt)
- [Model selector](#Model-selector)
- [Model accuracy](#Model-accuracy)
- [Accuracy and Relative Cost](#Accuracy-and-Relative-Cost)
- [Personality](#Personality)
- [Goal or Intent](#Goal-or-Intent)
- [Additional Information](#Additional-Information)
- [Add Custom Value](#Add-Custom-Value)
- [Setup your Actions](#Setup-your-Actions)
- [Appointment Booking Actions](#Appointment-Booking-Actions)
- [Trigger Workflow](#Trigger-Workflow)
- [Contact Info](#Contact-Info)
- [Human Handover, Stop Bot, Auto Followup, and Transfer Bot](#Human-Handover,-Stop-Bot,-Auto-Followup,-and-Transfer-Bot)
- [Test Your Bot](#Test-Your-Bot)
- [Test and Train Your Bot in Real Time](#Test-and-Train-Your-Bot-in-Real-Time)
- [When To Use Each Bot Goals Area](#When-To-Use-Each-Bot-Goals-Area)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Bot Goals in Conversation AI?**

Bot Goals define the agent’s personality, goal or intent, supporting instructions, and available actions. These settings help the agent stay aligned with your business needs, whether it is answering questions, collecting lead details, booking appointments, or handing off conversations.

The Bot Goals tab is designed to help you configure the agent’s response behavior and goal-based actions together. The prompt controls how the agent communicates, while actions control what the agent can do during or after a conversation.

---

## **Key Benefits of Bot Goals**

Bot Goals help your Conversation AI agent respond with purpose instead of only answering one message at a time. By configuring prompts, actions, and testing tools together, you can create a more consistent and outcome-focused conversation experience.

- **Clearer response behavior:** Define the agent’s personality, goal, and supporting instructions.

- **Goal-focused conversations:** Guide contacts toward outcomes such as getting answers, sharing details, or booking appointments.

- **Action-based automation:** Allow the agent to perform actions such as booking appointments, triggering workflows, or collecting contact information.

- **Real-time testing:** Test responses while configuring the agent so you can refine behavior before launch.

- **Better handoffs:** Use actions and testing feedback to improve when the agent should continue, pause, or hand the conversation to another process.

---

## **How To Access Bot Goals**

Bot Goals are configured inside each Conversation AI agent. Since each agent can have its own prompt, actions, and testing behavior, make sure you select the correct agent before making changes.

1. Go to **AI Agents**.
2. Select **Conversation AI**.
3. Open or select the agent you want to configure.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084693031/original/cUsWgoOnxuUhseVHHQNGjDH93avHtU6Kjw.png?1793583957)

---

## **Prompt**

The **Prompt** area defines the core behavior of the agent. It combines the agent’s personality, goal or intent, and additional information so the agent can respond in a way that matches your business needs and communication style.

The Prompt area may include:

- Model selector

- Word count or available word limit

- Personality

- Goal or Intent

- Additional Information

- Add Custom Value

- Prompt Guidelines

Depending on your account or UI version, the primary objective field may appear as **Goal** or **Intent**. Both refer to the main outcome the agent should work toward during the conversation.

---

## **Model selector**

Use the **Model** dropdown to select an available OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, or Google Gemini model for your Conversation AI agent. To access Claude and Gemini, enable **Conversations AI Provider Support** under **Settings → Labs**.

Each agent can use a different model. Switching models preserves existing prompts, actions, knowledge bases, channels, and agent settings. The model dropdown displays relative cost indicators from $ to $$$$.

**Existing OpenAI model options include:**

1. GPT-6 Sol
2. GPT-6 Luna
3. GPT-5.6 Sol
4. GPT-5.6 Luna
5. GPT-5.5
6. GPT-5.4
7. GPT-5.4 Mini
8. GPT-5.4 Nano
9. GPT-5.2
10. GPT-5.1

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081019482/original/50wfdZH_LY6gd-wllIUok5y7GjKXJbidxQ.png?1789505837)

**To change an agent's model:**

1. From your **Sub-Account** view, navigate to **AI Agents → Conversation AI → Agents List**.
2. Select the agent you want to edit and open the **Build** tab.
3. Select an OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini model from the **Model** dropdown.
4. **Optional:** Click the **settings (gear) icon** beside Model and select a **Secondary Model** different from the primary. The fallback can use the same provider or another provider.
5. Use **Test your agent** to verify responses and configured actions, then click **Save**.

You can also change the primary model using **Build with AI** by requesting a model switch in natural language.

For complete setup instructions and the supported Claude and Gemini models, see [How to Use Claude and Gemini Models in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009540-how-to-use-claude-and-gemini-models-in-conversation-ai).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081019523/original/MV6OKSHqhvnYcOswuEEmF13av6PWKCEmOw.png?1789505911)

---

## **Model accuracy**

**Note:** The accuracy comparisons below cover OpenAI models evaluated in earlier releases. They do not include Claude or Gemini models.

In an earlier OpenAI production evaluation, all eight GPT-5.x models matched or exceeded GPT-4.1 accuracy.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081019619/original/wUMB9IwofxEJMtofGBulASwNFb8DDmH03g.png?1789506088)

Accuracy comparison of GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.x models based on production conversations.

### **GPT-6.1 Sol Performance**

GPT-6.1 Sol offers accuracy comparable to GPT-6 Sol, with faster response times for the slowest replies and slightly lower cost per reply.

| Metric | GPT-6.1 Sol | GPT-6 Sol comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accuracy | 92.9% | 94.2% |
| Median reply time | 2.33 seconds | Comparable |
| Slowest replies | Approximately 11% faster | Relative to GPT-6 Sol |
| Cost per reply | Approximately 2% lower | Relative to GPT-6 Sol |

GPT-6.1 Sol provides another option for agents that need Sol-tier accuracy with improved response times and slightly lower costs.

---

## **Accuracy and Relative Cost**

The chart below compares response accuracy and relative cost for GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.x models from an earlier OpenAI evaluation. Claude and Gemini are not included in this comparison. For current relative model costs, refer to the Model dropdown.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081019643/original/u9rWWjCh-aYRfB6ZLUTPdBN5K0Ng8j9E_Q.png?1789506149)**

Accuracy and relative cost per reply for GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.x models.

---

## **Personality**

Personality determines who the agent is and how it should sound during conversations. This helps the agent match your brand’s communication style and create a consistent experience for contacts.

Use Personality to define tone and role, such as:

- Friendly and approachable

- Professional and concise

- Formal and structured

- Enthusiastic and energetic

- Warm and knowledgeable

Example:

You are a friendly restaurant booking assistant. Keep responses warm, helpful, and concise.

---

## **Goal or Intent**

Goal or Intent defines the agent’s primary objective. This tells the agent what it should focus on accomplishing during the conversation.

Use Goal or Intent for outcomes such as:

- Answering customer questions

- Generating leads

- Booking appointments

- Collecting required information

- Sharing a resource after qualification

- Guiding customers to the right next step

Example:

Your goal is to guide customers toward booking a reservation at the restaurant.

---

## **Additional Information**

Additional Information gives the agent supporting rules, context, boundaries, and conversation guidelines. This field is useful for explaining how the agent should handle specific situations while working toward its goal.

Use Additional Information for instructions such as:

- Ask one question at a time.

- Maintain a casual, purposeful, and concise tone.

- Mirror the customer’s language and manner of speaking.

- Avoid using emojis.

- Do not guess when the answer is unavailable.

- Let the contact know a team member can help when human review is needed.

Example:

Ask one question at a time. If the answer is not available in training content, do not guess. Let the contact know a team member can help.

---

## **Add Custom Value**

Add Custom Value lets you insert dynamic account, contact, or business information into the prompt. This helps personalize the agent’s instructions without manually typing the same information each time.

Custom values may be useful when you want the prompt to reference available information such as the business name, contact details, assigned user, or other supported values in the account.

Example:

You are a bot for {{ai.business\_name}}, tasked to assist customers.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081020340/original/3bYtQ-oNgQ6zOiADzdaN4Jpq_GskJL7riQ.png?1789507891)

---

## **Setup your Actions**

The **Setup your Actions** area contains the actions the agent can perform during or after a conversation. These actions help move the conversation from response handling into practical next steps, such as booking, automation, contact updates, or handoff.

Available actions may vary by account, configuration, or release status. Common actions may include:

- Appointment Booking

- Trigger a Workflow

- Contact Info

- Human Handover

- Stop Bot

- Auto Followup

- Transfer Bot

Use the action-specific articles for full setup details. This overview explains what each action is generally used for.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081020348/original/3piRKI7rtcpjqbfegYdtRoU9UjfwRNbKbg.png?1789507940)

---

## **Appointment Booking Actions**

Appointment Booking actions help the agent support scheduling during a conversation. These settings define how the agent should use calendars, booking links, post-booking workflows, and handoff behavior after an appointment is booked.

Appointment Booking may include options such as:

- **Pick a calendar:** Select the calendar the agent should reference for available slots and booking.

- **Send booking link only:** Send the calendar booking link instead of booking directly in the conversation.

- **Pause bot responses after booking:** Stop further bot responses once an appointment is successfully booked.

- **Trigger workflow after booking:** Start a selected workflow after a successful booking.

- **Transfer employee or bot after booking:** Transfer the conversation after the appointment is booked, depending on available configuration options.

**HighLevel Pro Tip:** Avoid including detailed calendar slot information directly in the prompt. Calendar availability should come from the booking configuration, not static prompt text. Adding specific slot details to prompts can cause inaccurate responses if availability changes.

Related article: [Appointment Booking in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000210-appointment-booking-in-conversation-ai)

---

## **Trigger Workflow**

Trigger Workflow allows the agent to start a workflow based on the conversation. This is useful when a conversation should lead to a follow-up process, internal notification, lead routing, tagging, pipeline update, or another automated action.

Before connecting a workflow to the agent, create and configure the workflow you want the bot to trigger. The agent can only trigger workflows that are available and properly set up in the account.

Common use cases include:

- Send an internal notification after a qualified lead responds.

- Start a follow-up sequence after the bot collects required information.

- Add a tag or update a contact after a specific conversation outcome.

- Move a contact into a pipeline stage after the agent identifies interest.

Related article: [Trigger a Workflow within Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004098-trigger-a-workflow-within-conversation-ai)

---

## **Contact Info**

Contact Info allows the agent to collect missing contact details and save them to selected contact fields. This is useful when the agent needs to gather information such as a business name, date of birth, service preference, budget range, or other custom details.

Contact Info is best used when the selected contact field is empty. It is not intended to overwrite existing contact field values.

Common use cases include:

- Collect a missing business name.

- Ask for a preferred service.

- Save a customer type or service area.

- Capture a custom field needed for follow-up.

Related article: [Add Contact Info Bot Action in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004097-bot-actions-add-contact-info)

---

## **Human Handover, Stop Bot, Auto Followup, and Transfer Bot**

Some accounts may include additional actions that control how the agent hands off, pauses, continues, or transfers a conversation. These actions help manage the conversation after the agent identifies that another process or responder should take over.

Examples of additional actions may include:

- **Human Handover:** Route or hand off the conversation when human review is needed.

- **Stop Bot:** Stop the bot from continuing the conversation in specific scenarios.

- **Auto Followup:** Continue follow-up based on configured behavior.

- **Transfer Bot:** Move the conversation to another bot or specialized agent.

Use these actions when the conversation should no longer be handled in the same way by the current agent. Availability and behavior may vary based on account configuration.

---

## **Test Your Bot**

The **Test Your Bot** panel lets you test the agent while configuring Bot Goals. This helps confirm that the prompt, actions, and response behavior work as expected before the agent is used in live conversations.

Testing is especially useful after changing Personality, Goal/Intent, Additional Information, or action settings. Use realistic customer messages to confirm the agent responds naturally and follows the intended rules.

---

## **Test and Train Your Bot in Real Time**

Real-time testing helps you refine the agent while reviewing its responses. The test panel lets you simulate customer conversations, provide feedback, reset the conversation, and adjust the prompt as needed.

Use the test panel to:

- **Chat with the bot:** Send sample messages to see how the agent responds.

- **Give feedback on answers:** Use positive or negative feedback to help improve response behavior and identify missing training content.

- **Edit prompt behavior:** Update Personality, Goal/Intent, or Additional Information when responses do not match expectations.

- **Reset the conversation:** Clear the test conversation after making changes so you can test again from a fresh conversation.

Testing should be repeated after major prompt or action changes.

---

## **When To Use Each Bot Goals Area**

Each area inside Bot Goals supports a different part of the agent experience. Use the table below to decide which setting to update.

| **Bot Goals Area** | **Use It For** | **Example** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Prompt** | Define response behavior, personality, goal, and instructions | Tell the agent to sound professional and ask one question at a time. |
| **Appointment Booking** | Help contacts schedule appointments | Book a consultation or send a booking link. |
| **Trigger Workflow** | Start automation after a conversation outcome | Notify sales after a qualified lead responds. |
| **Contact Info** | Collect and save missing contact details | Ask for a business name or preferred service. |
| **Human Handover / Stop Bot / Transfer Bot** | Control handoff, stopping, or routing behavior | Hand off billing complaints to a human. |
| **Test Your Bot** | Validate behavior before launch | Test whether the agent follows the prompt and actions. |

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What do Bot Goals control?**  
Bot Goals control the agent’s prompt, personality, goal or intent, supporting instructions, available actions, and testing experience.

**Q: What is the difference between Prompt and Setup your Actions?**  
The Prompt controls how the agent communicates and what it should focus on. Setup your Actions controls what the agent can do, such as booking appointments, triggering workflows, or collecting contact information.

**Q: Why do I see Goal in one account and Intent in another?**  
Depending on your account or UI version, the primary objective field may appear as Goal or Intent. Both define the main outcome the agent should work toward.

**Q: Should I add calendar availability to the prompt?**  
No. Calendar availability should come from appointment booking settings. Adding specific slots to the prompt may cause inaccurate responses if availability changes.

**Q: Can Bot Goals update contact fields?**  
Yes, when the Contact Info action is configured. This is typically used to collect and save missing contact information.

**Q: Can Bot Goals trigger workflows?**  
Yes. Use Trigger Workflow when the conversation should start an automation after a specific outcome or condition.

**Q: Should I test the bot after changing Bot Goals?**  
Yes. Always test after changing prompts or actions to confirm the agent responds correctly and follows the intended behavior.

**Q: Why is the bot not following my prompt?**  
The prompt may be vague, conflicting, or missing important context. Make the instruction more specific, remove conflicts, and test again.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Customize Conversation AI Agent Responses with Prompts and Instructions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002255-customize-conversation-ai-agent-responses-with-prompts-and-instructions)

- [Appointment Booking in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000210-appointment-booking-in-conversation-ai)

- [Add Contact Info Bot Action in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004097-bot-actions-add-contact-info)

- [Trigger a Workflow within Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004098-trigger-a-workflow-within-conversation-ai)

- [Training Your Conversation AI Bot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008470-training-your-conversation-ai-bot)

- [AI Action Logging & Filtering in Conversations](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005004-ai-action-logging-filtering-in-conversations)

title_en: How to Import n8n Workflows into Managed Agents
source_md:
Bring your existing n8n automations into HighLevel without manually rebuilding every workflow step. The **Import from n8n** feature analyzes an n8n workflow export and prepares a Managed Agent using its triggers, logic, and actions. You can review what carried over, what changed, and what still needs configuration before creating the agent. This guide covers importing your workflow, reviewing the conversion, completing setup, and saving or publishing your Managed Agent.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is n8n Workflow Import for Managed Agents?](#What-is-n8n-Workflow-Import-for-Managed-Agents?)
- [Key Benefits of n8n Workflow Import](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000009248/edit?portalId=48000045315#Key-Benefits-of-n8n-Workflow-Import)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000009248/edit?portalId=48000045315#Prerequisites-and-Limitations)
- [How To Setup n8n Workflow Import in Managed Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000009248/edit?portalId=48000045315#How-To-Setup-n8n-Workflow-Import-in-Managed-Agents)
  - [How n8n Workflow Steps Are Converted](#How-n8n-Workflow-Steps-Are-Converted)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

# 

# **What is n8n Workflow Import for Managed Agents?**

n8n Workflow Import lets you convert an existing n8n automation into a HighLevel Managed Agent using its exported JSON file. Instead of recreating each node, the importer analyzes the workflow and prepares an agent with instructions, starting conditions, decision rules, and connected actions.

The importer identifies how individual workflow steps can operate within HighLevel. For example, conditional branches become agent decision rules, AI nodes become part of the agent's reasoning, and supported app actions use HighLevel integrations, CRM actions, or API calls.

Before creating the agent, you can review which steps carried over, which were adapted, and which items need additional attention.

The **Review & set up** screen also identifies required app connections, configuration values, and starting conditions. Once you complete the review, you can save the agent as a draft or create and publish it.

Imported agents are organized in the **Imported from n8n** folder in Agent Studio.

---

## **Key Benefits of n8n Workflow Import**

Importing an existing automation gives you a starting point based on a workflow you have already built. The review process helps you understand how that automation translates into a Managed Agent before you use it in HighLevel.

- **Less manual rebuilding:** Convert an exported n8n workflow into a Managed Agent without recreating every node and connection individually.

- **Transparent workflow conversion:** Review the steps that carried over, were adapted, or require additional attention. Adapted steps include explanations of how their behavior changed.
- **Guided configuration:** Review triggers, connect required apps, and provide missing values directly within the import experience.

- **Natural-language decision rules:** Conditional logic and supported AI operations become agent instructions and reasoning rather than remaining separate workflow nodes.

- **HighLevel integration:** Imported agents can use supported HighLevel CRM actions, Conversations, forms, calendars, Knowledge Bases, and app connections.

- **Controlled agent creation:** Review the proposed agent before saving a draft or publishing it. Analyzing the workflow alone does not create an agent.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Before importing a workflow, prepare its JSON export and review the connections it depends on. Some workflow behavior may require adaptation or manual configuration to work within HighLevel.

**Prerequisites**

- **An existing n8n workflow:** Have an n8n workflow available for export.

- **Workflow JSON:** Export the workflow as a `.json` file or have its JSON content ready to paste.

- **File size:** The importer accepts JSON file uploads up to **10 MB**.

- **Managed Agents access:** Open the Managed Agents area in Agent Studio and look for **Import from → n8n (Beta)**.

- **Required integrations:** Be prepared to connect external apps that the imported workflow needs.

- **Configuration details:** Have any required IDs, values, or account-specific information available to finish setup.

**Limitations and important considerations**

- **Beta feature:** The n8n import option is labeled Beta in the supplied interface. [NEEDS CONFIRMATION: Verify current Beta availability, rollout eligibility, and any importer-specific permissions.]

- **Credentials are not transferred:** The importer does not import n8n credentials or API keys. Required apps must be connected through HighLevel.

- **Some steps are adapted:** The importer may convert fixed workflow logic into agent instructions or use a different HighLevel action. Results can vary when behavior depends on the agent's reasoning.

- **Manual review may be required:** The importer highlights items such as inferred decision rules and setup details that need confirmation before publishing.

- **Existing resource IDs need verification:** IDs from the original workflow, such as sheet, channel, or list IDs, are flagged for review instead of being silently trusted.

- **Analysis does not create an agent:** An agent is created only after you select **Save as draft** or **Create & publish**.

---

## **How To Setup n8n Workflow Import in Managed Agents**

The import process takes you from an n8n JSON export to a configured Managed Agent. You can review the generated instructions, verify conversions, and complete required connections before deciding whether to save a draft or publish.

### 

### **Step 1: Open the n8n Importer**

Start in the HighLevel sub-account where you want to create the Managed Agent. The importer is available from the Managed Agents tab in Agent Studio.

- Log in to HighLevel and open the appropriate **Sub-Account**.
- Select **AI Agents** from the navigation menu.
- Select **Agent Studio**.
- Select the **Managed Agents** tab.
- Click **Import from** in the upper-right area of the Agents page.
- Select **n8n (Beta)** from the dropdown menu.

  The **Import from n8n** window opens.

### 

### **Step 2: Upload or Paste the n8n Workflow JSON**

The importer accepts an exported n8n workflow as a JSON file or pasted JSON content. This allows you to start from the workflow definition without manually recreating its nodes.

- In the **Import from n8n** window, locate the upload area labeled **Drop your n8n workflow export**.
- Add your workflow using either option:

  - Drag and drop the exported `.json` file into the upload area, or click the area to browse for the file.
  - Select **Paste JSON instead** to provide the workflow JSON directly.
- If uploading a file, make sure it is a JSON export no larger than **10 MB**.
- After providing the workflow JSON, click **Analyze workflow**.

The importer begins analyzing the workflow. No agent is created at this stage.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083809041/original/PmC9cv-2H2PsaCt_nQuCS9dQM4GORl1DtA.png?1792543227)

### **Step 3: Analyze the Workflow**

HighLevel analyzes the exported workflow to identify its steps, required resources, and potential Managed Agent configuration. The progress screen shows how the importer processes the original automation.

The analysis follows these stages:

- **Reading the workflow:** Reads the uploaded n8n workflow definition.
- **Mapping each step:** Identifies the workflow steps that need conversion.
- **Checking this account's forms, calendars and knowledge bases:** Reviews relevant HighLevel resources available in the sub-account.
- **Planning the agent:** Determines how the workflow can be represented as a Managed Agent.
- **Writing the agent:** Creates the proposed agent instructions and behavior from the analyzed workflow.
- **Checking it against your workflow:** Compares the generated agent plan with the original workflow.

The analysis screen also displays the number of workflow steps identified.

After analysis finishes, the importer presents the generated agent for review.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083809059/original/qeQpGgYEOgFOmwGRbEbl0uPVS4LF4JaaSw.png?1792543284)

### 

### **Step 4: Review the Generated Agent and Conversion Results**

Reviewing the generated agent helps you identify differences between the original n8n workflow and its proposed HighLevel implementation.

**Review the generated agent**

- In **Review & set up**, locate the generated agent summary.
- Review the agent's name and description to confirm that they match the workflow's intended purpose.
- Review the displayed starting condition, app connections, and capabilities.
- You can expand **Agent instructions** to inspect the generated instructions. The instructions describe what starts the agent, its actions, decision rules, follow-ups, and stopping conditions.

**Review how the workflow was converted**

- Scroll to **How your workflow came across**.
- Review the conversion summary showing how many steps were carried over or adapted.
- Inspect the conversion results:

  - **Carried over:** Steps the importer retained in the converted agent.
  - **Adapted:** Steps implemented differently within the Managed Agent.
  - **Not possible / Not needed:** Review any steps the importer identifies as unsupported or unnecessary.
- Review the reasons shown for adapted steps.

  Adaptations may include changes to how a workflow starts, when a step runs, or whether an action is completed through an app, the CRM, or an API call.
- Review any warnings or items identified for human verification.

  Some original workflow rules may become agent instructions instead of fixed code. These rules may produce slightly different results and should be checked against the intended behavior.

### 

### **Step 5: Complete the Required Agent Setup**

The **Review & set up** screen groups the configuration items needed before the imported agent can run as intended. The required items depend on the workflow's triggers, integrations, and data references.

**Configure how the agent starts**

- Locate **Finish setup** in the import window.
- Under **How it starts**, review the generated starting condition.
- If an **Edit** button appears, select it to review or adjust the starting condition as needed.

  For example, an n8n workflow that runs periodically may be converted to a **Schedule** trigger.
- Confirm that the trigger matches the original automation's intended timing or starting event.

**Connect required apps**

- Locate **Apps to connect**.
- Review each listed app and its connection status.
- Select **Connect** when an app is marked **Not connected**.
- If an app is already connected, use **Manage** when available to review its connection.

  The supplied example shows a HubSpot MCP connection. Until that app is connected, steps requiring it are skipped and reported.

**Set required values**

- Locate **Values to set**.
- Review any fields marked **Needs input**.
- Enter the required value in the corresponding input field.
- Click **Save** to store the value.

For example, an imported workflow may require a sales representative owner ID to complete its configuration.

- Review any original resource IDs flagged by the importer. Confirm whether to keep the existing reference or replace it with an appropriate link or ID.

**Review additional requirements**

- Complete any Knowledge Base configuration requested by the importer.

- Review any remaining warnings or setup requirements before publishing.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083809149/original/2VuFGuAndR7CPoc3p3MjhdLl0P5JHaZn9w.png?1792543736)

### **Step 6: Save as Draft or Create and Publish**

After reviewing the converted workflow and its configuration, choose whether to save the imported agent for later setup or publish it.

- Return to the bottom of the **Review & set up** window.
- Review any remaining configuration requirements.
- Choose one of the available actions:

  - **Save as draft:** Create the Managed Agent as a draft so you can complete or refine its setup later.
  - **Create & publish:** Create and publish the Managed Agent after the required setup items are completed.
- If required configuration items are incomplete, **Create & publish** may remain unavailable until those items are resolved.
- After selecting **Save as draft**, review the **Done** screen.

  The supplied draft completion screen displays **Draft agent created**, the agent's name, its Draft status, and any remaining required items.
- Select **Open agent** to continue configuring the new agent, or select **Done** to finish the import flow.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083809169/original/cTDcBQQmQCKRTX_lVp2PI1NgemLPsRnmWA.png?1792543797)

### **Step 7: Locate the Imported Agent and Finish Setup**

Imported agents are organized in a dedicated folder in Agent Studio. If you save an agent as a draft, you can open it and complete the remaining configuration using the AI builder.

- From the **Sub-Account** view, select **AI Agents → Agent Studio → Managed Agents**.
- Locate the **Imported from n8n** folder.
- Open the folder and select the imported Managed Agent.

  Alternatively, select **Open agent** directly from the import completion screen.
- If the agent has outstanding configuration items, review the **Finish setup** notice.
- Use the available links or **Replace** option to address the remaining requirements.
- You can also ask the AI builder:

  **"What's left to set up?"**

  The builder can identify outstanding configuration items and present them as a checklist.
- After completing the outstanding tasks, you can dismiss the **Finish setup** notice.

```
For agents using an inbound webhook  

An imported workflow that begins with an external webhook requires the sending system to use the Managed Agent's webhook URL.
Copy the provided URL and register it in the external system that sends the events.
```

---

## **How n8n Workflow Steps Are Converted**

The importer translates n8n components into Managed Agent behavior rather than recreating the original node graph. Understanding these conversions helps you verify that the agent's starting conditions, decisions, and actions match your automation's intended purpose.

### **Triggers and Starting Conditions**

The importer evaluates what starts the original workflow and maps it to a supported Managed Agent trigger.

| n8n Workflow Component | Managed Agent Conversion |
| --- | --- |
| Webhook node | Inbound webhook trigger with its own URL |
| Periodic checks | Scheduled trigger |
| Form-based events | HighLevel forms |
| Booking events | HighLevel calendars |
| Message-based events | HighLevel Conversations |

External services such as Stripe, Shopify, HubSpot, and Pipedrive can send supported events to an inbound webhook.

For webhook-based imports, the agent receives instructions about where to register the URL and which events the sending system should deliver.

### 

### **Decision Logic, Wait Steps, and AI Nodes**

The importer converts workflow logic into agent instructions and follow-up behavior. This reduces the need to maintain the original visual node structure within the Managed Agent.

| n8n Workflow Component | Managed Agent Conversion |
| --- | --- |
| IF nodes | Decision rules in the agent's instructions |
| Switch nodes | Decision rules that describe how the agent selects a path |
| Wait nodes | Follow-ups at defined points |
| OpenAI nodes | Agent reasoning |
| LLM chains | Agent reasoning and instructions |
| AI Agent nodes | Agent reasoning and instructions |

AI components become part of the Managed Agent's own reasoning rather than requiring the original model-node structure.

When fixed logic is adapted into instructions, behavior may differ slightly from the original node-based execution.

Review the importer's adaptation notes and manually verify any rules identified for additional checking.

### 

### **App Connections, CRM Actions, APIs, and Knowledge Bases**

The importer evaluates external application actions and data lookups to identify how the Managed Agent can perform those tasks through HighLevel.

| n8n Workflow Component | Managed Agent Conversion |
| --- | --- |
| Supported app nodes | Marketplace app connections |
| CRM-related actions | HighLevel CRM actions |
| External API operations | API calls |
| Knowledge lookups | HighLevel Knowledge Bases |

Some actions may be implemented differently from their original n8n nodes.

The importer identifies these adaptations and explains when an operation will run through an app, the CRM, or an API call.

Required integrations and account-specific values still need to be configured before the affected operations can work as intended.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is importing an n8n workflow the same as connecting n8n through GHL MCP?**

No. The n8n importer converts an exported workflow into a HighLevel Managed Agent.

The existing GHL MCP integration connects HighLevel with workflows that continue to run in n8n. These are different integration approaches.

**Q: What happens if an imported workflow requires an app that is not connected?**

The importer identifies required app connections during **Review & set up**.

In the supplied HubSpot MCP example, steps that require the connection are skipped and reported until the app is connected.

Review the connection requirements before publishing your agent.

**Q: What happens to sheet IDs, channel IDs, or other references from the original workflow?**

The importer flags these references for review rather than automatically trusting them.

You can confirm whether the existing reference is appropriate or replace it with another link or ID.

This helps you avoid carrying account-specific references into the wrong configuration.

**Q: Why might an imported agent behave differently from the original n8n workflow?**

Some n8n steps use fixed code or explicit branching rules. The importer may adapt these operations into agent instructions and decision rules.

The review screen identifies these adaptations and may highlight inferred logic that needs manual verification.

Check those rules carefully to make sure the generated agent follows the intended business process.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Setup and Use Managed Agents in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007931-how-to-setup-and-use-super-agents-in-agent-studio)

- [Automate Workflows with GHL MCP and N8N](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007777-automate-workflows-with-ghl-mcp-and-n8n)

- [How to Create and Manage Folders in Agent Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007417-how-to-create-and-manage-folders-in-agent-studio)

- [Scheduled Triggers for Managed Agents in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008245-scheduled-triggers-for-managed-agents-in-highlevel)

title_en: Create Google Demand Gen campaigns in Ad Manager
source_md:
**Google Demand Gen campaigns in HighLevel Ad Manager** help you reach potential customers with visually rich ads across Google surfaces like YouTube, Discover, Gmail, and partner inventory. This campaign type is useful when you want to build awareness, drive clicks, or optimize for conversions before someone performs a direct search.

HighLevel brings campaign creation, audience targeting, and ad setup into one workflow so you can launch faster and manage more from one place. It is especially helpful for advertisers who want a simpler way to create Google campaigns without switching between multiple tools.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Google Demand Gen in HighLevel Ad Manager?](#What-is-Google-Demand-Gen-in-HighLevel-Ad-Manager?)
- [Key Benefits of Google Demand Gen Campaigns](#Key-Benefits-of-Google-Demand-Gen-Campaigns)
- [Campaign Goals](#Campaign-Goals)
- [Audience Targeting](#Audience-Targeting)
- [Ad Formats and Creative Requirements](#Ad-Formats-and-Creative-Requirements)
- [How To Setup Google Demand Gen Campaigns](#How-To-Setup-Google-Demand-Gen-Campaigns)
  - [Conversions](#Conversions)
  - [Clicks](#Clicks)
  - [YouTube Engagements](#YouTube-Engagements)
  - [Single Image Ads](#Single-Image-Ads)
  - [Single Video Ads](#Single-Video-Ads)
  - [Carousel Ads](#Carousel-Ads)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is Google Demand Gen in HighLevel Ad Manager?**

Google Demand Gen campaigns help you connect with people earlier in the buying journey using visual ad placements across Google-owned and partner surfaces. In HighLevel Ad Manager, you can create these campaigns, choose a goal, define targeting, add creative assets, and publish from a guided workflow inside the platform. This makes it easier to manage setup while still using Google Ads delivery and optimization behavior behind the scenes.

Choose where your ads can appear:

- **All Google channels** – Allows Google to automatically select eligible channels and inventory.
- **Manual channel selection**, including:  
    
  - YouTube
    - In-stream
    - In-feed
    - Shorts
  - Google Discover
  - Gmail
  - Google Maps
  - Google Display Network

**Google Demand Gen campaigns in HighLevel Ad Manager** help you reach potential customers with visually rich ads across Google surfaces such as YouTube, Discover, Gmail, Maps, and the Google Display Network.

---

## **Key Benefits of Google Demand Gen Campaigns**
