Google Demand Gen campaigns are valuable when you want a campaign type that combines broad reach, strong visual formats, and easier campaign setup inside HighLevel. They can help you attract attention before someone actively searches for your offer, while still giving you control over targeting, budget, and creative setup.

- **Visual reach:** Run image- and video-led campaigns across YouTube, Discover, Gmail, and other Google partner surfaces to capture attention earlier in the customer journey.

- **Flexible optimization:** Choose from Conversions, Clicks, or YouTube Engagements based on whether your goal is action, traffic, or video interaction.

- **Centralized setup:** Build the campaign inside HighLevel Ad Manager instead of managing each part in separate tools.

- **Audience control:** Use Google audience segment options such as Customer Match, Website Visitors, Interest Segments, and Lookalike Segments to reach more relevant people.

- **Creative flexibility:** Depending on the selected goal, you can use supported formats such as single image ads, single video ads, or carousel ads.

- **Stronger campaign preparation:** HighLevel also supports related Google Ads workflows like conversion action setup and campaign-level assets, which can improve readiness before launch.

---

## **Campaign Goals**

Your campaign goal determines how Google will optimize delivery, so choosing the right objective is one of the most important setup decisions. Picking a goal that matches your business outcome helps the platform focus on the actions that matter most, whether that is traffic, conversions, or engagement.  

HighLevel’s Google Demand Gen flow supports these campaign goals:

- **Conversions:** Best when you want Google to optimize toward conversion actions such as leads or other tracked outcomes. This option requires conversion readiness, so make sure the relevant Google Ads conversion actions are already available before launch. HighLevel also supports creating and managing Google Ads offline conversion actions inside Ad Manager.

- **Clicks:** Best when your goal is driving traffic to a page, offer, or funnel. This is useful when you want to prioritize visits rather than optimize toward a specific conversion event.

- **YouTube Engagements:** Best when you want to focus on video interaction. This option is tied to video-based creative, so users should plan for video assets before selecting it.

---

## **Audience Targeting**

Audience targeting shapes who sees your ads, which directly affects campaign relevance and performance. Strong targeting helps you balance reach with intent so your budget is spent on people who are more likely to care about your offer.

When setting up a Demand Gen campaign in HighLevel Ad Manager, you can work with Google audience segment types that help refine who you reach. HighLevel’s Google Ads audience segment support includes:

- **Customer Match:** Use first-party customer data to reach people based on existing customer lists. This is useful for remarketing, re-engagement, or audience expansion strategies.

- **Website Visitors:** Target people who have visited your website. This is often useful for retargeting warm traffic that already knows your brand.

- **Interest Segments:** Reach users based on interests and buying signals. HighLevel references Affinity and In-Market audience concepts to support broader or more intent-focused targeting.

- **Lookalike Segments:** Use an existing seed audience to help Google identify additional users who may be relevant to your campaign. Google is transitioning Lookalike segments in Demand Gen toward an audience-suggestion model, where the seed audience can act as a signal and Google may reach qualified users beyond the original similarity thresholds.

For broader planning, location targeting, language targeting, and placements are also part of the ad group setup flow in the Demand Gen campaign article. HighLevel also notes that Google placement behavior follows Google Demand Gen rules, so users should expect Google’s platform behavior to influence how eligible placements are used.

---

## **Ad Formats and Creative Requirements**

Creative setup is central to Demand Gen performance because this campaign type depends on visual assets to attract attention across Google surfaces. Preparing the right ad format and assets in advance helps prevent setup errors and makes it easier to match your creative to your chosen campaign goal.

HighLevel’s Demand Gen article references these supported ad formats:

- **Single Image Ads**

- ****Single Video Ads****

- ****Carousel Ads****

Keep these points in mind while preparing creative:

- **Goal and format should match:** YouTube Engagements is tied to video-focused delivery, so video assets should be ready before choosing that goal.

- **Assets should be prepared early:** The Demand Gen article recommends having creative assets ready before you begin.

- **Campaign-level assets may also support your campaign setup:** HighLevel supports Business Logos, Image Assets, Call Extensions, and Sitelinks at the campaign level for Google Ads. These assets are designed to improve visibility and keep assets consistent across ads in a campaign.

- **Creative consistency matters:** Using the correct logos, images, and destination details helps reduce friction during review and gives your ads a more complete appearance. This is especially helpful when your ads may appear across multiple Google surfaces

---

## **How To Setup Google Demand Gen Campaigns**

A structured setup process reduces mistakes and makes it easier to publish a campaign that is actually ready to perform. Before building the ad itself, it is important to confirm account access, Google connection, audience readiness, and any conversion tracking requirements tied to your chosen goal.

**Confirm Ad Manager access in HighLevel.**

Make sure Ad Manager is enabled for the sub-account and visible to the correct user based on agency setup and permissions. Agencies can enable and resell Ad Manager for sub-accounts, and team permissions control who can access it.

**Connect your Google account and Google Ads account.**

Before publishing Google campaigns, connect Google with Ad Manager. HighLevel’s onboarding flow for Google is required before campaign creation can move forward successfully.

**Prepare any required conversion actions.**

If you plan to use **Conversions** as the campaign goal, make sure the needed conversion actions are available. HighLevel supports creating and managing Google Ads offline conversion actions inside Ad Manager, which is helpful for tracking outcomes like qualified leads, booked appointments, or closed deals.

**Open Ad Manager and create a new campaign.**

From the Ad Manager home screen, click **Create Campaign** and choose **Google** as the platform. Then continue through the campaign creation flow.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069613414/original/0vPUd0WXs2fKyXHwLccKeW1KQ0pVwOKA3g.jpeg?1776777029)**

Select Google as the advertising platform. Choose Demand Gen Ads as the campaign objective

**Demand Gen campaigns are ideal when you want to:**

- Reach new audiences before they search
- Run visual or video-first campaigns
- Support awareness and consideration goals
- Build full-funnel Google advertising strategies from a single platform

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614222/original/5fa1nDi2kt5usZNiA8AMe8M722bDtkkRYg.jpeg?1776777380)**

**Choose your campaign goal.**

Select **Conversions**, **Clicks**, or **YouTube Engagements** based on the outcome you want. Use a goal that matches the main action you want Google to optimize toward.

### **Conversions**

- Select an existing conversion goal from your connected Google Ads account
- Optionally enable Target CPA to optimize toward a specific cost per conversion

### 

### **Clicks**

- Optimizes the campaign for traffic
- Optionally enable Target CPC
- No conversion goal is required

### 

### **YouTube Engagements**

- Optimizes the campaign for eligible YouTube engagement actions, such as channel subscriptions or follow-on views
- Serves only on YouTube inventory
- Requires video creative
- Supports conversion-focused bidding, including Target CPA when applicable
- The Google Ads account and relevant YouTube channel must be properly linked for YouTube engagement conversion actions

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069613484/original/N9QOzc7-ilvSDjcKd4HHW_mwdy7LH7nt8w.jpeg?1776777063)**

****Set budget and schedule.****

Enter the campaign budget and define the schedule so the campaign has clear delivery rules from the start. This step controls how your campaign spends and when it becomes active.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069613530/original/XqgaWI-tCSA6fagd4PlK4ju4e3RKX9XGOg.jpeg?1776777082)**

****Configure ad group settings.****

Set up the ad group details, including targeting options such as location targeting, language targeting, and placements. These settings help narrow the campaign to the markets and audiences you want to reach.

**Choose where your ads can appear:**

- All Google channels (automatic placement)
- Manual placement selection, including:

  - YouTube (In-stream, In-feed, Shorts)
  - Google Discover
  - Gmail
  - Google Display Network

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069613763/original/jXDv5pud4hhGN9T-p6fB3n96V73-aCVMKQ.jpeg?1776777153)**

****Define the audience.****

Choose the audience segment strategy that best fits the campaign, such as Customer Match, Website Visitors, Interest Segments, or Lookalike Segments. Use warmer audiences for re-engagement and broader interest or lookalike audiences for prospecting.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614571/original/rjmaNHssYytZfv9RJ7JqTVHHZZE8d7t9AA.jpeg?1776777545)**

****Create the ad using supported creative formats.****

Add the creative assets required for your chosen format, such as a single image, single video, or carousel. If you are using YouTube Engagements, make sure the ad uses video assets.

### **Single Image Ads**

- Upload up to 20 images
- Upload up to 5 business logos (required)
- Add up to 5 headlines and 5 descriptions
- Choose a CTA and business name

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614513/original/3vgoFnLpDGy7vy3IRIuo2_G7g5F3EGt6yQ.jpeg?1776777527)**

### **Single Video Ads**

- Add up to 5 YouTube video URLs
- Videos must be at least 10 seconds long
- Recommended to include multiple aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1)
- Upload business logos
- Add headlines, long headlines, descriptions, CTA, and business name
- Sitelinks are supported (shared at the campaign level)

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614515/original/oNV0vNikWaZwT2thoZaNFcCsioQX4qjHqQ.jpeg?1776777528)**

### **Carousel Ads**

- Add a minimum of **2 cards and up to 10 cards**
- Each card includes:  
    
  - One image
  - Headline
  - Final URL
- Keep the image aspect ratio consistent across all cards
- Use consistent branding across the carousel

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614509/original/btwC1TLBCcFSQ6MVptgIxR0usN58U72XvQ.jpeg?1776777527)**

****Review and publish the campaign.****

Check the summary carefully to confirm the goal, audience, budget, schedule, and creative are correct. Once everything is complete, publish the campaign from Ad Manager.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069614400/original/FAeX8mTmxM3c7_mU2v3m9Ts0Z1_ETf9oUA.jpeg?1776777488)****

**Important Notes**

- Google account connection is required before you can publish Google campaigns from HighLevel Ad Manager.

- Conversion-based optimization depends on having the correct conversion actions available.

- Creative choice should align with the selected campaign goal, especially when using YouTube Engagements.

- HighLevel also supports Google campaign-level assets such as logos, image assets, call extensions, and site links, which may improve campaign completeness depending on your setup.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: When should I choose Conversions instead of Clicks?**

Choose Conversions when you want Google to optimize for a tracked business outcome, such as a qualified lead or booked appointment. Choose Clicks when your main goal is traffic to a landing page, website, or offer.

**Q: Do I need to connect Google before creating a Demand Gen campaign?**Yes. HighLevel’s Google onboarding and account connection flow is a required step before publishing Google campaigns through Ad Manager.

**Q: What should I do if no conversion goal appears during setup?**Check whether the required Google Ads conversion actions are already configured and available. HighLevel supports creating and managing Google Ads offline conversion actions inside Ad Manager, which can help when conversion tracking is not ready yet.

**Q: Can I use audience segments without leaving HighLevel?**

Yes. HighLevel supports Google Audience Segments directly inside Ad Manager, including Customer Match, Website Visitors, Interest Segments, and Lookalike Segments.

Google is transitioning Lookalike Segments in Demand Gen toward an audience-suggestion model during 2026. Depending on your Google Ads account and rollout status, Lookalike audiences may act as signals that help Google identify relevant users beyond the original similarity thresholds.

**Q: Which ad format should I prepare before starting?**Prepare the format that matches your goal and campaign strategy. HighLevel’s Demand Gen flow supports single image ads, single video ads, and carousel ads, and YouTube Engagements is tied to video-focused creative.

**Q: Are additional campaign assets available for Google campaigns in HighLevel?**Yes. HighLevel supports Business Logos, Image Assets, Call Extensions, and Sitelinks at the campaign level for Google Ads.

**Q: Where can Google Demand Gen ads appear?**

Demand Gen ads can appear across eligible Google surfaces, including YouTube, Discover, Gmail, Google Maps, and the Google Display Network. Available placements can depend on your campaign settings, ad format, assets, and Google Ads eligibility.

**Q: What if I cannot access Ad Manager in my sub-account?**Confirm that Ad Manager has been enabled for the sub-account and that the correct user permissions have been granted. Agency-level setup and staff access control both affect visibility.

**Q: Is Demand Gen the same as a Google Search campaign?**No. Demand Gen is a visually driven campaign type built for earlier-stage discovery and engagement across Google surfaces, while Search campaigns focus on keyword-driven search intent. HighLevel documents them as separate campaign workflows.

**Q: How do Lookalike Segments work in Demand Gen campaigns?**

Lookalike Segments use an existing seed audience to help Google find additional users who may be relevant to your campaign. Google is transitioning Demand Gen Lookalikes toward an audience-suggestion model during 2026, where the seed audience and selected reach level can act as signals rather than strict targeting limits. The exact behavior available may depend on your Google Ads account and rollout status.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Connect Google with Ad Manager](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000004542?portalId=48000045315)

- [Ad Manager - Create & Manage Google Ads Offline Conversions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000005431?portalId=48000045315)

- [Ads Manager - Audience Segments for Google Ads](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000006800?portalId=48000045315)

- [Ad Manager - Configure Google Ads Additional Assets at Campaign Level](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000005789?portalId=48000045315)

- [Ad Manager - Create a Google Search Ad Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000004543?portalId=48000045315)

source_md:
**Restaurant Settings** lets you manage how your restaurant operates in HighLevel. Update your business information, opening hours, pickup and delivery options, payments, reservations, floor layout, and notifications from one place. These settings help your team run daily operations and keep guests informed. This article explains the available options and how to change them.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is Restaurant Settings?](#What-Is-Restaurant-Settings?)
  - [Key Benefits of Restaurant Settings](#Key-Benefits-of-Restaurant-Settings)
  - [Restaurant Details](#Restaurant-Details)
  - [Prep Time, Pickup, and Delivery](#Prep-Time,-Pickup,-and-Delivery)
  - [Dine-in and Floor Layout](#Dine-in-and-Floor-Layout)
  - [Reservation Settings](#Reservation-Settings)
  - [Checkout and Payments](#Checkout-and-Payments)
  - [Internal and Customer Notifications](#Internal-and-Customer-Notifications)
  - [How to Set Up Restaurant Settings](#How-to-Set-Up-Restaurant-Settings)

---

# **What Is Restaurant Settings?**

Restaurant Settings brings together the information entered during [Restaurant Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009586-restaurant-setup-guide-get-ready-to-take-orders-and-reservations) and ongoing options for dine-in, tips, reservations, and notifications. Changes can be reflected wherever the settings are used, including your restaurant website, Restaurant Orders, and Reservations.

![The pages in Restaurant Settings, grouped the way they appear on the left.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883815/original/ir-qM7Nl7-TyzSBjMvNAymUm5K5Iqgv0WA.png?1793738249)

---

## **Key Benefits of Restaurant Settings**

Keeping your settings up to date helps your team fulfill orders, manage tables, and communicate accurate information to guests.

- **Centralized management:** Update restaurant details, hours, and service rules from one location.
- **Flexible ordering:** Control pickup, delivery, preparation times, and ordering availability.
- **Pricing control:** Set order markups, delivery fees, payment options, and tips.
- **Table management:** Configure dining areas, capacities, and reservation rules.
- **Clear communication:** Customize alerts for staff and updates for guests.

---

## **Restaurant Details**

Restaurant Details stores the information guests use to recognize, locate, and contact your restaurant. Select **Edit** on a card to update its settings. The phone preview shows how your restaurant information appears to guests; customize the actual guest pages through [Restaurant Website](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009590-restaurant-website-how-to-customize-and-publish-your-site).

- **Brand:** Business name, logo, and brand color.
- **Location:** Address, phone number, email, and time zone.
- **Store hours:** Weekly opening hours that pickup, delivery, reservations, and your menu can follow.
- **Links:** Social media pages and other links.

**Important:** Your business name, logo, and location are shared with your HighLevel sub-account. Editing them here changes them wherever they are used, including your business profile, emails, invoices, and website.

---

### **Add a Closure**

Closures mark dates when the whole restaurant is unavailable, such as holidays or staff training days.

1. Under **Closures**, click **Add closure**.
2. Select the **Date** and optionally enter a **Reason**.
3. Click **Add closure** to save.

To stop only pickup or delivery, use **Scheduled downtime** for that service instead.

---

## **Prep Time, Pickup, and Delivery**

Preparation and fulfillment settings determine how long orders take, when guests can place them, and what they pay for pickup or delivery. Review these settings when your kitchen capacity, service hours, or delivery coverage changes.

### **Prep Time**

Enter the **Default prep time** in minutes. It represents how long your kitchen usually needs to prepare an order and is used to estimate readiness for pickup and delivery.

### **Pickup**

Pickup lets guests place orders online and collect them at your restaurant. The top of the Pickup page indicates whether guests can order now.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Do you want to offer pickup?** | Turns pickup ordering on or off. |
| **Use your store hours** | Accepts pickup orders during store hours. Click **See store hours** to check them. |
| **Take scheduled orders** | Allows guests to order ahead and choose a later pickup time. |
| **Pickup markup** | Adds a percentage to item prices on pickup orders. Enter 0 for menu prices. |
| **Scheduled downtime** | Stops pickup on a chosen date. Click **Add time**, select a **Date**, add a **Reason**, and click **Add downtime**. |
| **Advanced settings → Order limits** | Sets an optional minimum order amount before tax. Leave it empty for no minimum. |

Click **Save changes** after updating pickup.

**Note:** When pickup is enabled but the website has not been published, the page may show **On, but guests can’t order it yet**. Publish your restaurant website to make pickup ordering available.

![Pickup settings. The top of the page shows whether guests can order pickup now.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883817/original/J0IKehtk5O6JLlvw2PAQQ6cw7XpQ0gSpIg.png?1793738250)

### **Delivery**

Delivery lets guests order online and receive their food from your restaurant's delivery staff. It uses the same hours, scheduled orders, markups, downtime, and order limits as pickup, plus delivery areas and fees.

**Delivery pricing** determines how far you deliver and what customers pay:

- **How you charge:** Use **Distance bands** for a fixed fee per range (for example, $2.99 for 2–4 miles) or **Per mile** for a distance-based rate.
- **Distance unit:** Select **Miles** or **Kilometers**.
- **Measured from:** Review the origin address and click **Change** to select a different one.
- **Delivery areas:** Define each area's distance, delivery fee, free-delivery threshold, and estimated delivery time. Areas appear as rings around your restaurant on the map.

**To add a delivery area:**

1. Click **Add area** and choose **Distance** as the area type.
2. Enter an **Area name** and starting and ending distances.
3. Enter the **Delivery fee** (0 for free delivery).
4. Optionally turn on **Free delivery on larger orders** and enter the qualifying amount.
5. Set the **Estimated delivery time** and click **Add area**.

![Add a delivery area.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883820/original/4X27u7QKByQ9odie8ujrPoAgNAXMu3oPxA.png?1793738251)

To modify or remove an area, use its three-dot menu and choose **Edit** or **Delete**. To check guest pricing, click **Test an address** and enter an address or distance. This shows the delivery area, fee, and time without changing your settings.

![Test an address shows what a guest would pay.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883819/original/IEXLnvlriuzeA_ZPHMkgslHYRQ1mSkaAwg.png?1793738251)

Click **Save changes** when finished.

**Note:** **Delivery markup** increases item prices separately from the delivery fee. For example, a 10% markup changes a $15 item to $16.50. Use 0 for menu prices. The supplied settings identify ZIP code areas as coming soon.

---

## **Dine-in and Floor Layout**

Dine-in settings control what guests see when they scan table QR codes, while Floor Layout defines the tables used for reservations and walk-ins.

### **Dine-in**

Turn **Dine-in** on or off to control table service. Your team takes dine-in orders in [Reservations](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009589-restaurant-reservations-manage-bookings-tables-and-guests); the menu item price is what the table pays.

Under **A scanned code opens**, choose **Your menu** (the current HighLevel menu), **Menu PDF**, or **Menu link** (an external menu). Guests view the menu, and your staff takes their order.

**Note:** Table QR codes are available once your restaurant website is published. Until then, click **Set up website**.

### **Floor Layout**

Floor Layout is a map of your dining areas and tables. Each reservation or walk-in is assigned to a configured table.

1. Choose the dining area beside the page title, such as **Main dining**. Use the three-dot menu beside **Save** for additional area options.
2. Use the top toolbar to add round, square, or rectangular tables, booths, walls, dividers, or text labels. Undo and redo are also available.
3. Drag items into position. Use select, pan, grid, snap, zoom, and **Fit area** tools to adjust your view.
4. Click a table to edit its **Label**, **Capacity**, **Table/Booth** type, **Active** status, **Bookable online** status, or **Minimum party**.
5. Click **Save**.

![Floor layout. Use the toolbar at the top to add tables, booths, walls, dividers and labels.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883833/original/DeC10sPgcF7qCOwMwxfZndQyBpx2PqY0rg.png?1793738257)

---

## **Reservation Settings**

Reservation rules determine when guests can book, how long they have a table, and whether they need to pay a deposit. These settings help manage availability and allow time to prepare tables between parties.

### **Reservation Hours and Table Rules**

- **Use your store hours:** Leave this on for bookings during store hours, or turn it off to set separate reservation hours.
- **Time slots:** Choose reservation start intervals of 15, 20, 30, 45, or 60 minutes, or use **Custom**.
- **Table times:** Define how long parties of each size keep their tables. Edit or delete existing rows or click **Add party size**.
- **Time between reservations:** Leave a buffer to clear and reset the table after a party.

![Table rules decide how long each party keeps a table.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883846/original/XeSeRmc4Qq_8wgk79KukWvrNA2N9hxikDw.png?1793738260)

### **Online Booking**

Online booking rules limit which reservations guests can make through your restaurant website while allowing staff to handle special requests.

- **Online booking:** Enable or disable website reservations.
- **When guests can book:** Set the **Earliest** and **Latest** booking limits, such as 30 days ahead and two hours before a reservation.
- **Largest party online:** Set the maximum online party size. Larger groups are directed to call; staff may still book them.
- **Areas guests can book:** Turn an area off to reserve it for staff bookings.
- **Let guests choose their area:** Allow guests to select a dining area when booking.

### **Deposits**

A reservation deposit is paid upfront and applied toward the guest's final bill. A connected payment provider is required.

1. Turn on **Deposits**.
2. Enter the **Amount** and choose **Per guest** or **Per reservation**.
3. Configure **Deposit rules** and whether to **Charge deposits on bookings made by staff**.
4. Set the eligibility period for a **Full refund**.
5. Click **Save settings**.

![Deposits turned on: $10 per guest for parties of 6 or more.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883849/original/CklnlB9EofIha_GNXebpJ6uePMqndp7TOA.png?1793738260)

---

## **Checkout and Payments**

Checkout and Payments controls online card payments and the tip options offered to guests. Review these settings before accepting real orders or charging reservation deposits.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Payment provider** | Shows whether a provider is connected. Click **Manage in Payments** to update it. |
| **Live mode** | When on, the restaurant accepts real orders and payments. Turn it off for test mode. |
| **Tips** | Configure **Suggested amounts**. Click **Add** for another amount, or remove an existing one. |
| **Default tip** | Sets the initially selected tip, such as 15%. |
| **Let guests enter their own amount** | Allows guests to enter a custom tip instead of choosing a suggestion. |

![Checkout and payments. Turn off Live mode to run in test mode.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883832/original/_U1Zm-YAT-ttRYhoFka4-2bdTAp-A7sh9w.png?1793738257)

Checkout and payments. Turn off Live mode to run in test mode.

**Important:** Enable **Live mode** before accepting real orders and payments.

---

## **Internal and Customer Notifications**

Internal notifications alert your staff when orders or reservations need attention. Customer notifications keep guests informed as their orders and bookings move through different stages.

### **Internal Notifications**

Choose the **Orders** or **Reservations** tab to adjust staff notifications.

- **On-screen order alert:** A pop-up and sound for a new order until it is accepted.
- **Who gets it:** Configure **All staff at this location** with **Ring**, **Silent**, or **Off**, and add staff **Exceptions**.
- **Sound:** Choose the **Ringtone**, **Repeat** frequency, and device **Volume**. Click **Send test alert** to check it.
- **Order staff alerts:** Notify staff of a **New order** waiting for acceptance or an **Order canceled** (including rejection, noncollection, or failed delivery).
- **Reservation staff alerts:** Notify the team about a **New reservation** (online or staff-made) or a **Cancellation**. Click the pencil icon (**Edit**) to change an alert.

![Internal notifications for orders: who gets the on-screen alert, and how it sounds.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883842/original/cWuDvEwrBh7deKqTjPaZgFZ32ev6B8iiNQ.png?1793738260)

### 

### **Customer Notifications**

Use the **Orders** and **Reservations** tabs to manage the messages guests receive.

| For | Messages |
| --- | --- |
| **Pickup orders** | Order received, Order accepted, Ready to collect, Collected, Order canceled |
| **Delivery orders** | Order received, Order accepted, On its way, Delivered, Order canceled |
| **Reservations** | Confirmed (with booking-management link), Reminder, Updated, Canceled. The supplied configuration describes SMS reminders two hours before and email reminders 24 hours before. |

**To edit a message:**

1. Click the pencil icon (**Edit**) beside the notification.
2. Select **Email** or **SMS** and turn **Enabled** on or off.
3. Edit the email **Subject** and message. Use **Insert merge tag** to add guest names, order numbers, and other details; **Reset to default** restores the starting content.
4. Optionally enter a **From name** and **From email**.
5. Check the **Preview** and click **Save**.

![Edit a message. The preview on the right shows what guests get.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883848/original/uRbOZFOzUz8wCYn_cSw8oJ2YMO7DKtBl_Q.png?1793738260)

---

## **How to Set Up Restaurant Settings**

Opening Restaurant Settings gives you access to the controls described above. Review and save each applicable page so your ordering options, reservation rules, and notifications match how your restaurant operates.

1. In the HighLevel sub-account, click **Restaurants** in the left navigation.
2. In the Restaurants panel, click **Restaurant Settings**.

![Click Restaurants, then Restaurant Settings.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883814/original/v_cHquBkdzfrVl9PQ71hWjL_9HbMvUN_Lw.png?1793738249)

3. Choose a page from the left menu. **Restaurant details** opens first.
4. Update the settings you need and use the page's **Save**, **Save changes**, or **Save settings** control.

![Restaurant Settings, open on Restaurant details. Choose a page from the list on the left.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084883818/original/gPpQBh4ZW43kbkgw9tpmk980f0AT69Fygw.png?1793738250)

**Tip:** Some restaurant pages link directly to these settings. For example, **Pickup settings** on the Restaurant Website dashboard opens **Pickup**.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why does pickup say “On, but guests can’t order it yet”?**

Your restaurant website is not yet published. Publish it through Restaurant Website.

**Q: How do I close for a holiday without disabling everything permanently?**

Use **Restaurant details → Add closure** for the restaurant, or **Scheduled downtime** for pickup or delivery alone.

**Q: Can I test payments before going live?**

Yes. Turn off **Live mode** under Checkout and Payments, then turn it back on before taking real orders.

**Q: Why isn't a table available for online booking?**

Check its **Active** and **Bookable online** settings, party-size rules, reservation hours, and whether the dining area permits online bookings.

**Q: Can I keep a dining area for staff bookings only?**

Yes. Turn that area off under **Reservation settings → Areas guests can book**. Staff can still book it.

**Q: Who receives a new-order alert?**

Staff selected under **Internal Notifications → Orders → On-screen order alert**. Use **Exceptions** to apply different settings to individual staff members.

**Q: Can I change the message guests receive after booking?**

Yes. Open **Customer Notifications → Reservations**, edit the message with the pencil icon, and click **Save**.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Restaurant Setup Guide: Get Ready to Take Orders and Reservations](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009586-restaurant-setup-guide-get-ready-to-take-orders-and-reservations)
- [How to Create a Restaurant Menu in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009587-how-to-create-a-restaurant-menu-in-highlevel)
- [How to Manage and Customize Restaurant Menus in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009592-how-to-manage-and-customize-a-restaurant-menu-in-highlevel)
- [Restaurant Orders: How to Manage Orders and Payments](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009588-restaurant-orders-how-to-manage-orders-and-payments)
- [Restaurant Reservations: Manage Bookings, Tables, and Guests](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009589-restaurant-reservations-manage-bookings-tables-and-guests)
- [Restaurant Website: How to Customize and Publish Your Site](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009590-restaurant-website-how-to-customize-and-publish-your-site)

title_en: Opportunity Score in Ad Manager
source_md:
Opportunity Score helps you review campaign readiness in HighLevel Ad Manager before publishing. Available for Meta, Google, and LinkedIn campaigns, it checks applicable setup areas, highlights recommended improvements, and helps you prioritize updates that may improve campaign readiness.

Use Opportunity Score as a pre-launch review tool to catch setup gaps before sending your campaign for publishing. Recommendations are tailored to the selected advertising platform and campaign configuration, so the guidance you see may vary by platform, objective, campaign type, ad format, and applicable settings.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Opportunity Score?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Opportunity-Score?)
- [Key Benefits of Opportunity Score](#Key-Benefits-of-Opportunity-Score)
- [Opportunity Score Panel](#Opportunity-Score-Panel)
- [Platform-Aware Recommendations](#Platform-Aware-Recommendations)
- [Opportunity Score Recommendation Categories](#Opportunity-Score-Recommendation-Categories)
- [What to Fix First](#What-to-Fix-First)
- [How To Review and Improve Opportunity Score](#How-To-Review-and-Improve-Opportunity-Score)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

# **What is Opportunity Score?**

Opportunity Score is a campaign-readiness tool in HighLevel Ad Manager that helps you review important parts of your campaign before launch. It gives you a 0–100 score, a band label, and specific recommendations so you can identify setup areas that may need attention before publishing.

Opportunity Score is available for Meta, Google, and LinkedIn campaigns. It evaluates only the campaign settings that apply to the selected platform, objective, campaign type, ad format, and configuration. This means two campaigns may receive different recommendation categories even when they are created in the same Ad Manager.

A higher score generally means fewer visible setup gaps were detected, while a lower score means there are recommended areas to review before publishing. Opportunity Score does not automatically edit, publish, or guarantee results for your campaign.

---

## **Key Benefits of Opportunity Score**

- **Cross-platform review:** Review campaign readiness for Meta, Google, and LinkedIn campaigns from the Review screen.

- **Clear readiness score:** View a 0–100 score and band label, such as Low, Medium, or High.

- **Platform-aware guidance:** Receive recommendations based on the selected advertising platform and the settings that apply to the campaign.

- **Actionable recommendations:** See suggested improvements for applicable setup areas such as audience, budget, creative, tracking, and keywords.

- **Prioritized fixes:** Use the “What to fix first” list to focus on recommendations that may have the highest impact on campaign readiness.

- **Faster navigation:** Click recommendations or **Fix** links to return to the related section of the campaign builder.

- **Better setup confidence:** Reduce missed setup issues before launching your campaign.

---

## **Opportunity Score Panel**

The Opportunity Score panel gives you a detailed view of campaign readiness before publishing. Use this panel to review the overall score, category-level feedback, recommendation impact, and prioritized updates from one place.

The panel may include:

- Overall Opportunity Score from 0–100

- Band label, such as Low, Medium, or High

- Category cards for applicable setup areas such as Audience, Budget, Creative, Tracking, and Keywords

- Category-level scores or statuses

- Recommendation text explaining what may need attention

- Impact labels such as Low impact, Medium impact, or High impact

- Links that guide you back to the relevant campaign setup area

- A “What to fix first” list with prioritized recommendations

---

## **Platform-Aware Recommendations**

Advertising platforms use different campaign structures and requirements. Opportunity Score adjusts its checks to the selected platform and campaign configuration so recommendations remain relevant instead of applying the same checklist to every campaign.

| **Platform** | **Areas Opportunity Score May Review** | **How Recommendations Are Applied** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Google** | - Keywords - Audience targeting - Budget - Creative assets and ad copy - Conversion tracking - Ad schedule - Language - Placements - Bidding setup - Applicable campaign assets | Only settings relevant to the selected Google campaign type and configuration are evaluated. For example, the Keywords category appears only when keyword configuration applies. |
| **LinkedIn** | - Audience targeting - Location targeting - Budget - Creative configuration - Destination URLs - Lead-gen setup - Language - Other campaign-specific requirements | Recommendations adapt to the selected LinkedIn objective, ad format, and campaign configuration, so different campaigns may display different categories. |
| **Meta** | - Audience and location targeting - Budget - Creative and media - Headlines and ad copy - Calls to action and destinations - Tracking and conversion configuration | Meta uses the same pre-publish Opportunity Score workflow while evaluating settings relevant to the selected Meta campaign configuration. |

```
Note: Not every campaign displays the same recommendation categories. HighLevel considers only the settings that apply to the selected platform, objective, campaign type, ad format, and configuration.
```

---

## **Opportunity Score Recommendation Categories**

Opportunity Score groups recommendations by campaign setup area so you can quickly understand what needs review. Categories are displayed only when they are applicable to the selected platform and campaign configuration.

### **Audience**

Audience recommendations help you review whether your targeting may be too broad, too narrow, or missing important targeting details. Available audience settings depend on the advertising platform and campaign configuration.

Common audience recommendations may include:

- Refining broad targeting
- Reviewing location targeting
- Adding or adjusting applicable interests or audience characteristics
- Checking exclusions
- Reviewing retargeting or similar audience settings when supported
- Confirming the audience matches the campaign goal

---

### **Budget**

Budget recommendations help you identify whether your selected budget may limit campaign delivery or optimization. A budget that may be restrictive for the selected campaign configuration can be highlighted before launch.

Common budget recommendations may include:

- Increasing a daily or lifetime budget
- Reviewing whether the budget matches the audience or campaign configuration
- Confirming the campaign has enough budget to support meaningful delivery
- Checking budget settings before publishing

---

### **Creative**

Creative recommendations help you review the ad content and assets before publishing. The creative elements evaluated depend on the selected platform, campaign objective, and ad format.

Common creative recommendations may include:

- Reviewing incomplete or potentially limiting ad copy
- Adding or updating media or creative assets
- Checking destination links
- Confirming the call-to-action matches the campaign goal
- Reviewing applicable headlines, descriptions, or other ad assets
- Previewing the ad before launch

---

### **Tracking**

Tracking recommendations help you review conversion-related setup when it applies to the campaign. This can help identify missing or potentially limiting measurement settings before publishing.

Common tracking recommendations may include:

- Reviewing conversion setup
- Confirming destination or event tracking details
- Checking tracking-related warnings before publishing
- For Meta campaigns, tracking recommendations may also review:
  - Meta Pixel or Conversions API events mapped to the primary conversion goal
  - Standard or custom conversion setup
  - Event destinations, such as a website or lead form

---

### **Keywords**

Keyword recommendations are available for applicable Google campaign types and help you review whether the selected keyword setup could be refined before launch. The Keywords category appears only when keyword configuration is relevant to the campaign.

Keyword recommendations may include:

- Refining selected keywords
- Reviewing keyword match types when applicable
- Adding negative keywords when appropriate
- Reviewing keyword configuration against the campaign goal

---

## **What to Fix First**

The “What to fix first” area helps you prioritize recommended updates instead of reviewing every setup field manually. Recommendations are ordered based on their potential impact on campaign readiness, allowing you to focus on higher-priority items first.

Use this area as a pre-publishing checklist. Each applicable item includes a **Fix** action that takes you back to the related section of the campaign builder so you can review the setting more quickly.

Example prioritized fixes may include:

1. Increase budget
2. Refine audience targeting
3. Refine keywords for an applicable Google campaign
4. Review creative
5. Check tracking setup

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080118093/original/DohavbWj8SBgPy-zTejzbH9RlAPFlDlNNA.png?1788529454)**

---

## **How To Review and Improve Opportunity Score**

Reviewing Opportunity Score before publishing helps you catch setup gaps while the campaign is still editable. Completing the relevant campaign setup first gives Opportunity Score more information to evaluate and can produce more useful recommendations.

### **Go to Marketing > Ad Manager**

Open **Marketing**, then select **Ad Manager**. This is where you can create, edit, review, and publish supported advertising campaigns in HighLevel.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075234875/original/E_DubxkONAe8ulWWMMyNVlUNbcf0js8_Vg.png?1783260458)

### **Create a new campaign or open an existing draft**

Start a new Meta, Google, or LinkedIn campaign, or open an eligible campaign draft that has not been published yet. Opportunity Score is available on the Review screen before publishing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237031/original/_kK1YFsKJHIM_kFVAy6CMIbIfT2wWuXMSg.png?1783266370)

### **Complete the campaign setup steps**

Fill out the required campaign details before reviewing the score. Depending on the platform and campaign configuration, this may include audience, budget, creative, tracking, keywords, destination URLs, language, placements, bidding, lead-gen settings, or other applicable fields.

Completing the applicable setup first helps Opportunity Score provide more relevant recommendations because only settings that apply to the selected campaign are evaluated.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237083/original/VY0fcVJV6ybWqsK-iBBSSOcRgWTT7C3ihA.png?1783266477)

### **Go to the Review screen**

Open the **Review** screen after completing the campaign setup. Opportunity Score appears before publishing so you can check campaign readiness while the campaign is still editable.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237099/original/lIV1M4e5MkbPQeDHYChZ_b6bF-e9YEPWdA.png?1783266548)

### **Open the Opportunity Score panel**

Click the **Opportunity Score** area to open the score panel. The panel gives you a closer look at the overall score, score band, applicable category feedback, recommendation impact, and suggested improvements.

### 

### **Review the overall score and band label**

Check the 0–100 score and band label, such as **Low**, **Medium**, or **High**. The score gives you a quick snapshot of campaign readiness based on the applicable setup areas reviewed by Opportunity Score.

A lower score does not prevent publishing, but it means there may be setup recommendations worth reviewing before launch.

### 

### **Review recommendation categories**

Look through the category cards in the panel. Depending on the campaign, Opportunity Score may display areas such as **Audience**, **Budget**, **Creative**, **Tracking**, and **Keywords**.

Not every campaign will show the same categories. HighLevel displays only the recommendations relevant to the selected platform, objective, campaign type, ad format, and applicable settings.

### 

### **Check impact labels**

Review the impact labels attached to recommendations, such as **Low impact**, **Medium impact**, or **High impact**. Impact labels help you decide which updates may matter most for campaign readiness.

Prioritize higher-impact items first when you are short on time or reviewing multiple recommendations.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237218/original/pbE5SCRwRHUelaznW43Qqa9LqyAsoeHy5w.png?1783267106)

### **Review the What to fix first list**

Use the **What to fix first** list as a prioritized checklist. This area highlights recommended updates based on their potential impact on campaign readiness.

Items vary by campaign and may include increasing budget, refining audience targeting, refining Google keywords, reviewing creative, or checking tracking setup.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237228/original/84Qn23MxEfKyp6DfeKJdcXojWwwMbqZTXw.png?1783267163)

### **Click a recommendation or Fix link**

Click a recommendation or **Fix** action to return to the related section of the campaign builder. This helps you move directly from the recommendation to the setup area that may need attention.

### **Make the suggested update**

Review the related setup area and decide whether to apply the recommendation. Recommendations are guidance, not automatic changes, so use your campaign goal and business context before changing campaign settings.

### **Return to the Review screen**

After making updates, return to the **Review** screen. Opportunity Score may update based on the changes made to the campaign setup.

### **Review the updated Opportunity Score**

Check the score, band label, category feedback, and recommendations again. Continue making updates if needed, or move forward if the campaign setup looks ready.

### **Publish the campaign when ready**

Once you have reviewed the score and made any appropriate changes, complete your final campaign review and publish when ready.

Opportunity Score helps with pre-launch readiness, but it does not guarantee campaign delivery, conversions, revenue, or performance. After publishing, use Ad Manager statistics to measure actual campaign results.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155075237266/original/o0cC6tMR1odZ7SWmIHtJFVs13krKOzTStw.png?1783267246)

```
Note: Opportunity Score provides guidance to help improve campaign readiness. Recommendations do not automatically modify campaign settings and do not predict or guarantee delivery, conversions, revenue, or campaign performance.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does Opportunity Score publish or edit my campaign automatically?**

No. Opportunity Score only provides guidance. It does not automatically change campaign settings, publish the campaign, or apply recommendations for you.

**Q: Can I publish a campaign with a Low Opportunity Score?**

Yes. A high score is not required to publish. However, reviewing the recommendations before launch can help you identify setup gaps that may need attention.

**Q: Does Opportunity Score guarantee better campaign performance?**

No. Opportunity Score is a pre-launch setup guidance tool. It does not predict or guarantee delivery, conversions, revenue, or future campaign performance.

**Q: Why did my Opportunity Score change after editing my campaign?**

The score may update when you change applicable campaign settings. Return to the Review screen after making updates to review the latest score and recommendations.

**Q: Why do two campaigns show different recommendation categories?**

Opportunity Score considers the platform, objective, campaign type, ad format, and applicable settings for each campaign. Because campaign configurations differ, two campaigns may receive different categories and recommendations.

**Q: Do all Meta, Google, and LinkedIn campaigns receive the same recommendations?**

No. Recommendations are platform-aware and campaign-specific. HighLevel displays only the checks and recommendations that apply to the selected campaign configuration.

**Q: Do I need to fix every recommendation?**

No. Recommendations are guidance, not required actions unless they relate to a required campaign setup field. Use your campaign goal and business context to decide which recommendations to apply.

**Q: What happens when I click Fix?**

Clicking **Fix** takes you to the related section of the campaign builder where you can review or update that part of the campaign setup.

**Q: Does Opportunity Score measure live campaign performance?**

No. Opportunity Score helps review campaign readiness before publishing. Use Ad Manager statistics after launch to evaluate live or published campaign performance.

---

## **Related Articles**

title_en: Campaign Rejection Reasons and Resolutions
source_md:
If your A2P 10DLC Campaign registration request is rejected for eligible reasons, you need to correct and resubmit your request. For a full list of eligible rejection reasons see below. If eligible, you can re-submit your Campaign registration after correcting the identified content violation by deleting and resubmitting the campaign.

## Rejection types eligible for resubmission

Each of the below rejection codes are eligible for resubmission. To resolve these issues, please take the corrective action(s) outlined in the table below, and then re-submit your Campaign registration request with the updated information.

| Error Code | Rejection category | Rejection reason | Correction needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 30886 | Invalid Campaign Description | Campaign description does not thoroughly explain the purpose of the campaign or description does not match the use case. | Verify that the campaign description is accurate and detailed. If you are an ISV registering a direct offering to your customers, please indicate that in the campaign description. Resubmit campaign for review. |
| 30893 | Invalid Sample Message Use Case | Sample messages are either not provided, unclear, or content does not match the campaign use case. | Verify that sample messages are accurate and detailed. Sample messages should reflect actual messages to be sent under campaign and indicate templated fields with brackets. At least one of the sample messages needs to include your business name. Use case and campaign description need to match campaign description. |
| 30892 | Invalid Sample Message - Public URL Shorteners | Public URL shorteners are not accepted. The website URL included in the sample messages was either from a public URL shortener or is non-secured. | Remove public URL shorteners from sample messages.  Your sample messages or campaign links use a public URL shortener such as bit.ly or tinyurl. To fix this:   - Use the full web address instead. - A branded short link on your own domain is fine. |
| 30891 | Invalid Website URL | Invalid URL was provided for registration. Websites need to be functioning. If this is a registration pre-launch, it needs to be indicated in campaign description. | Verify that provided websites are functioning or detail is provided if the registration is for a pre-launch website.  Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: the website address on your registration did not load for reviewers, or it points at your form page rather than your business site. To fix this:   - Submit your main business website, not just the page with your form. - Check the address loads with nothing broken, and that it is the same domain as on your brand registration. - Check your buttons and links work, and that social icons point to your own pages rather than the social network’s home page. - If you have not launched yet, wait until the website is live and then resubmit.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: reviewers could not load the website URL on your campaign or brand. To fix this:   - Submit your main business website, not just the page with your form. This is the most common cause. - Check the address loads with nothing broken, and that it is the same domain as the one on your brand registration. - Check your buttons and links work, and that social icons point to your own pages rather than the social network’s home page. - If you have not launched yet, say so in your campaign description and add a URL that hosts screenshots or mockups of your in-progress website. |
| 30896 | Opt-in Error | Opt-in message workflow is not sufficient for campaign type and consent is required or opt-in is shared with 3rd parties. | Verify opt-in meets CTIA's guidelines. All methods of opt-in need to be listed. If opt-in is collected through a paper form or behind a login, please provide a hosted link to the image of opt-in. If opt-in occurs on a website, please provide a link to the website. The website needs to have a privacy policy and terms of service. Ensure opt-in is not shared with 3rd parties.  Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: reviewers did not see clear, standalone consent to text messages on your site. To fix this:   - Remove any other form on the site that collects phone numbers or SMS consent. - Link a live privacy policy and terms from the page the widget sits on. - Check the widget loads on the website URL on your brand registration, not only on a subpage.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: the opt-in you submitted does not clearly show people agreeing specifically to text messages. To fix this:   - Add an unticked checkbox for text messages only. It cannot be combined with email signup or with accepting your terms. - Put wording beside it that names your business, what you will send, message frequency, that message and data rates may apply, and how to stop. - Link a live privacy policy and SMS terms from the same page as the form. - Make sure the screenshot and the opt-in description in your campaign show the same form reviewers will find at your URL. |
| 30919 | Website lacks business information | Reviewers opened the website on your brand registration and could not tell what your business does or that you send text messages. | Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: reviewers opened the website on your brand registration and could not tell what your business does or that you send text messages. To fix this:   - Add your company name, a specific description of what you offer, and contact details. - Add more than one page. A single page with no about section and no description of your products will be rejected. - Remove any leftover placeholder text like [company name]. - Link your privacy policy and Terms of Service on the website.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: reviewers could not tell from the website in your campaign what your business does or that you send text messages. To fix this:   - Submit your main business website, not a landing page or a form page. - Add your company name, a specific description of what you offer, and contact details. "Consulting" is not enough. Say what kind, and for whom. - Add more than one page. A single page with no about section and no product description will be rejected. - Show the registered business name from this campaign somewhere on the site. The footer, terms, or privacy policy is fine. - Mention your text messaging programme, and link your privacy policy. - Remove any leftover placeholder text like [company name]. |
| 30887 | Opt-out Error | Campaign indicated collecting and processing consumer Opt-Outs, but the workflow is unclear, missing opt-out keywords or opt-message. | Verify that opt-out workflow is accurate and update Message Flow (labeled as 'How do end-users consent to receive messages' while submitting) description with opt-out process. If opt-out is managed, add opt-out keywords and update opt-out message to include acknowledgement of opt-out request, confirmation that no further messages will be sent, and brand name.  Your campaign says you handle opt-outs, but the process is missing detail, keywords, or a confirmation message. To fix this:   - Describe the opt-out process in your campaign. - Add your opt-out keywords. - Make your reply to STOP confirm the request, say no more messages will be sent, and include your business name. |
| 30890 | Subscriber Help | HELP message reply does not contain brand name, phone number, or email address. | Verify that subscriber help message contains brand name, phone number, or email address. Message needs to guide customers on who them can contact after replying "help".  When someone replies HELP, your reply does not tell them who to contact. To fix this:   - Add your business name and either a phone number or an email address to your HELP reply. |
| 30889 | Embedded Phone Number | Embedded phone number use is selected, but is not reflective in the sample message. | Verify embedded phone number selection is accurate. Update the Sample Messages with Embedded Phone Number or update Embedded Phone Number selection. |
| 30888 | Age Gate Not Present / Not Acceptable | Age gate is not present. | Verify and add a robust age gate to your website or opt-in policy.  Your site or opt-in flow has no age check, which is required if you sell alcohol, tobacco, or anything else age-restricted. To fix this:   - Ask for a date of birth in your opt-in flow. - Put the check inside the flow for signing up for messages, not just somewhere on the site. |
| 30881 | Invalid Brand Support Email | Support email is not associated with the brand. The brand support email was either invalid or associated with a public domain email. | Verify brand support email is valid and not associated with a public domain email.  Your contact email is on Gmail, Yahoo, or another free provider, and carriers do not accept those. To fix this:   - Use an email on your own business domain, ideally matching your website. - If your email domain is genuinely different from your website domain, explain why in your campaign description. - If you are a sole trader without your own domain, use the same free address that appears publicly on your website or contact page. |
| 30894 | Invalid Brand Information | Campaign registration needs to be associated with the brand behind the campaign. If you are an ISV registering a direct offering, campaign description needs to indicate a direct offering. | Verify brand information is valid.  This campaign was not matched to the brand registered for your business. To fix this:   - Nothing to update in your campaign settings. Contact support with your location ID and we will review the brand link before resubmitting. |
| 30895 | Direct Lending - Campaign and Content Attribute Error | Campaign is for direct lending or loan arrangement and is missing content attribute indicating direct lending. | Verify direct lending or loan arrangement is selected for campaign registration. If the campaign is not related to direct lending or loan arrangement, please update the campaign description. |
| 30903 | Incorrect Sole Prop Brand Registration | Brand behind the campaign does not meet the small business Sole Proprietor (EIN) criteria set by TCR and mobile carriers. Campaign can not be registered with a Sole Proprietor use case. | Register the brand as a standard brand and register a standard or acceptable campaign use case that aligns with the registered brand’s classification.  An LLC, Inc., Co., or any incorporated business cannot register as a Sole Proprietor. Carriers will keep rejecting this until the registration type changes, so resubmitting alone will not work. To fix this:   - If you have an EIN, register your brand again as Standard or Low Volume instead of Sole Prop. - Then submit your campaign, choosing a use case that fits the new registration. |
| 30907 | Website URL Validation Issue | Website URL does not match the campaign description or Brand information. | Confirm the website aligns with the registered Brand and Campaigns.  What your site says does not line up with your registered business or what your campaign describes. To fix this:   - Make your use case, your sample messages, and your website all describe the same business. - Look for contradictions. If your site offers consulting, your sample messages should not be retail promotions. - If you trade under a different name, put that name somewhere on the site. The footer, terms, or privacy policy is fine. - If you have changed or added a website recently, mention it in your campaign description. |
| 30908 | Compliant Privacy Policy Required | A compliant privacy policy was not provided in the Message Flow or could not be located on the website. | Verify privacy policy is accessible to end-users and include a direct link to the privacy policy with the Message Flow.  Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: reviewers could not find a compliant privacy policy on your website. To fix this:   - Publish it on a live, direct link on your own domain. A pop-up does not count. - Add this sentence, word for word: "No mobile information will be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. Information sharing with subcontractors in support services, such as customer service, is permitted." - Link it from the page the widget sits on, not only in the footer.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: reviewers could not reach or verify the privacy policy on your campaign. To fix this:   - Publish it on a live, direct link on your own domain. A pop-up or a modal does not count. - Put the link in the footer of your opt-in form. - Add the same link to the privacy policy field on your campaign. |
| 30909 | CTA Verification Issue | Call to Action with the campaign could not be verified. | Provide complete CTA information and all possible methods end-users consent to messaging.  Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: the carrier-mandated, A2P-compliant chat widget was not found on the "Brand Website" URL. To fix this:   - Reviewers use the website URL on your brand registration, not a subpage. Make sure the widget loads at that exact address, in a private browser window, with no login, cookie wall, or 404. - Make sure you have not used a customised chat widget instead of the chat widget generated during your A2P submission. - Remove any other form on the site that collects phone numbers or SMS consent. Reviewers may have assessed that form instead of the widget. - If the site is not live yet, wait until it is before resubmitting.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: reviewers went to the opt-in URL in your campaign and could not find the form, keyword, or consent wording you described. To fix this:   - Open the exact URL you submitted in a private browser window. It has to load with no login, no cookie wall, and no 404. A link to your home page will not do if the form sits elsewhere. - Make the form itself visible on that page, with all required disclosures next to the phone number field. - Match your opt-in description in the campaign to what is actually on the page. Reviewers compare the two. - If you selected more than one collection method (on paper, over the phone, by QR code, or by text-in keyword), describe every one and attach evidence for each. - If your page is not live yet, add a URL that hosts screenshots or a mockup instead. |

## Rejection types ineligible for resubmission

Each of the below rejection errors are due to forbidden messaging categories, and are therefore ineligible for resubmission. Please note that in addition to A2P 10DLC Messaging content restrictions, any use cases that violate the platform's Acceptable Use Policy or Messaging Policy are also not allowed on the platform, regardless of number/sender type or destination country.

| Error Code | Rejection Category | Rejection reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Sex | Submission included content such as nudity, pornography, sex toys, or other adult content |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Hate | Submission included speech that is hateful, profanity, violent, incites violence, or similar speech |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Alcohol |  |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Firearms | Submission included: Firearms, Ammo, Gun Ranges (Common for guns to be sold at Gun Ranges) |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Tobacco / Vape | Submission included products such as: Cigarettes, Cigars, Tobacco Products (Chew, etc), Vape, Vape Juice, or similar items |
| 30883 | Content Violation - SHAFT - Marijuana / CBD | Submission included products such as: Cannabis, Marijuana, CBD, THC, Hemp or similar items |
| 30884 | Spam/Phishing | Spam/Fraud team has flagged the number/business/traffic for spam or phishing. |
| 30885 | High Risk | Spam/Fraud team has flagged the number/business/traffic for fraud or deceptive marketing.  Privacy policy or Terms associated with the campaign may indicate that SMS opt-in consent or phone numbers are being shared with third parties or affiliates. |
| 30897 | Disallowed Content | Submission included: disallowed content types, such as Loan Marketing, 3rd party debt collection, gambling, sweepstakes, stock alerts, cryptocurrency, risk investments, debt reduction, credit repair, 3rd party lead generation, federally illegal substances.  Privacy policy or Terms associated with the campaign may indicate that SMS opt-in consent or phone numbers are being shared with third parties or affiliates. |
| 30882 | Terms & Conditions | Campaign does not meet Terms and Conditions.  Chat Widget (Quick Setup) campaigns: your terms and conditions are missing something carriers require. To fix this:   - Publish terms on your own website on a live, direct link, and link them from the page the widget sits on. - Cover: your business name and what you send, how often, that message and data rates may apply, how to opt out (reply STOP), how to get help (reply HELP), that carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages, and a link to your privacy policy.   Manual (Self-Serve) campaigns: your terms and conditions are missing something carriers require, or reviewers could not reach them. To fix this:   - Host your Terms of Service on a live, direct link, and put that link in your campaign as well as on the opt-in page. - If you prefer, keep the terms inside your privacy policy rather than on their own page, as long as your campaign says that is where they are. |
| 30898 | Excessive EIN | Same EIN is used for multiple brands. Only register minimum number of brands per EIN and do not resubmit until brand registration is updated.  The same EIN has been used for more brands than carriers allow. Resubmitting now will not help. To fix this:   - Reduce the number of brands registered under this EIN before trying again. |

## Who rejected my A2P 10DLC Campaign Registration?

If a rejected Campaign has a valid campaign\_id, it means that our 3rd party vetting partner has rejected it and a vetting charge of $15 has occurred. Resubmissions after a rejected campaign are now $0.

An appeal can be filed for such cases if the rejection was due to a mistake. To appeal a Campaign, please Contact Support to request an appeal.

title_en: FAQs for Affiliates
source_md:
Affiliates use HighLevel’s affiliate tools to share tracked referral links, monitor campaign activity, review leads and customers, and track commissions. The affiliate experience appears inside the Client Portal and is also referred to as the Affiliate Portal. This guide answers common questions about referral tracking, campaign access, manual attribution, affiliate status, and historical affiliate data.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Affiliate Manager FAQs?](#What-are-Affiliate-Manager-FAQs?)
- [Key Benefits of Affiliate Manager and the Affiliate Portal](#Key-Benefits-of-Affiliate-Manager-and-the-Affiliate-Portal)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#Prerequisites-and-Limitations)
- [How Affiliate Tracking Works](#How-Affiliate-Tracking-Works)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [How do new affiliates get their referral links?](#How-do-new-affiliates-get-their-referral-links?)
  - [Why are my affiliate campaign numbers not changing during testing?](#Why-are-my-affiliate-campaign-numbers-not-changing-during-testing?)
  - [Is the Affiliate Portal different from the Client Portal?](#Is-the-Affiliate-Portal-different-from-the-Client-Portal?)
  - [Where can affiliates view their performance?](#Where-can-affiliates-view-their-performance?)
  - [Can affiliates track referral-link clicks?](#Can-affiliates-track-referral-link-clicks?)
  - [Can sales be tracked using coupon codes?](#Can-sales-be-tracked-using-coupon-codes?)
  - [Can I customize an affiliate’s referral ID?](#Can-I-customize-an-affiliate%E2%80%99s-referral-ID?)
  - [Can affiliates see the leads and customers attributed to them?](#Can-affiliates-see-the-leads-and-customers-attributed-to-them?)
  - [Can an admin hide referral email addresses from affiliates?](#Can-an-admin-hide-referral-email-addresses-from-affiliates?)
  - [Where can affiliates view commissions and payout information?](#Where-can-affiliates-view-commissions-and-payout-information?)
  - [Can I manually assign an existing contact to an affiliate?](#Can-I-manually-assign-an-existing-contact-to-an-affiliate?)
  - [Is importing a contact the same as adding a manual sale?](#Is-importing-a-contact-the-same-as-adding-a-manual-sale?)
  - [Can I manually credit an affiliate for a sale?](#Can-I-manually-credit-an-affiliate-for-a-sale?)
  - [What can I do if Add Manual Sale does not show a campaign?](#What-can-I-do-if-Add-Manual-Sale-does-not-show-a-campaign?)
  - [What happens when I remove an affiliate from a campaign?](#What-happens-when-I-remove-an-affiliate-from-a-campaign?)
  - [What happens when I suspend an affiliate from a campaign?](#What-happens-when-I-suspend-an-affiliate-from-a-campaign?)
  - [What happens when I mark an affiliate inactive?](#What-happens-when-I-mark-an-affiliate-inactive?)
  - [What is the difference between removing, suspending, and marking an affiliate inactive?](#What-is-the-difference-between-removing,-suspending,-and-marking-an-affiliate-inactive?)
  - [What happens when I delete an affiliate?](#What-happens-when-I-delete-an-affiliate?)
  - [Do affiliates keep their history after being removed or suspended?](#Do-affiliates-keep-their-history-after-being-removed-or-suspended?)
  - [Can affiliates have sub-affiliates?](#Can-affiliates-have-sub-affiliates?)
  - [Can an affiliate participate in more than one campaign?](#Can-an-affiliate-participate-in-more-than-one-campaign?)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Affiliate Manager FAQs?**

Affiliate Manager FAQs answer common questions about affiliate referral links, attribution, campaign access, commissions, leads, customers, and affiliate status.

Account admins manage affiliates and campaigns in Affiliate Manager. Affiliates access their assigned campaigns and performance information through the affiliate area of the Client Portal, also referred to as the Affiliate Portal.

---

## **Key Benefits of Affiliate Manager and the Affiliate Portal**

Affiliate Manager gives account admins tools to manage affiliate relationships, while the Affiliate Portal gives affiliates access to their own campaign and performance information.

- **Tracked referral activity**: Affiliate-specific referral links allow HighLevel to attribute eligible clicks, leads, customers, and sales to the correct affiliate.
- **Campaign visibility**: Affiliates can review campaigns they are assigned to and access available referral links.
- **Performance tracking**: Affiliates can review metrics such as clicks, leads, customers, commissions, and related campaign activity.
- **Lead and customer visibility**: Affiliates can review referral records attributed to their activity.
- **Commission visibility**: Affiliates can review earned commissions, revenue, payout status, and applicable payout terms.
- **Flexible affiliate management**: Admins can remove, suspend, deactivate, or delete affiliates depending on the intended outcome.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Affiliate tracking depends on the affiliate, campaign, and referral activity being correctly associated.

- Affiliates must be assigned to an applicable affiliate campaign before accessing that campaign through the Affiliate Portal.
- Referral traffic must use the affiliate’s tracked URL containing their affiliate ID for HighLevel to attribute activity to that affiliate.
- Opening the campaign’s standard destination URL without the affiliate ID does not simulate an affiliate referral.
- Affiliate Portal visibility depends on the affiliate’s current campaign assignments and status.
- Account admins can configure certain Affiliate Portal settings, including email masking.
- Unique referral-link clicks are tracked for affiliate campaigns.
- Importing a contact as an affiliate lead is not the same as creating a manual sale or commission.
- Deleting an affiliate is destructive and removes affiliate-related historical data from Affiliate Manager.

---

## **How Affiliate Tracking Works**

Affiliate tracking depends on the unique affiliate information included in the referral URL. Using the correct tracked URL is especially important when testing a campaign. Each affiliate receives a tracked referral link for the campaigns they are assigned to. The link contains information HighLevel uses to identify that affiliate.

Affiliates can get their referral link from the email sent through Affiliate Manager or from their assigned campaign inside the Affiliate Portal.

When testing affiliate tracking:

1. Open the affiliate’s actual referral link.
2. Confirm the URL contains the affiliate’s tracking information.
3. Complete the intended test activity through that tracked link.
4. Review the applicable affiliate or campaign metrics in Affiliate Manager.
5. Review the affiliate-facing information in the Affiliate Portal when needed.

If you open the campaign’s normal destination URL without the affiliate’s tracking information, HighLevel cannot attribute that visit to the affiliate. Affiliate campaign metrics therefore will not change for that affiliate.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

### **How do new affiliates get their referral links?**

When an affiliate is added to an applicable campaign, HighLevel provides access to that campaign’s affiliate referral information.

The affiliate can obtain their referral link from the email sent through Affiliate Manager or from the affiliate area of the Client Portal.

The affiliate should share their tracked referral link rather than the campaign’s standard destination URL.

### **Why are my affiliate campaign numbers not changing during testing?**

Make sure you are testing with the affiliate’s tracked referral URL.

The affiliate’s URL contains their affiliate tracking information. HighLevel uses that information to associate eligible activity with the affiliate.

Opening the campaign’s normal URL without the affiliate ID will not attribute the activity to that affiliate.

When testing, copy the affiliate’s actual referral link from their email or the Affiliate Portal before completing the test activity.

### **Is the Affiliate Portal different from the Client Portal?**

The affiliate experience is available through the Client Portal. HighLevel documentation also refers to the affiliate-specific experience as the **Affiliate Portal**.

Affiliates use this area to access assigned campaigns, referral links, performance information, leads, customers, commissions, and related affiliate data.

### **Where can affiliates view their performance?**

Affiliates can review performance information from their affiliate dashboard in the Client Portal.

Available information can include leads, customers, clicks, commissions, and campaign-related activity.

### **Can affiliates track referral-link clicks?**

Yes. HighLevel tracks unique referral-link clicks for affiliate campaigns.

Affiliates can review their referral-link click activity from the Affiliate Portal.

### **Can sales be tracked using coupon codes?**

Yes. HighLevel supports affiliate sale tracking using coupon codes.

Coupon tracking can be useful when an affiliate cannot conveniently share a referral URL.

See **How to Track Affiliate Sales Using Coupons** for configuration details.
