[**Watch the Claude setup walkthrough**](https://www.loom.com/share/b23bfe32e8be42838bd6eab12a0b932f)

1. Open **Claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**.
2. Enter this server URL:

   ```
   https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
   ```
3. Click **Connect** and complete the LeadConnector sign-in and consent flow.
4. Choose the sub-account(s) to connect and approve access.
5. Start a new chat to use the LeadConnector tools.

### **Claude Code**

Run this command in your terminal:

```
claude mcp add --transport http leadconnector https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2
```

Alternatively, add this configuration to `.mcp.json` at your project root:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "leadconnector": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2"
    }
  }
}
```

On first use, Claude Code opens a browser for LeadConnector authorization. Sign in, select the sub-account(s), and approve access. Verify the connection with:

```
claude mcp list
```

### **Claude Cowork**

1. Open the **connectors / integrations** settings in Claude Cowork.
2. Choose **Add custom connector**.
3. Enter `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2`.
4. Complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow: sign in, choose the sub-account(s), and approve access.

Your Cowork agents can then use the LeadConnector tools.

### 

### **ChatGPT**

[**Watch the ChatGPT setup walkthrough**](https://www.loom.com/share/3ede9d77f11e433a8250ae89dda88532)

1. Open **Settings → Security and login** in ChatGPT and turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Open **ChatGPT Plugins**, select the **plus** button, and create a new plugin.
3. Enter a name and description. Under **Connection**, add this MCP server URL and create the connection:

   ```
   https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/
   ```
4. Complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow: sign in, choose the sub-account(s), and approve access.
5. Start a new conversation and add the LeadConnector connection from the tools menu.

### **Codex**

Add the server and start OAuth authorization:

```
codex mcp add leadconnector --url https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/
codex mcp login leadconnector
```

In the **Codex IDE extension**, open the **gear menu → MCP servers → Add server**, choose **Streamable HTTP**, and enter the same URL. Select **Authenticate** when prompted to complete OAuth.

Other compatible OpenAI clients can use this URL as a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server and complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow when prompted.

### **Cursor**

Add this configuration to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project, or to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` to make the connection available across projects:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "leadconnector": {
      "url": "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2"
    }
  }
}
```

If you already have other servers configured, add the `leadconnector` entry to the existing `mcpServers` object.

Complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow when Cursor prompts you: sign in, choose the sub-account(s), and approve access.

### **Muse**

[**Watch the Muse setup walkthrough**](https://www.loom.com/share/486b586d39184e019cf14633fb52e8fd)**.**

LeadConnector is available as an official app in Muse. Connect the app and complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow:

sign in, choose the sub-account(s), and approve access.

Muse uses `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/muse/v2/` for its OAuth connection.

### **Grok Bot**

**[Watch the Grok Bot setup walkthrough](https://www.loom.com/share/75c7d02515a348689b709838af00089a).**

1. Open **Grok Bot → Connect apps**.
2. Search for **HighLevel** and choose **Add**.
3. Complete the LeadConnector OAuth flow: sign in, choose the sub-account(s), and approve access.

To attach the app to a specific task, you can type `@` in chat and select **HighLevel**.

## **Confirm Your Connection**

Start with a simple request:

Find the last 5 contacts I added in HighLevel.

Your assistant can discover the available contact operations and retrieve records within the permissions you granted. 

For an agency connection, name the sub-account you want to use.

---

## **Working with One or Multiple Sub-accounts**

### **Single sub-account**

A single-sub-account connection is bound to the sub-account you choose during OAuth authorization for the lifetime of that connection.

### **Agency connection**

Where agency-wide access is available, you can connect once and work across the sub-accounts selected during installation.

1. **Choose the sub-accounts during installation.** Select one, several, or all of the sub-accounts offered by the agency installation.
2. **Name the sub-account in your request.** If the intended sub-account is unclear, the assistant uses `list_locations` and asks you to choose.
3. **Switch within the same chat.** Ask about another authorized sub-account without reconnecting.

**For example:**

List the contacts tagged “vip-2026” in Downtown Clinic, then compare the count with Uptown Med Spa.

The assistant resolves the sub-account names, queries each sub-account separately, and compares the results. **Every request targets one sub-account** and is authorized against your installation. The connection cannot access sub-accounts you did not include.

**Availability:** Single-sub-account connections are available today. Agency-wide connections are rolling out through the multi-sub-account, or bulk, installation option. If installation offers only one sub-account, the multi-sub-account option is not enabled for your app yet.

[**Watch the multiple-sub-account walkthrough**](https://www.loom.com/share/c42958a4af2e4b61a67992b07263001d).

---

## **How the Four MCP Tools Work**

The server exposes four unified tools. Your assistant uses these tools to find and run the operations available to your connection.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `list_locations` | Find the sub-accounts available to the connection, or return its single bound sub-account. |
| `search_operations` | Discover active operations for the task, including record searches and read, create, update, and delete actions. |
| `describe_operation` | Check an operation's inputs, example payload, required scopes, and safety information. |
| `execute_operation` | Run an operation within OAuth scopes, permissions, sub-account boundaries, and built-in safety checks. |

You can ask your assistant to use `search_operations` to check what is available to your connection at any time.

---

## **What You Can Do**

The active catalog covers the following areas. Availability depends on your OAuth scopes and permissions.

| Area | Examples of supported operations |
| --- | --- |
| **Contacts** | Search and manage contacts, duplicate lookup, tags, notes, tasks, followers, campaigns, appointments, business assignment, and workflow enrollment. |
| **Conversations & Messages** | Manage conversations; read and send messages; work with attachments, scheduled messages, status updates, recordings, transcriptions, exports, and typing indicators. |
| **Opportunities & Pipelines** | Work with pipelines, lost reasons, opportunity searches, create/update/delete/upsert actions, followers, and status changes. |
| **Calendars & Appointments** | Work with calendars, groups, appointments, events, notes, notifications, free and blocked slots, resources, availability schedules, services, service locations, and bookings. |
| **Payments** | Manage coupons, payment provider configuration, integrations, orders, fulfillment, recorded payments, subscriptions, and transactions. |
| **Products & Store** | Work with products, prices, collections, inventory, reviews, store placement, shipping carriers, zones and rates, and store settings. |
| **Invoices, Estimates & Documents** | Work with invoices, estimates, templates, schedules, manual payments, send and void actions, invoice creation from estimates, proposals, and document links. |
| **Social Planner** | Work with social accounts, posts, comments, categories, tags, CSV imports, category queues, calendar views, edit sessions, and statistics. |
| **Blogs​** | Work with blog sites, authors, categories, posts, and slug checks. |
| **Emails** | Work with templates, folders, imports, campaigns, scheduling, campaign statistics, bulk-action campaigns, workflow campaigns, and email verification. |
| **Forms & Surveys** | Retrieve forms, surveys, and submissions. |
| **Funnels** | Work with funnels, funnel pages, page counts, and redirects. |
| **Workflows** | List and search workflows; browse step types; read, create, validate, update, publish, and delete workflow definitions; and read execution logs and step statistics. Contact enrollment and removal use contact operations. |
| **Voice AI** | Work with agents, agent actions, and call logs. |
| **Phone System** | Work with number pools, active and available numbers, and phone-number purchasing. |
| **Knowledge Base** | Work with knowledge bases, website crawling and training, crawl status, FAQs, and files. |
| **Media Library & Files** | Work with files and folders, create folders, and perform bulk media updates and deletion. |
| **Brand Boards** | Work with design kits, brand voices, and default brand settings. |
| **Custom Objects, Fields & Associations** | Work with object schemas, records, record searches, custom fields and folders, association definitions, and record relationships. |
| **Locations & CRM Settings** | Search and retrieve sub-accounts; work with conversation channels, custom values, recurring tasks, tags, templates, time zones, and task searches. |
| **Businesses & Users** | Search, create, update, and delete businesses and users. |
| **Marketplace & Wallet** | Retrieve installer details, work with wallet charges and fund checks, and retrieve location wallet transactions. |
| **Ads & Affiliates** | Use supported Facebook, Google, and LinkedIn advertising operations, audiences, lead forms, reporting, affiliates, commissions, and payouts. |
| **Additional CRM areas** | Work with supported operations for chat widgets, links, snapshots, campaigns, and courses. |

---

## **Example: complete a task from one prompt**

After connecting, you can give your assistant a request such as:

Find the contact with email [jane@example.com](mailto:jane@example.com), add the tag “vip-2026”, and create an opportunity for them in “Sales Pipeline” worth $5,000.

The assistant uses `search_operations` to discover the contact lookup, tagging, and opportunity operations. It checks their inputs, scopes, and safety information with `describe_operation`, then uses `execute_operation` to find the contact and perform the supported actions. It reports the results back in natural language.

---

## **Permissions and Security**

- **You select the sub-accounts.** Each request is authorized against the installation and can access only a sub-account included in that connection.
- **OAuth scopes limit actions.** The assistant can perform only the operations allowed by your grant.
- **Sensitive actions have additional checks.** Sensitive and irreversible operations are subject to confirmation and safety checks before execution.
- **You control ongoing access.** Review or revoke the connection's access from your LeadConnector account.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

#### **Q: Do I need a Private Integration Token?**

The client connections in this guide use OAuth. Complete the LeadConnector sign-in and consent flow to authorize access; you do not need to manually create or rotate a token for these connections.

#### **Q: Which server URL should I use?**

Use the URL for your client in the connection table above. Claude clients use the Anthropic endpoint, ChatGPT and Codex use the OpenAI endpoint, and Cursor uses its own endpoint. Muse and Grok Bot also offer officially listed apps.

### 

#### **Q: Why do I see four tools instead of hundreds?**

The four tools let the assistant discover and run the active operation catalog. Individual CRM operations are found through `search_operations`, inspected through `describe_operation`, and run through `execute_operation`.

#### **Q: How many operations are available?**

The active catalog includes more than 550 operations across 38 domains. Your connection can use only the operations allowed by its OAuth scopes and permissions. Ask your assistant to search for the operation you need.

#### **Q: Can my assistant create, update, or delete records?**

Yes, where the operation is supported and your OAuth grant permits it. Sensitive and irreversible actions also have confirmation and safety checks.

#### **Q: Can I use one connection for several sub-accounts?**

Agencies can use a multi-sub-account installation where it is enabled. Each operation still runs against one authorized sub-account. If installation only offers a single sub-account, the multi-sub-account option is not yet enabled for your app.

#### **Q: Can the assistant access a sub-account I did not select?**

No. Requests outside the sub-accounts included in the installation are refused.

#### **Q: How do I remove access?**

Review or revoke the integration's access from your LeadConnector account.

---

### **Technical Reference**

For the source documentation, see [LeadConnector MCP Server in the HighLevel Marketplace documentation](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/other/mcp).

title_en: Ad Manager - Audience Controls
source_md:
Audience Controls determine where ads can be shown and, when supported, which audiences a campaign can target. Available controls vary by advertising platform, campaign type, and campaign configuration.

Meta, Google, and LinkedIn use different audience-targeting structures in Ad Manager. This guide explains geographic targeting, Meta Intended Audience controls, Google audience options, LinkedIn targeting, and audience eligibility states.

---

# **What are Audience Controls in Ad Manager?**

Audience Controls define the geographic areas and supported audience criteria used by an ad campaign. The exact controls available depend on the advertising platform, campaign type, and targeting restrictions that apply to the campaign.

Meta campaigns can include optional Intended Audience settings such as Target Interests, Lookalike Audiences, and Retargeting. Google and LinkedIn use their own platform-specific geographic and audience controls.

Some Ad Manager workflows may display a **Budget and Audience** step. Current platform-specific campaign builders can place audience controls at different levels of the campaign structure.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931474/original/oQHUyl1hbE02YHorzzxex41fnnxFPJ0jfA.jpeg?1790473737)

---

## **Key Benefits of Audience Controls**

Audience Controls help define where a campaign can run and which eligible audiences can be included in its targeting.

- **Geographic Targeting:** Select supported geographic areas and use Include or Exclude controls where available.

- **Audience Refinement:** Add optional audience criteria when supported by the advertising platform and campaign.

- **Reusable Audiences:** Select eligible Lookalike or Custom Audiences without rebuilding an audience definition.

- **Audience Visibility:** Review estimated audience size and audience eligibility when HighLevel provides those indicators.

- **Platform-Specific Targeting:** Use audience controls designed for Meta, Google, or LinkedIn campaign requirements.

---

## **Where To Find Audience Controls**

Audience Controls appear at different campaign levels depending on the advertising platform. Use the platform-specific workflow below instead of assuming every campaign uses the same **Budget and Audience** step.

### 

### **Meta Campaigns**

Current Meta campaigns configure Audience Controls at the **Ad Set** level. This area contains Geographic Location and, when supported, the optional Intended Audience settings.

1. From the HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, select **Marketing**.
2. Select **Ad Manager**.
3. Create a new Meta campaign or open the applicable campaign setup.
4. Continue to the **Ad Set** level.
5. Locate **Audience Controls**.
6. Configure **Geographic Location**.
7. Configure **Intended Audience** when needed.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081866049/original/x9ywkr0Yz4G-9Mq8kYEY2wN4DKScJaTIvA.png?1790340567)

### **Google Campaigns**

Google uses campaign-level audience settings rather than Meta's Target Interests, Lookalike Audience, and Retargeting cards. Available controls depend on the Google campaign type.

1. From the HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, select **Marketing**.
2. Select **Ad Manager**.
3. Create or open the applicable Google campaign.
4. Continue to the **Campaign** configuration.
5. Locate the available geographic and audience controls.
6. Configure the required settings before continuing to the next campaign level.

### **LinkedIn Campaigns**

LinkedIn defines geographic and intended-audience targeting at the **Campaign** level inside a Campaign Group. Geographic targeting is required, while Intended Audience attributes are optional.

1. From the HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, select **Marketing**.
2. Select **Ad Manager**.
3. Create or open a LinkedIn **Campaign Group**.
4. Create or open the applicable **Campaign**.
5. Configure **Geographic Location**.
6. Configure **Intended Audience** when additional targeting is needed.

---

## **How To Configure Geographic Location**

Geographic targeting defines the physical areas where a campaign can be eligible to show. Search, radius, Include, and Exclude controls can vary by advertising platform and targeting mode.

### **Add a Geographic Location**

Start by selecting the specific geographic area you want the campaign to target. Review similarly named search results carefully before adding the location.

1. Open the geographic-location search field.
2. Enter the supported city, state, country, place, or address.
3. Select the intended result from the dropdown.
4. Review the selected geographic area on the map.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931481/original/vXBNi9Wn-QyNvOKYX0wudHxNzpSEcXbgLg.jpeg?1790473789)
5. Configure the available radius or Include/Exclude controls when needed.

---

### **Include or Exclude a Geographic Location**

Use Include or Exclude when the selected platform and targeting mode support those controls. This lets you add an eligible area to targeting or remove an area from it.

- **Include:** Adds the selected geographic area to the campaign targeting.
- **Exclude:** Removes the selected geographic area from eligible targeting.

Use the **X** control beside a selected location to remove that location entirely.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931496/original/olNY5AwtrQHyWd0EoJiHd5TaDWglLA69VA.jpeg?1790473885)

---

### **Configure Radius Targeting**

Radius targeting lets you define a supported distance around a selected point when that targeting mode is available.

Use the radius control or slider shown in the campaign builder to adjust the targeting distance. Review the resulting area on the map before continuing.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931493/original/zV0WPtLA5Dxw3P5_wD1vwiPkmPY8MFwnVA.jpeg?1790473844)

#### **Google Radius Targeting**

Google Search campaigns provide separate **Location** and **Radius** geographic-targeting modes. Radius targeting lets you define a supported distance around an address or coordinate.

Google does not support Include or Exclude controls when using **Radius** targeting. The defined radius is included as the campaign's geographic reach.

### **Google Ads: EU Political Ads**

Google campaigns require an additional declaration about EU political advertising. This control is specific to Google Ads and should not be treated as a general Meta or LinkedIn Audience Control.

Select the option that accurately describes the campaign:

- **No, this campaign doesn't have EU political ads**
- **Yes, this campaign has EU political ads**

A selection is required before the supported Google campaign can continue to publication. Refer to Google's current Political Content policy when determining the requirements that apply to a campaign.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931506/original/9YrglahdtHN0wrktDqoY8QStnMdfXM-z8A.jpeg?1790473932)

---

## **Meta Intended Audience Controls**

The Meta campaign builder can provide an **Intended Audience (Optional)** section for refining campaign targeting. The available controls can depend on the campaign configuration and any targeting restrictions that apply.

The current interface includes:

1. **Target Interests**
2. **Lookalike Audience**
3. **Retargeting**

### **Target Interests**

Target Interests lets you refine the Meta audience using the targeting controls available for the campaign.

The current interface can include:

- **Interests**
- **Language**
- **Gender**
- **Age Range**

Select the available criteria needed for the campaign and review the resulting audience before continuing.

Meta Special Ad Category campaigns restrict several of these targeting controls. Current HighLevel documentation states that age and gender cannot be edited and that most detailed targeting options are unavailable for those campaigns.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931511/original/orwwD2RJGE4OnTwvsmnpwdOUDHmsXPBB0w.jpeg?1790474000)

---

### **Lookalike Audience**

A Lookalike Audience uses an eligible source audience to identify people with similar characteristics. The source audience does not have to represent only existing customers.

Select **Lookalike Audience**, then use **Create new or select lookalike audience** to choose an eligible audience available from the connected Meta ad account.

When available, HighLevel displays an estimated audience size based on the selected audience and targeting criteria.

Lookalike Audiences are not allowed for Meta Special Ad Category campaigns.

For detailed creation steps, use the dedicated **Create Lookalike Audiences in Ad Manager** article.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931513/original/P1ZmrdemW5ByatGr-Xn7yl99oK4Qk7mSsA.jpeg?1790474032)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931522/original/rTZKwWvjHZ57k727wzqE_A4518NE_t_DEA.jpeg?1790474059)

### 

### **Retargeting**

Retargeting lets you select eligible Custom Audiences for the campaign. A Custom Audience can originate from several supported sources instead of only prior interactions on Meta.

Supported Custom Audience sources currently include website activity, Facebook Page engagement, Lead Form activity, and Customer List data. Customer List audiences can also use uploaded customer identifiers or HighLevel Smart Lists.

Select **Retargeting**, then use **Create new or select retargeting audience** to choose an eligible Custom Audience.

When available, HighLevel displays the estimated audience size for the selected targeting criteria.

For detailed creation steps, see **Create Custom Audiences in Ad Manager**.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931527/original/nljD8VsP9WZLC0gD7fEeWzoHzqTPbb8OPg.jpeg?1790474115)

### 

### **Audience Status and Estimated Size**

HighLevel displays audience eligibility in the Lookalike and Retargeting audience selectors. The status determines whether the audience can currently be selected for campaign targeting.

- **Ready:** The audience is eligible for selection.
- **Not Ready:** The audience cannot currently be selected.

When available, use the information icon or tooltip to review why an audience is Not Ready.

For example, the interface may report:

> The audience is too small to be used in campaign creation.

**Ready** is an eligibility status. It does not guarantee campaign performance or advertising results.

Estimated audience size shows the approximate number of monthly active Meta users who match the current targeting criteria.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081931528/original/r3YE1HTQDhgsA78745ldPzOGsgbc8jxxDw.jpeg?1790474146)

## **Google Audience Controls**

Google uses a different audience model from Meta. Available Google targeting controls depend on the selected campaign type and should not be described using Meta's Target Interests, Lookalike Audience, and Retargeting structure.

Current Google Search campaign controls include Geographic Location and the required EU political-ads declaration. Additional demographic or audience controls can be available based on the Google campaign type.

### **Google Audience Segments**

Supported Google campaign types can provide **Audience Signals** or **Audience Segments** for additional targeting. HighLevel's current Google Audience Segments workflow supports multiple segment types. ([HighLevel Support Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006800?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Google Ads Audience Segments in HighLevel's Ad Manager : HighLevel Support Portal"))

These can include:

- **Customer Match**
- **Website Visitors**
- **Interest Segments**
- **Lookalike Segments**

Availability depends on the selected Google campaign type.

For detailed Google audience creation and targeting, see **Ads Manager - Audience Segments for Google Ads**.

## 

## **LinkedIn Audience Controls**

LinkedIn uses professional profile and company attributes for audience targeting. Geographic targeting is mandatory, while additional Intended Audience attributes are optional.

### 

### **Geographic Targeting**

Every LinkedIn campaign requires at least one geographic location. Supported location targeting includes countries, states, regions, and cities, with Include and Exclude controls available for selected locations.

1. Open the LinkedIn Campaign.
2. Locate **Geographic Location**.
3. Search for the required location.
4. Add the location to the campaign.
5. Select **Include** or **Exclude** where needed.

### **Intended Audience**

LinkedIn's optional Intended Audience controls use professional attributes rather than Meta's audience cards. Use these controls when the campaign needs additional professional or organizational targeting.

Available attribute categories can include:

- **Company**
- **Demographics**
- **Job Experience**
- **Education**
- **Interests & Traits**

Specific attributes can include options such as industry, company size, job title, seniority, job function, education, and professional interests.

For advanced Include/Exclude behavior and attribute-group logic, see **Audience Targeting for LinkedIn Campaigns in Ad Manager**.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Where are Audience Controls in a Meta campaign?**  
In the current Meta campaign builder, Audience Controls are configured at the **Ad Set** level.

**Q: Is Intended Audience required for Meta campaigns?**  
No. The current interface identifies **Intended Audience** as optional.

**Q: Can I include or exclude a geographic location?**  
Yes, when the selected advertising platform and geographic targeting mode support Include and Exclude controls.

**Q: Can I exclude part of a Google Radius target?**  
No. Current Google Search documentation states that Include and Exclude controls are not supported for Radius targeting.

**Q: What does Ready mean for a Meta Lookalike or Retargeting audience?**  
Ready means the audience is eligible for selection. It does not guarantee campaign performance.

**Q: What does Not Ready mean?**  
The audience cannot currently be selected. When available, use the information icon or tooltip to review the reason.

**Q: Can I use a Lookalike Audience for a Meta Special Ad Category campaign?**  
No. Current HighLevel Meta campaign documentation states that Lookalike Audiences are not allowed for Special Ad Category ads.

**Q: Are Google audience controls the same as Meta Intended Audience controls?**  
No. Google uses platform-specific geographic targeting and Audience Segment features.

**Q: Does LinkedIn use the same audience controls as Meta?**  
No. LinkedIn uses mandatory geographic targeting and optional professional attributes such as company, job experience, education, demographics, and professional interests.

---

### **Related Articles**

- Ad Manager - Create New Facebook Ad Campaigns [Open article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002435-create-new-ad-campaign-in-ad-manager?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Create Custom Audiences in Ad Manager [Open article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003236?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Create Lookalike Audiences in Ad Manager [Open article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003264-create-lookalike-audiences-in-ad-manager?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Ads Manager - Audience Segments for Google Ads [Open article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006800?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Ad Manager - Create a Google Search Ad Campaign [Open article](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004543?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Custom Objects in Client Portal AI
source_md:
Client Portal AI now supports Custom Objects, making it possible to create interactive member portals that collect and save information directly to your HighLevel CRM. Build portals for service requests, applications, inquiries, and other business processes using natural-language prompts. Client Portal AI can generate the required Custom Objects, fields, and relationships, then present a plan for your approval before creating anything. This gives you more control over your data while making it easier for members to submit and access information.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Custom Objects in Client Portal AI?](#What-Are-Custom-Objects-in-Client-Portal-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Custom Objects in Client Portal AI](#Key-Benefits-of-Custom-Objects-in-Client-Portal-AI)
- [How to Set Up Custom Objects in Client Portal AI](#How-to-Set-Up-Custom-Objects-in-Client-Portal-AI)
- [How Custom Object Detection Works](#How-Custom-Object-Detection-Works)
- [AI-Generated Custom Object Plans](#AI-Generated-Custom-Object-Plans)
- [Custom Object Approval and Modifications](#Custom-Object-Approval-and-Modifications)
- [Payments with Custom Object Records](#Payments-with-Custom-Object-Records)
- [Custom Object Limits and Reuse](#Custom-Object-Limits-and-Reuse)
- [Supported Platforms and Availability](#Supported-Platforms-and-Availability)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Custom Objects in Client Portal AI?**

Custom Objects in Client Portal AI allow you to build member-facing experiences that collect, organize, and display information stored in your HighLevel CRM. Instead of manually configuring every data structure, you can describe what you want your portal to do and let Client Portal AI propose the Custom Objects needed to support it.

A **Custom Object** is a CRM record type used to store information that doesn't fit into standard records such as Contacts, Companies, or Opportunities.

For example, a coaching business might use Custom Objects to manage strategy call applications, while a property management company might use them to collect tenant service requests.

---

## **Key Benefits of Custom Objects in Client Portal AI**

Custom Objects help transform AI-generated portals from informational experiences into interactive tools that support real business processes. By connecting member submissions to your CRM, you can collect structured information without creating every data structure manually.

- **AI-Assisted Setup:** Describe the information you want to collect, and Client Portal AI generates an appropriate Custom Object plan.
- **Centralized CRM Records:** Store member-submitted applications, requests, and inquiries directly in your HighLevel sub-account.
- **Approval Before Creation:** Review object structures, fields, relationships, sample records, and visibility settings before approving changes.
- **Flexible Data Organization:** Create Custom Objects with customized fields, dropdown options, and associations that reflect your business needs.
- **Reduced Duplicate Objects:** Reuse suitable existing Custom Objects instead of creating unnecessary duplicates.
- **Member Record Access:** Allow members to submit and view records through dedicated portal pages.
- **Flexible Record Visibility:** Support individual records, company-associated records, and read-only access to all records.
- **Payment Collection:** Use Pay and Buy buttons with HighLevel invoices when a supported payment provider is connected.
- **Object Limit Management:** Review available options when your sub-account approaches its Custom Object limit.

---

## **How to Set Up Custom Objects in Client Portal AI**

Creating Custom Objects through Client Portal AI begins with a clear description of the information your members need to submit. Reviewing the AI-generated structure before approval ensures that the resulting portal pages and CRM records support your intended business workflow.

Follow these steps to create a portal that collects and saves member-submitted information.

**Step 1: Open Client Portal AI**

Access Client Portal AI in the appropriate HighLevel sub-account and start a new portal build. 

Make sure you are working in the sub-account where the Custom Objects should be created.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083489441/original/mnnqqBlcAS884zE6DpMwPoqleHphSovA2Q.png?1792143479)

**Step 2: Describe Your Portal Requirements**

Enter a natural-language prompt explaining what your portal should do and what information members need to submit. For example:

"A member portal for Northstar Collective, a coaching brand with 80,000 agency owners. Members browse upcoming workshops and apply for a 1:1 strategy call."

You can make your prompt more specific by describing the fields you want to collect.

For example:

"Allow members to submit a strategy call application with their business name, monthly revenue range, primary challenge, and preferred consultation topic. Members should be able to view their own applications."

Clear requirements help Client Portal AI propose the appropriate data structure and member-facing experience.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083489546/original/-B6xIDMfHmw7HdQHAZlEdWxHI3vfy5t7BA.png?1792143513)

**Step 3: Confirm Custom Object Usage**

When Client Portal AI identifies that your request requires saved information, it asks:

**"Use custom objects in your CRM for this?"**

Select **Yes** to continue. Client Portal AI will prepare a proposed Custom Object plan for your review.

If you do not want to proceed with Custom Objects, you can decline the request.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083489710/original/VXJCQogK57aPE9BO3xFxELdLJGo02ZK2jA.png?1792143604)

**Step 4: Review the Proposed Custom Object Plan**

Inspect the configuration generated by Client Portal AI. Pay particular attention to:

- Proposed Custom Object names.
- Fields and dropdown options.
- Relationships with Contacts, Companies, or other Custom Objects.
- Example records.
- Member record visibility.
- Whether existing objects will be reused.

Check that the structure matches the information your business needs to collect.

**Step 5: Request Modifications if Needed**

If the plan requires changes, describe them in natural language.

For example:

"Add an Application Status dropdown with New, Under Review, Approved, and Declined."

Client Portal AI can revise the proposed plan.

Review the updated configuration before continuing.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083490094/original/ZZ45Xv0E_-fYETKn43uyN-pfjixr1hCzKA.png?1792143749)

**Step 6: Approve the Custom Object Plan**

Once the plan meets your requirements, approve it. Client Portal AI then creates the approved Custom Objects in the sub-account's CRM. If you are not ready to proceed, use **Not now** to postpone creation.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083490260/original/aXTg42MoTIeZgj0icfb4rt063mYNfSQKsQ.png?1792143834)

**Step 7: Open the Created Custom Objects**

After the creation process completes, look for links to the new Custom Objects below the Client Portal AI response. Open the links to review the newly created objects in your CRM.

For additional CRM record management instructions, see [Creating and Updating Custom Object Records](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004023-creating-and-updating-custom-object-records).

**Step 8: Review the Member-Facing Portal Experience**

Open the generated portal experience and locate the pages associated with your Custom Objects.

Verify that:

- Each expected Custom Object page is available.
- The submission experience contains the intended fields.
- Record visibility matches the approved plan.
- Payment actions, when included, are configured appropriately.

**Step 9: Test a Member Submission**

Use an appropriate test member account to verify the experience. Submit a sample application or request, then inspect the corresponding Custom Object in the CRM. Also test the relevant member visibility rules using suitable test accounts before inviting real members.

**Step 10: Make the Portal Available to Members**

Once the portal and CRM configuration have been reviewed and tested, use the available Client Portal access and invitation options to make the experience available to members. For general portal configuration, branding, domain setup, and invitations, see [How to Set Up the Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000193-how-to-set-up-the-client-portal-).

---

## **How Custom Object Detection Works**

Client Portal AI evaluates your portal-building prompt to determine whether your requested functionality requires storing information in the CRM. Understanding this distinction helps you write prompts that produce the appropriate portal experience without unnecessarily creating Custom Objects.

When your prompt includes activities that require saving member-submitted information, Client Portal AI displays a confirmation question:

"Use custom objects in your CRM for this?"

```
Important: Client Portal AI requests your confirmation before beginning the Custom Object planning process. Objects are not created simply because a prompt mentions a request, application, or similar activity.
```

---

## **AI-Generated Custom Object Plans**

A Custom Object plan defines the CRM structure required to support the information your portal collects. Reviewing this plan helps ensure that member submissions are organized correctly and connected to the appropriate CRM records.

**Reusing Existing Custom Objects**

Client Portal AI can reuse a suitable Custom Object that already exists in the sub-account rather than creating a duplicate. Reusing an existing object helps maintain consistent CRM data structures and preserves available Custom Object capacity. Review the proposed reuse carefully to ensure that the existing object is appropriate for the new portal workflow.

---

## **Custom Object Approval and Modifications**

The approval workflow provides control over which CRM structures Client Portal AI creates. Reviewing the proposed plan before approval helps prevent unwanted objects, unnecessary fields, and incorrect data relationships. After Client Portal AI generates a plan, you can review the proposed configuration and decide how to proceed.

The available actions include:

- **Request Changes:** Describe the modifications you want using natural language.
- **Approve:** Accept the proposed configuration and allow Client Portal AI to create the required objects.
- **Not Now:** Postpone the proposed creation instead of approving it immediately.

```
Important: Requests for later changes also go through a review process. Existing Custom Object restrictions still matter; for example, HighLevel does not allow an existing object's internal name or primary display field to be changed after creation.
```

---

## **Payments with Custom Object Records**

Payment actions allow certain Custom Object workflows to include payment collection directly within the member experience. This is useful when an application, registration, or request requires payment as part of the business process.

Client Portal AI supports **Pay** and **Buy** buttons that initiate payments through HighLevel invoices. A payment provider must be connected before these actions can process payments. For example, a business could create a portal that allows members to submit a paid service request.

For more information about invoice configuration, see [How to Send Your First Invoice](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006908).

---

## **Custom Object Limits and Reuse**

Custom Object limits determine how many distinct record types a sub-account can maintain. Understanding these limits helps you plan AI-generated portal functionality without unnecessarily using the available CRM capacity.

HighLevel supports a maximum of **10 Custom Objects per sub-account**. Client Portal AI can propose up to three objects within a single plan, but the sub-account's overall limit still applies. When insufficient capacity is available, the review process provides options to:

- Reuse an existing Custom Object that is no longer needed for its original purpose.
- Free an available Custom Object slot.
- Skip the proposed object creation.

For example, if a sub-account already contains nine Custom Objects, it has capacity for only one additional object. A proposal containing multiple new objects would therefore require capacity management or reuse.

```
Important: Deleting an existing Custom Object is not the same as simply removing an unused configuration. HighLevel documentation states that deletion permanently removes the object and its related records, fields, associations, and dependent configurations. Review the consequences before deleting an object to free capacity.
```

Learn more in [Custom Objects in All Plans + Higher Limit](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006631-custom-objects-in-all-plans-higher-limit).

---

## **Supported Platforms and Availability**

Platform availability determines where AI-generated Custom Object functionality can be used. Reviewing supported experiences before building your portal helps prevent compatibility issues and clarifies which features are planned for future releases.

| Platform or Experience | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| Client Portal (Web) | Supported |
| Vibe — Describe it workflow | Supported |
| Branded Mobile App | Not yet supported |

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What happens if I select Not now during the approval process?**

Selecting Not now postpones the proposed Custom Object creation. The objects in that proposal are not created through that unapproved action. The release note does not specify whether an unfinished proposal is retained for later reopening.

**Q: Can Client Portal AI reuse a Custom Object that already contains records?**

Client Portal AI can propose reusing an existing Custom Object. Before approval, review whether its current fields, relationships, and intended use are compatible with the new portal. The release does not specify every condition governing reuse.

**Q: Can Client Portal AI modify existing Custom Objects after they are created?**

Later changes go through another review process. However, the changes permitted by the CRM remain subject to HighLevel's existing Custom Object restrictions, including immutable internal names and primary display fields.

**Q: Can I create more than three Custom Objects using Client Portal AI?**

The AI can propose up to three objects at a time. This does not change the overall limit of 10 Custom Objects per sub-account. The release does not specify a separate cumulative limit on successive plans.

**Q: Does company-level visibility depend on CRM associations?**

The release confirms company-level record visibility and support for CRM relationships. The exact rules used to determine company membership and access should be verified when configuring the portal.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started with Custom Objects](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003896)
- [Creating and Editing Custom Objects](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003897)
- [Creating and Updating Custom Object Records](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004023-creating-and-updating-custom-object-records)
- [Custom Objects in All Plans + Higher Limit](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006631-custom-objects-in-all-plans-higher-limit)
- [How to Set Up the Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000193-how-to-set-up-the-client-portal-)
- [App Permissions in Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002136-app-permissions-in-client-portal-enabling-disabling-a-child-app)

# **What is AI Usage Limits?**

AI Usage Limits help you control, monitor, and manage billable AI usage across your HighLevel account. You can set monthly spending limits at the agency, sub-account, and user levels, decide whether AI should continue or pause when a limit is reached, and monitor usage as it grows. 

Limits apply to **billable** AI usage. Usage that is already included in a sub-account's plan is free and does not count toward a limit — only pay-per-use and subscription overage charges do.

```
Note: By default, no Spending Limit is configured. If Spending Limits are disabled, AI usage can continue beyond included plan allowances and applicable overages are billed at pay-per-use rates. When a Spending Limit is enabled, the "When the limit is reached" setting determines whether AI continues or stops.
```

---

## **Products Covered**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078983290/original/KmcZN3yDQX3Js9H060nDIwwIhAYvkrZ_LQ.png?1787305163)

---

## **Choose What Happens When an AI Usage Limit Is Reached**

Limits are enforced on monthly usage. When a limit is reached, what happens next depends on the setting you choose.

Wherever you set an AI Usage Limit, either through agency defaults or on an individual sub-account, you can configure **When the limit is reached**.

```
Important: Every sub-account uses Keep AI running, just notify by default unless you change the setting. If a limit is configured and usage continues past it, that behavior is expected. Select Block AI at the limit when the limit must be enforced.

A sub-account's own configuration overrides the agency default, including the selected behavior when the limit is reached.
```

### **Keep AI running, just notify**

This is the default option.

AI usage continues after the configured limit is reached, and an alert is sent. The limit acts as a soft threshold that helps you identify when usage needs attention without interrupting client activity.

### **Block AI at the limit**

AI stops when the configured limit is reached. Usage resumes when the limit is increased or when usage resets at the beginning of the next calendar month.

A single setting does not have to apply to every client. You can configure an agency default for most sub-accounts and customize individual sub-accounts when needed.

```
Note: The two options remain unavailable until a limit is enabled. Without an active limit, there is no threshold for these options to control.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078984893/original/DdRZzoVeUEHbJJZfNrQXVgoXV8dy2jxgNw.png?1787305969)

---

## **How AI Usage Limits Work Across Your Account**

AI Usage Limits follow a hierarchy that lets agencies establish defaults while still giving individual sub-accounts and users more specific controls. Understanding this hierarchy helps prevent unexpected behavior when multiple limits apply at the same time.

### **1. Agency-Level Default (Top Level)**

Agency-level settings establish the default monthly limit per sub-account and per user.

They also define the default behavior when a limit is reached:

- Keep AI running and notify
- Block AI at the limit
- These defaults apply automatically to sub-accounts that do not have custom settings.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/8zQ0tjPUuQUQsgvhs24w+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+16.09.42.png)

If you later **change** the **agency** **default**, **sub-accounts** still **using company defaults follow the updated configuration**.

**Pay-Per-Use** and **individual** **AI** **Employee** **plans** are **configured** **separately** because usage limits behave differently depending on the billing model.

```
Note: By default, no spending limit is configured. Sub-accounts and users remain unlimited until a limit is enabled and an amount is entered.

For AI Employee plans, Spending Limits control how much billable usage is allowed after included plan usage is consumed. If Spending Limits are disabled, usage can continue at applicable pay-per-use rates.
```

**![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Ac6uyx8OPwJ1M4E1kThg+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+16.11.40.png)**

### **2. Sub-Account-Level Limits**

Each sub-account can have its own monthly AI spending limit.

**You can:**

- **Override** the **agency** **default**
- Set a **custom** **monthly** **limit** for the sub-account
- Select **alert**-**only** or **blocking** **behavior** specifically for that sub-account
- **View** **current** **usage** against the configured limit

**Key details:**

- **Limits** **reset** at the **start** of **each** **calendar** **month**.
- Progress bars show the percentage of the limit consumed.
- Changing any value moves the sub-account to custom settings.
- Select **Reset to company defaults** to return the sub-account to agency defaults.
- The maximum configurable sub-account limit is **$1,000 per month**.

**![](https://jumpshare.com/share/ijeMw9ZG0HkDK8sBRT6g+/GIF+Recording+2026-08-21+at+17.21.00.gif)**

### **3. User-Level Limits**

User-level limits let you control billable AI consumption for individual users inside a sub-account. These limits provide an additional layer of control when individual team members should have different AI budgets.

```
Note: When both a sub-account limit and a user limit apply, the limit with the least remaining allowance takes effect first.

For example, if a user has $2 remaining on a $20 user limit while the sub-account still has $50 remaining on a $100 limit, the user's limit is reached first.
```

**You can:**

- Set a **default** **user** **budget** for the sub-account
- Configure a **maximum** **user** **limit** of **$500 per month**  
    
  ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Bgn86r8ZuiYB28CrUJG3+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+17.39.38.png)
- **Override** the **default** **for****specific** **users** and set **Unlimited** **user** **budget** as well.  
    
  ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/snyzu5sgogVqYwrd1KiT+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+17.40.57.png)

---

## **Pay-Per-Use and AI Employee Plan Behavior**

```
Note: For current plan coverage and AI pricing details, see AI Product Pricing.
```

If AI stops after included usage is exhausted, check the location’s **Spending Limit** and **When the limit is reached** settings. A location configured with **Block AI at the limit** stops AI when its limit is reached, while **Keep AI running, just notify** allows usage to continue.

**If Spending Limits are disabled,**AI continues and applicable overage usage is billed at pay-per-use rates.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079012271/original/59aUPkcqVdKjy6NIu0QTq7POLdI4sfp_LA.png?1787318750)

---

## **What Happens When an AI Usage Limit Is Reached**

The experience after reaching a limit depends on whether the sub-account is configured to continue AI usage or block additional AI activity. Knowing the difference is especially important before enforcing limits for customer-facing workflows.

### **With Keep AI running, just notify**

When the limit is reached:

- **AI actions continue normally.**
- Usage warnings appear as the limit approaches and after it is exceeded.
- Threshold alerts are sent so you can decide whether the limit should be increased.

### **With Block AI at the limit**

When the configured limit is reached:

- AI actions are paused.
- Users cannot generate new AI outputs.
- The sub-account sees a message titled **"[Product] is paused — limit reached"**.

The options available from that message depend on how the sub-account's billing permissions are configured.

What the sub-account is offered depends on how you have set them up:

| If the sub-account | They see |
| --- | --- |
| **Can manage its own billing** | Buttons to increase the limit or enable extra usage themselves, plus **Upgrade plan** where an upgrade is available |
| **Cannot manage its own billing** | **Request more usage**, which sends the request to you |

**AI resumes** as soon as the **limit** **is** **raised** or **automatically** when **usage** **resets** at the **start** **of** the **next** **calendar** month.

```
Important: If you plan to switch a client to Block AI at the limit, consider notifying them before making the change because this setting can directly interrupt their AI usage.
```

---

## **How Billing Works When an AI Usage Limit Is Reached**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079016292/original/X6T-l8OPw_hjiyNnvAtVbOVNRG51-1YuaQ.png?1787320272)

---

## **Requesting More AI Usage**

### **Sub-Accounts That Cannot Manage Their Own Billing**

When a sub-account reaches its limit and cannot self-serve, it can ask you for more.

How it works:

1. The user clicks **Request more usage**
2. The request is sent to agency admins
3. Admins are notified by email and in the **Requests** tab in Usage Limits

The sub-account sees the state of their request while they wait:

| State | What the sub-account sees |
| --- | --- |
| **Request sent** | **Request sent** — "Your agency will review and update your limit." |
| **Sent again before you respond** | **Request already sent** — the same message; duplicates are not queued |
| **You approve** | The new limit applies and AI resumes |
| **You decline** | **Request declined** — "Your agency declined your recent limit request. You can request again later." |

```
Note: A declined request starts a short cooldown during which the request button is hidden, so a sub-account cannot re-request immediately. It is a pause, not a permanent block — they can ask again later.
```

### **Sub-Accounts That Can Manage Their Own Billing**

If a sub-account is allowed to manage its own billing, the request does not go to the agency.

Instead, the sub-account can use the paused message to:

- Increase its own limit
- Enable extra usage
- Upgrade its plan when an upgrade is available

---

## **How to Manage AI Usage Increase Requests**

1. Go to **AI Suite → Plans and Limits**.
2. Click on the **Notifications**icon.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/VtDB6m1FHZ3NiOdiis88+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+20.00.36.png)
3. Under the**Limit Requests** tab, **r****eview** the pending **request**.
4. Choose an action: **Adjust Limit** (approve), **Upgrade Plan**, or **Deny**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/cfIgcRuhES0fFVGRStev+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+20.02.47.png)

If you select **Adjust Limit**,

1. **Review** the **requested limit increase** and you can also **edit the amount as needed**.
2. **Review** the **newly calculated total limit**.
3. **Confirm** the approval.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/T5JJ6L2Oz6IVMIy2uPUZ+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+20.12.51.png)

---

## **Threshold Alerts**

Threshold Alerts provide early visibility into AI consumption before a configured limit is reached. AI Studio also displays in-product usage notification banners that help subscription and pay-per-use users monitor usage or spending and take action when needed.

```
Important: Percentage-based threshold alerts require an active limit. If no limit is configured, or the limit is $0, there is no percentage to calculate. AI Studio pay-per-use spending notifications are separate from percentage-based limit alerts.
```

Alerts are triggered at:

- **70%**
- **80%**
- **90%**
- **100%**

Threshold alerts can highlight users and sub-accounts approaching their configured limits.

Alerts are sent regardless of whether the account uses:

- **Keep AI running, just notify**
- **Block AI at the limit**

With **Keep AI running, just notify**, threshold alerts are the primary signal that usage has approached or passed the configured limit.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/QNT0IpS4dQtlS9IQ9VPr+/Screen+Shot+2026-08-21+at+20.48.10.png)

---

## **AI Studio Usage Notification Banners**

AI Studio displays usage notification banners directly in the product so users can monitor their consumption and take action before reaching their usage limits. These banners are enabled automatically for users who have access to AI Studio.

**For subscription users, AI Studio usage banners appear as usage increases:**

- **70% usage:** Usage alert
- **85% usage:** Warning
- **Approaching or reaching 100%:** Critical and usage exhaustion notifications

- **Sub-account users with rebilling enabled:** The banner can provide an option to adjust usage limits directly.
- **Sub-account users without rebilling:** The banner can provide an option to request a limit increase from the Agency Admin.
- **Agency users:** Relevant actions are available to review and adjust usage limits directly.

```
Note: No setup is required for AI Studio usage notification banners. They are enabled by default for users with access to AI Studio.
```

---

## **Monitoring Usage**

You can track usage directly from the Usage Limits page.

Includes:

- Monthly usage per sub-account
- Usage vs limit visualization
- User-level consumption

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Tapt5BFEff9KKEnaqPgl+/AgencyView_UsageBar_View1.png)

---

## **Rate Limit Window for Ask AI and AI Studio**

```
Note: For more details, explore our guides on AI Studio – Pricing and Ask AI Session Examples & Usage Costs. 
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079163956/original/ghLtE1GFnLFzjdlYQkM8qiqXG8BDwNY1Qg.png?1787575904)

---

## **How does the 5 hour window work?**

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/J2nO0WaTWeJMLDTFqZx6+/ChatGPT+Image+Sep+22%2C+2026%2C+03_33_53+PM.png)

---

## **Where can you See the Used Allowances?**

**AI Suite**  (Agency view) > **Plans & Limits** > Click any sub account or **three dots** and then **Configure Limits** > Increase> Check **Included allowances** & **Rate Limit Windows**. 

### 

---

## **Important Notes**

- Limits apply on a monthly basis and reset at the start of each **calendar month**
- What happens at the limit depends on your **When the limit is reached** setting; the default is to keep AI running and send an alert
- A sub-account is never billed past its limit
- On subscription plans, the **Extra usage** toggle can stop AI independently of any spending limit.
- Limit changes take effect **immediately**; the usage figures shown can lag by up to 5 minutes
- Maximum configurable limits: **$1,000/month** per sub-account, **$500/month** per user

---

### **Related Articles**

- [AI Product Pricing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006652)
- [AI Usage Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007742-ai-usage-dashboard)
- [Fixed-Rate Rebilling for AI Products](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008422-fixed-rate-rebilling-for-ai-products)
- [AI Tools in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002166)

title_en: Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer in Ad Manager
source_md:
The Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer in HighLevel Ad Manager gives advertisers greater flexibility to manage advertising budgets at the campaign or ad set level. You can let Meta automatically distribute your campaign budget, assign individual budgets to ad sets, or enable budget sharing to optimize spend across eligible ad sets. With support for Daily and Lifetime budgets, bid strategies, and post-publish budget adjustments, you can manage your Meta advertising spend directly within HighLevel.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer in Ad Manager?](#What-is-Meta-Campaign-Budget-Optimizer-in-Ad-Manager?)
- [Key Benefits of Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer](#Key-Benefits-of-Meta-Campaign-Budget-Optimizer)
- [Campaign Budget vs. Ad Set Budget](#Campaign-Budget-vs.-Ad-Set-Budget)
- [Budget Sharing Across Ad Sets](#Budget-Sharing-Across-Ad-Sets)
- [Daily and Lifetime Budgets](#Daily-and-Lifetime-Budgets)
- [Bid Strategies for Meta Campaigns](#Bid-Strategies-for-Meta-Campaigns)
- [How to Set Up Meta Campaign Budgets in Ad Manager](#How-to-Set-Up-Meta-Campaign-Budgets-in-Ad-Manager)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer in Ad Manager?**

Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer is a budgeting feature in HighLevel Ad Manager that allows you to choose how your advertising budget is allocated across Meta campaigns and ad sets. Understanding the difference between campaign-

level and ad set-level budgeting helps you select the right configuration for your advertising goals.

When creating or editing a Meta campaign, you can choose between two budget configurations:

- **Campaign budget:** Set a single budget for the entire campaign and allow Meta to automatically distribute spending across the ad sets.
- **Ad set budget:** Set individual budgets for each ad set, giving you more control over how much is allocated to different audiences or advertising strategies.

When using Ad set budget, you can also enable optional budget sharing, allowing Meta to redistribute up to 20% of an ad set's budget between eligible ad sets based on performance. These options allow you to balance automated budget optimization with more granular spending control.

---

## **Key Benefits of Meta Campaign Budget Optimizer**

Managing your Meta advertising budget effectively helps you control spending while giving Meta the flexibility to optimize campaign delivery. The enhanced budget settings allow you to choose the level of control that best fits your advertising strategy.

- **Flexible Budget Management:** Choose between a single campaign-level budget or individual budgets for each ad set.
- **Automated Budget Distribution:** Allow Meta to distribute your campaign budget across ad sets based on available opportunities.
- **Controlled Budget Sharing:** Enable optional sharing of up to 20% of an ad set's budget with other eligible ad sets while maintaining individual budget configurations.
- **Daily and Lifetime Budget Options:** Manage spending using a Daily budget or define a total budget for a scheduled campaign or ad set.
- **Bid Strategy Flexibility:** Select supported bidding strategies, including Highest volume and Cost per result goal, to align campaign delivery with your advertising objectives.
- **Post-Publish Budget Adjustments:** Update supported budget configurations after publishing without creating a new campaign, subject to Meta's editing restrictions.
- **Simplified Campaign Management:** Configure budgets, schedules, and applicable bidding settings directly within HighLevel Ad Manager.

---

## **Campaign Budget vs. Ad Set Budget**

Choosing where your advertising budget is managed determines how spending is distributed across your campaign. Campaign budget allows Meta to allocate spending automatically, while Ad set budget gives you direct control over the budget assigned to each ad set.

**Campaign Budget**

Campaign budget allows you to define one budget for the entire Meta campaign. Instead of assigning a separate amount to every ad set, Meta distributes the available campaign budget across ad sets based on opportunities to achieve your campaign objective.

With Campaign budget, you can configure:

- Daily or Lifetime budget.
- Campaign-level budget amount.
- Applicable bid strategy.

**Example:** If you configure a campaign budget of $50 per day and have three ad sets, Meta determines how to distribute that budget across the ad sets. Spending does not need to be divided equally.

```
When to use Campaign budget: Choose this option when you want Meta to manage budget distribution across ad sets rather than manually assigning a separate budget to each one.
```

**Ad Set Budget**

Ad set budget allows you to define and manage the budget for each ad set individually. Each ad set has its own budget settings, enabling you to assign different amounts to different audiences, targeting configurations, or advertising strategies.

With Ad set budget, you can configure:

- Individual Daily or Lifetime budgets.
- Applicable ad set schedules.
- Cost per result goal when supported by the selected configuration.
- Optional budget sharing across eligible ad sets.

**Example:** If your campaign contains three ad sets, you could assign $20 per day to one ad set, $30 per day to another, and $50 per day to a third.

```
When to use Ad set budget: Choose this option when you want greater control over the spending allocated to individual ad sets. 

Ad set budgets remain individually configurable when budget sharing is enabled, but Meta may redistribute an eligible portion of those budgets.
```

---

## **Budget Sharing Across Ad Sets**

Budget sharing provides a balance between individual ad set budget control and automated spending optimization. By allowing Meta to redistribute a limited portion of budget across eligible ad sets, you can maintain your original budget configurations while giving Meta additional flexibility to respond to performance.

When you select Ad set budget, you can enable the following option:

**Share up to 20% of your budget with other ad sets**

When enabled:

- Meta can redistribute up to 20% of an ad set's budget to or from other eligible ad sets.
- Budget redistribution depends on performance and Meta's eligibility rules.
- Each ad set retains its individually configured budget.
- Budget sharing status is visible within the individual ad set's Budget section.

**Example:** Suppose you have two eligible ad sets, each configured with a $50 Daily budget. With budget sharing enabled, Meta may shift part of the budget between them based on performance, subject to the 20% sharing limit and applicable Meta rules.

Enabling budget sharing does not guarantee that Meta will redistribute the full 20%. Actual redistribution depends on the campaign configuration, eligibility, and performance.

---

## **Daily and Lifetime Budgets**

Daily and Lifetime budgets define how your advertising spend is managed over time. The selected budget allocation level determines whether you configure the amount and applicable schedule for the entire campaign or separately for each ad set.

**Daily Budget**

A Daily budget defines the amount you want Meta to spend per day. For example, you can configure:

- Campaign budget: $50 per day for the campaign.
- Ad set budget: $20 per day for one ad set and $30 per day for another.

The budget is configured at the campaign or ad set level based on your selected budget setup.

**Lifetime Budget**

A Lifetime budget defines the total amount available for the selected campaign or ad set over its scheduled duration. For example, you could configure a Lifetime budget of $500 for a campaign scheduled to run for 10 days. When using Lifetime budgets at the ad set level, configure the applicable start and end schedule for each ad set.

**Switching Between Daily and Lifetime Budgets**

When configuring a budget, changing between Daily and Lifetime may affect the automatically populated budget amount.

- If the default budget amount has not been modified, HighLevel may update the default amount based on the selected budget type or duration.
- If you have manually entered a budget amount, changing the budget type or schedule does not automatically overwrite your entered value.

---

## **Bid Strategies for Meta Campaigns**

Bid strategies determine how Meta approaches ad delivery within your selected budget configuration. Choosing the appropriate strategy allows you to prioritize generating more results or working toward a specified cost per result.

HighLevel Ad Manager supports applicable Meta bidding strategies, including:

**Highest Volume**

Highest volume allows Meta to use the available budget to generate as many results as possible. This strategy is useful when your priority is maximizing results within your selected advertising budget.

**Example:** An advertiser focused on generating the highest possible number of leads within an available budget may select Highest volume.

**Cost per Result Goal**

Cost per result goal allows you to provide Meta with a target average cost for the results generated by your advertising campaign. This strategy is useful when you have a preferred cost per lead, conversion, or other applicable campaign result. When the selected setup requires the target cost at the ad set level, you must enter the Cost per result goal within the respective ad set.

**Example:** If your preferred average cost per lead is $10, you can enter that target in the applicable Cost per result goal field.

---

## **How to Set Up Meta Campaign Budgets in Ad Manager**

Configuring your Meta campaign budget correctly helps ensure that the right amount and applicable schedule are assigned to your campaign or individual ad sets. The following steps explain how to select a budget allocation level, configure supported budgeting options, and prepare your campaign for publishing.

**Step 1: Create or Open a Meta Campaign**

1. Navigate to **Marketing > Ad Manager** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. To create a campaign, click **+ Create Campaign**.
3. Select **Facebook** as the advertising platform.
4. Choose **Start from Scratch** or an available campaign template.
5. Continue to the campaign builder.

To modify an existing campaign, locate the campaign in Ad Manager and select **Edit** from its action menu. For general campaign creation instructions, refer to [Ad Manager - Create New Facebook Ad Campaigns](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002435-ad-manager-create-new-facebook-ad-campaigns).  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083482125/original/y5IHABS6bJ8BvB-WFrnptkS8FCkdzWgLXQ.png?1792140053)

**Step 2: Choose Your Budget Setup**

1. Open the campaign-level **Budget** section.
2. Locate the budget allocation options.
3. Select one of the following:

   - **Campaign budget:** Manage one budget for the campaign.
   - **Ad set budget:** Manage budgets individually for each ad set.

Your selection determines where the applicable budget amount and schedule controls appear.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083481800/original/yZcrQBfn3_qXkJpUF3YsHV4CQYBJeLkaxQ.png?1792139916)

**Step 3: Configure Campaign Budget**

If you selected Campaign budget:

1. Select **Daily** or **Lifetime** budget.
2. Enter the budget amount for the campaign.
3. Configure any applicable schedule settings.
4. Select the supported **Bid strategy**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083481996/original/Z1cD-J401oHpkn9NxzH3_wVFL36KY-Dghw.png?1792139973)

Meta will manage how the campaign-level budget is distributed across the ad sets.

**Step 4: Configure Ad Set Budget**

If you selected Ad set budget:

1. Optionally enable **Share up to 20% of your budget with other ad sets**.
2. Open the first ad set in your campaign.
3. Navigate to its **Budget** section.
4. Select **Daily** or **Lifetime** budget.
5. Enter the individual ad set budget.
6. Configure the applicable schedule.
7. Enter the **Cost per result goal** if required by your selected bid strategy.
8. Repeat the process for each applicable ad set.

You can assign different budget amounts to individual ad sets.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083481962/original/E8vqZxBtL2ETEWlO4Xwp1qVburN1diAFFA.png?1792139954)

**Step 5: Publish Your Campaign**

1. Complete any remaining campaign, ad set, and ad configurations.
2. Click **Review**.
3. Verify your campaign details.
4. Click **Publish Campaign Now**.
5. Select **Confirm** to submit the campaign.

Meta will process the submitted campaign according to its applicable review policies. If you are editing an existing published campaign, submit the supported changes through the campaign editor.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What happens if an ad set is not eligible for budget sharing?**

Meta applies its eligibility rules when determining whether budget redistribution is available. An ineligible ad set may not participate in budget sharing. Check the available settings and contextual guidance within Ad Manager.

**Q: Can I enable budget sharing when using Campaign budget?**

No. The separate 20% budget sharing option is available with Ad set budget. When using Campaign budget, Meta already distributes the campaign-level budget across ad sets.

**Q: Why can't I change my budget configuration immediately after editing it?**

Meta may temporarily restrict subsequent budget setup changes after an update. This restriction can last approximately two hours. You can try again once Meta permits additional changes.

**Q: Can I switch from a Daily budget to a Lifetime budget after publishing?**

Existing HighLevel guidance identifies switching between Daily and Lifetime budget types as unavailable for published campaigns. This differs from supported post-publish changes between Campaign budget and Ad set budget.

**Q: Why is the Cost per result goal field not available in my selected setup?**

The field depends on the selected bid strategy and supported campaign configuration. When the target is applicable at the ad set level, it must be entered within the respective ad set.

**Q: Does setting a Cost per result goal guarantee that Meta will achieve my target cost?**

No. Cost per result goal provides a target for Meta's bidding optimization. Actual results and costs depend on campaign performance and delivery conditions.

**Q: Why did the default budget amount change when I selected Lifetime instead of Daily?**

HighLevel may update automatically populated budget values when you switch budget types or modify the applicable 

schedule. Amounts that you entered manually are not automatically overwritten by these changes.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Ad Manager - Create New Facebook Ad Campaigns](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002435-ad-manager-create-new-facebook-ad-campaigns)
- [Editing a Published or In-Review Meta Ad Campaigns](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004436)
- [How to Create a Meta Engagement Ad with Messaging Apps](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004717-how-to-create-a-meta-engagement-ad-with-messaging-apps)
- [How to Create a Meta Sales Objective Campaign for Conversion](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004797-how-to-create-a-meta-sales-objective-campaign-for-conversion)

title_en: How to Find Pipeline, Stage, and Opportunity IDs in HighLevel
source_md:
Pipeline, Stage, and Opportunity IDs are unique identifiers that can be used when working with HighLevel APIs, webhooks, imports, external integrations, audit logs, and other technical workflows. You typically do not need to enter these IDs when working directly inside the HighLevel interface because pipelines and stages can usually be selected by name. Knowing where these IDs fit becomes important when another system or process specifically requires them.
