title_en: Rentals - Global Settings
source_md:
The **Global Settings** page in Rentals allows you to control how your rental business operates at a global level. It standardizes key configurations—such as scheduling, notifications, branding, and payments—so that all listings and bookings follow consistent rules while still allowing listing-specific overrides.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Overview of Global Settings](#Overview-of-Global-Settings)
- [Key Benefits of Global Settings](#Key-Benefits-of-Global-Settings)
- [How to Access Global Settings](#How-to-Access-Global-Settings)
- [Booking Settings](#Booking-Settings)
- [Notifications](#Notifications)
- [Localized Default Notification Templates](#Localized-Default-Notification-Templates)
- [Booking Page Settings](#Booking-Page-Settings)
- [Payment Settings](#Payment-Settings)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **Overview of Global Settings**

The Global Settings area centralizes all important setup options for your rental business. Here, you can:

- Set business hours and booking behavior defaults.
- Configure customer and staff notification preferences.
- Customize the look and feel of your booking page.
- Set up payment methods and security deposit handling.

These settings apply to all new listings and bookings created after changes are made.

---

## **Key Benefits of Global Settings**

- **Consistency:** Standard rules apply to new listings and bookings, improving predictability across teams.
- **Operational Control:** Business hours and time selection settings shape when and how customers book.
- **Brand Trust:** Booking page branding, layout, and consent text create a cohesive customer experience.
- **Clear Payments:** Currency, Require Payment, and Deposits settings align checkout, invoices, and reconciliation.
- **Flexibility with Safety:** Admins can override some constraints when creating a booking, while buffers & inventory remain enforced.

---

## **How to Access Global Settings**

To access Global settings, navigate to **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Global Settings.**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093097/original/1BwVNtJs8LWa42igzFvnvZeRS-tF7LhAcQ.png?1760557519)**

The left panel will display four main configuration tabs. Each tab manages a distinct part of how your rental business functions.

- **Booking Settings**
- **Notifications**
- **Booking Page**
- **Payment**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093118/original/t0T5AEFnPKIT1FctoO9E7dVAekyhgxAJRA.png?1760557578)

---

## **Booking Settings**

The **Booking Settings** tab defines your business operating hours, scheduling behavior, and overall booking behaviors. Admins can always override global restrictions while creating bookings in-app.

#### **Business Operating Hours**

- Specify working days and hours to control when bookings can be made.
- Use the **+** button to add multiple time intervals within a single day.
- Deactivate any day by unchecking it.

```
Note: While bookings must start and end within your defined business hours, the total rental period can still extend beyond those hours. For example, if your business closes at 11:00 PM, a booking starting at 10:30 PM can still continue past closing time.
```

#### 

#### 

#### **Date-Specific Hours**

- Add custom operating hours for specific dates, such as holidays or events.
- Click **+ Add Date Specific Hours** to define unique availability windows.
- Hours set in Date-Specific Hours override the business availability hours for that day.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093281/original/Zyb2j7x2SVdtdVJeelglJf3sFNQrNR_JfQ.png?1760557856)

#### 

#### **How D****ate Grouping Works**

To keep the list clean, HighLevel groups selected dates:

- Consecutive dates are grouped into one range.
- Non-consecutive dates are split into separate ranges.

Each grouped range can be edited or deleted independently later.

#### **Additional Configuration**

- **Timezone** – Set the timezone in which your business operates; this will display on the booking page and all bookings are created in this timezone.
- **Slot Interval** – Define time increments for time selection (e.g., 15, 30, 60 minutes). It sets how frequently slots are shown on the booking page. For e.g., a 30-minute interval will display available slots every 30 minutes.
- **Auto-confirm Bookings** – Automatically confirm all new bookings upon creation. When disabled, bookings are set to Unconfirmed by default.
- **Enable Multi-item Cart** – Allow customers to book multiple listings in one checkout.
- **Away Mode** – Temporarily disable all new online bookings.
- **Default Rental Times** – Define default rental start and end times used associated with start date and end date when the time selector is disabled.
- **Set Cancellation Link Expiry** – Turn this on to limit how close to a booking's start time customers can cancel it themselves, using the link included in their confirmation and reminder notifications. When this is off, customers can cancel any time before the booking starts.  

  - **Cancellation Link Expires** – When Set Cancellation Link Expiry is on, choose how far in advance the link should stop working — in minutes, hours, or days before the booking starts.

```
Note: Default Rental Times override Business Operating Hours, but selected business days still apply.
```

```
Note: Customers can only cancel bookings that haven't started yet (marked as Active/Completed). Once a booking is marked Active or Completed, the cancellation link no longer works, regardless of this setting.
```

---

## **Notifications**

The **Notifications** tab manages customer and staff notifications triggered by booking events. Each notification can be configured to send through **Email,****In-App, SMS or Whatsapp** channels. Use the**Ed****it (Pencil)**icon beside each type to modify the template.

#### **Notifications Include:**

- **Appointment Booked (Unconfirmed)** – Triggered when a new booking is created but not yet confirmed.
- **Appointment Booked (Confirmed)** – Triggered when a booking is confirmed.
- **Cancellation** – Notifies when a booking is canceled.
- **Reschedule** – Notifies when booking times or dates are changed.
- **Reminder** – Sends a reminder before the booking start time.
- **Follow-up** – Sends a message after booking completion.

```
Note: The notifications are triggered for booking level events and not for updates to each individual listing.
```

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155074902158/original/7MWI0d3GpjXG_uphCYQnMCfo9mEb1buldQ.png?1782886367)**

---

## **Localized Default Notification Templates**

Default notification templates use the Business Profile Platform Language across supported Email, SMS, and WhatsApp channels.

- New Rentals locations: No action required. Default templates are automatically localized.
- Existing Rentals locations: Go to Global Settings → Notifications and select Reset to default on the relevant template to load the localized version.

Customized templates remain unchanged unless manually reset.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083350697/original/rrxh_T84bET2lR4HK6yyZEbB6by6B8ZFNw.png?1792004240)

---

## **Booking Page Settings**

The **Booking Page** tab controls how your customer-facing booking site appears and behaves.

#### **General Information**

- **Company Logo & Name** – Add your company name and upload your company logo, which will be displayed on your booking page.
- **Account Slug** – Defines your booking page URL (e.g., `/rentals/your-business-name`). It is also used as the base for all your listing URLs.
- **Default Location** – Set your rental location address.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093363/original/LTyEoZz163o2e0yb0VQpPwJ-u33ldr-ZIw.png?1760558179)

#### **Page Customization**

- **Theme** – Choose between a light or dark theme for your booking page, which affects the header, footer, and widgets.
- **Language** – Select the language in which the booking page will be displayed to customers.
- **Week Starts On** – Choose the day on which the week should begin in the date picker on the booking page.
- **Primary Color:** Set the color for all actions like buttons and date selection.
- **Background Color:** Choose the color for the background of the booking page.
- **Booking Page Layout** – Decide how listings appear on your booking page — display them in a card view, a list view, or give customers the option to choose their preferred view in real time.
- **Listing Selection Button Label –** Customize the button text that appears when customers select a listing (e.g., 'View Details')
- **Final Booking Button Label –**Set the text for the final button on the booking page, where customers complete their booking(e.g., 'Book Now').
- **Insert Custom Code** – Add custom CSS to further customize the look and feel of your booking page. Simply paste your code and save to apply changes.
- **Preview Booking Page** – View a live preview of the page before saving changes.
- **Add to Booking Button Label –**Customize the text displayed on the Add to Cart button when Enable Multi-item Cart is turned on. This setting appears only when Multi-item Cart is enabled.

```
Tip: Use Preview Booking Page to test how design and layout updates look before publishing.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093429/original/P6Z-nc5oz-3YBgoHjHjuUfQcdQq5PrJXvA.png?1760558274)

#### **Forms and Consent**

- **Default Form** – Choose the form that should be displayed when booking listings. You can use the Default Form (First Name, Last Name, Phone, Email & Additional Info) or create a custom form in Sites > Forms. The form helps in collecting booker's information and create a subsequent contact in the system.
- **Sticky Contacts** – This feature remembers customer information using browser cookies. It pre-populates the booking form for returning customers. This should only be enabled when customers are filling out the form themselves. If different customers use the same browser, the information may get overwritten.
- **Consent Checkbox & Message** – Enable this to obtain customer consent during the booking process. You can customize the consent message. This is only available when using the Default Form.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093453/original/1pmbuyVCfzv5HQrU7kBcpYgaOHqQVjcXIg.png?1760558313)

#### **Confirmation Page Settings**

After a booking is made, choose to show a custom message on the default confirmation page or redirect the customer to another page.

- **Confirmation Type** – Choose between a **Thank You Message** or **Redirect URL** after booking.
- **Confirmation Header & Message** – Customize the confirmation text shown after a booking is placed successfully (applicable when the Confirmation Type is set to **Thank You Message**)

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080593638/original/yZ6inPUwOC0Csi_i6HFXIhTR7ipjN2L6sQ.png?1789041038)**

- **Let a custom form override this with its own rules:**Enable this option to let the custom form control the confirmation page experience. When enabled:
  - If the form's On Submit action is set to **Thank you message** or **Redirect URL**, that is used as the confirmation page experience.
- If the form's On Submit action is set to **Order confirmation**, or if the form has no applicable On Submit action, the confirmation page settings configured here are used as the fallback.
- The form's conditional rules — such as redirects, custom messages, and lead disqualification — also apply after booking when this is enabled.

```
Note: Show/hide field conditions from a custom form always apply during booking, regardless of this setting.
```

---

## **Payment Settings**

The **Payment** tab defines how your business handles payments, deposits, and currencies.

#### **General Payment Settings**

- **Currency** – Select the currency in which payments will be displayed and collected. This will apply to all listings. If you are changing your currency, please ensure that the corresponding pricing for each listing is updated accordingly.
- **Require Payment at Booking** – Decide if customers must pay during booking or can pay later. If disabled, no payments are collected online, however, total price is still shown to the customer.
- **Enable Security Deposits** – Toggle security deposit handling for all bookings.
- **Security Deposit Mode:**

  - **Collect Upfront** – The deposit is included in the initial booking total.
  - **Card on File Only** – Customer’s card is saved but not charged upfront for security deposit. The deposit can be charged later manually from the Edit Booking page if needed. Customers using **Card on File** must pay with a credit or debit card. Other payment methods are disabled.

```
Note: If Online payments are toggled off, Security Deposit is included in the total due upfront and must be collected at the time of rental along with the listing total.
```

```
Important: Security deposit configuration directly impacts how payments behave in the Edit Booking screen.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093908/original/qXGyqAQzyA5V8Xz6-H0fjA0HPQnJFHFghQ.png?1760559123)

#### **Payment Mode**

- Choose between **Test Mode** (for safe testing) and **Live Mode** (for actual transactions).
- Connected gateways such as **Authorize.net** or **Stripe** appear here for management.

```
Tip: Always run test bookings in Test Mode before enabling Live Mode to verify invoice accuracy and payment flow.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056093935/original/zAtV5mpNTWrs7ARc9k9sGJpEssy7IjXrtA.png?1760559176)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What does Away Mode do?**  
When activated, it prevents customers from making new bookings while keeping existing bookings unaffected.

**Q: How do I test payment setup?**  
Enable **Test Mode** under the Payments tab to simulate transactions without charging customers.

**Q: Can I redirect customers after booking?**  
Yes, under **Booking Page → Confirmation Page Settings**, you can set a custom thank-you message or redirect URL.

****Q: Do direct links for specific listings or categories reflect changes made in Global Settings?**** 

Yes. Listings and category share links are filtered views of the same booking experience, so updates to Global Settings (layout, forms, payments, notifications) apply automatically.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Understanding Listings & Categories](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006573)
- [Create & Edit Listings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006579)
- [Configuring Pricing & Discounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006611)
- [Calendar View for Rentals](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006641)
- [Overview of Bookings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006622)
- [Creating a Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006624)
- [Editing a Rental Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006626)

title_en: Snapshot Asset Dependencies
source_md:
Snapshot Asset Dependencies helps keep related assets together when you create, refresh, or load a Snapshot. HighLevel identifies the supporting assets that selected Workflows and Email Templates need, reducing the chance of transferring an automation or template without the components it references. Use this guide to understand dependency coverage, review automatically included assets, and manage dependency selection before loading a Snapshot.

```
TLDR: Creating or refreshing a Snapshot automatically includes available dependencies for supported selected assets. When loading the Snapshot, turn on Auto include dependent assets in the Assets step to select those dependencies for the load. Use View dependencies to review them before continuing.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Snapshot Asset Dependencies?](#What-Are-Snapshot-Asset-Dependencies?)
- [Key Benefits of Snapshot Asset Dependencies](#Key-Benefits-of-Snapshot-Asset-Dependencies)
- [Supported Assets and Dependencies](#Supported-Assets-and-Dependencies)
- [How Dependencies Work](#How-Dependencies-Work)
- [Dependency Controls and Indicators](#Dependency-Controls-and-Indicators)
- [How To Use Snapshot Asset Dependencies](#How-To-Use-Snapshot-Asset-Dependencies)
  - [Create a Snapshot With Dependencies](#Create-a-Snapshot-With-Dependencies)
  - [Refresh a Snapshot to Recheck Dependencies](#Refresh-a-Snapshot-to-Recheck-Dependencies)
  - [Include Dependencies When Loading a Snapshot](#Include-Dependencies-When-Loading-a-Snapshot)
  - [Review Automatically Included Assets in Version History](#Review-Automatically-Included-Assets-in-Version-History)
- [Important Notes and Limitations](#Important-Notes-and-Limitations)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What Are Snapshot Asset Dependencies?**

A dependency is an asset that another asset references or needs to function correctly. For example, a Workflow may use an Email Template, reference a Custom Field, or apply a Tag. Transferring the Workflow without its supporting assets can leave parts of the automation incomplete.

Snapshot Asset Dependencies helps address this at two points: when assets are captured in a Snapshot and when they are selected for loading into a destination sub-account.

For example, when a selected Workflow references an Email Template, HighLevel can include that template in the Snapshot automatically. During loading, enabling **Auto include dependent assets** also selects the template for the destination sub-account.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084153241/original/GqoiBye7Iy5Pj2-5xQLow_X4ucyxxCMumQ.png?1792978830)

---

## **Key Benefits of Snapshot Asset Dependencies**

Dependency handling reduces the manual work involved in transferring interconnected assets.

- **Fewer missing components:** Include supporting assets that selected Workflows and Email Templates reference.
- **Less manual selection:** Reduce the need to find and select every related field, value, tag, or template individually.
- **Clearer asset review:** Use dependency indicators and tooltips to understand why an additional asset is included.
- **More reliable reuse:** Reduce missing-dependency issues when deploying configurations across sub-accounts.

---

## **Supported Assets and Dependencies**

Automatic dependency detection initially covers **Workflows** and **Email Templates**. The asset selector identifies email builder templates under **Email Builder Templates**.

Depending on what these assets reference, their dependencies can include Email Templates, Custom Fields, Custom Values, Tags, Pipelines and pipeline stages, Custom Objects, Trigger Links, and Brand Colors.

**Important:** An asset being included as a dependency is different from that asset type having its own automatic dependency detection. For example, a Tag may be included because a selected Workflow requires it. This does not mean automatic dependency detection covers every Snapshot asset category.

---

## **How Dependencies Work**

Creating or refreshing a Snapshot determines what it contains. Loading the Snapshot determines which of those assets are transferred to a destination sub-account.

| Snapshot action | Dependency behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Create a Snapshot** | HighLevel detects and automatically includes available dependencies for supported assets you select. |
| **Refresh a Snapshot** | HighLevel checks the selected supported assets again and includes any newly required dependencies it can resolve. |
| **Load a Snapshot** | Turning on **Auto include dependent assets** automatically selects dependencies alongside the assets you choose to load. |

A dependency must be captured in the Snapshot and included in the load to be transferred through that Snapshot. Selecting a Workflow alone is not a substitute for reviewing whether its supporting assets are included.

---

## **Dependency Controls and Indicators**

The asset-selection screen and Version History provide several ways to inspect dependencies.

| Control or indicator | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto include dependent assets** | Controls automatic dependency selection during the Snapshot load. Turn it on to select dependencies with their related assets. |
| **Dependencies included** | Shows the number of dependencies included in the current load selection. |
| **Dependencies not included** | Warns that detected dependencies are not included in the current load selection. |
| **Gray checked boxes** | Identify dependencies selected automatically while automatic inclusion is enabled. |
| **Information icon** | Provides dependency details. Hover over it to see a message such as **Required by Email Builder Templates** or **Required by Email Builder Templates, Workflow**. |
| **Orange warning icon** | Identifies a dependency that has not been selected for loading. Hover over the icon to review why it is required. |
| **View dependencies** | Filters the asset list to show dependencies. A **Dependencies** filter appears above the list. |
| **Show all assets** | Returns from the dependency-filtered view to the full asset list. |
| **Auto included** | Identifies an automatically included asset in Snapshot Version History details. |

**Note:** A dependency warning during asset selection does not necessarily mean the asset is missing from the Snapshot. It can mean the asset is available but has not been selected for the current load.

---

## **How To Use Snapshot Asset Dependencies**

Use the following steps to capture dependencies, review them, and include them when loading a Snapshot.

### **Create a Snapshot With Dependencies**

1. Go to **Agency View > Account Snapshots**.
2. Click **+ Create New Snapshot**.
3. Enter a Snapshot name and select the source sub-account.
4. Select the Workflows, Email Templates, and other assets you want to capture.
5. Click **Create**.

HighLevel automatically includes available dependencies for the supported assets you selected. You do not need to find and select each of those dependencies separately.

### 

### **Refresh a Snapshot to Recheck Dependencies**

Refresh an existing Snapshot after changing its source assets so the Snapshot can capture the latest configuration and dependencies.

1. Go to **Agency View > Account Snapshots**.
2. Locate the Snapshot and click its **Refresh** icon.
3. Select the assets you want to include or update.
4. Click **Refresh**.

Each refresh rechecks the dependencies of selected supported assets. In the refresh selector, information icons beside categories such as **Workflow** and **Email Builder Templates** explain that dependent assets will be included automatically and can be reviewed in Version History.

**Important:** Changes in the source sub-account do not update the Snapshot automatically. Refreshing the Snapshot also does not, by itself, distribute those changes to destination sub-accounts. Use the applicable loading or push-update process afterward.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084153268/original/284Kn0eygx6a8NUzwqSDarWWxE9zzWuzQg.png?1792978877)

### **Include Dependencies When Loading a Snapshot**

**Step 1: Open the Snapshot load flow.**

From **Agency View > Account Snapshots**, locate your Snapshot and open **Load Updates to Sub-Account**. Select the destination sub-account or sub-accounts, then continue to the asset-selection step.

You can also start from **Agency View > Sub-Accounts**, open the destination sub-account’s three-dot menu, select **Manage Client**, and choose **Actions > Load Snapshot**. Select the Snapshot and continue.

**Step 2: Select the assets you want to load.**

In the **Assets** step, expand the relevant categories and select the Workflows or Email Templates you want to transfer.

**Step 3: Turn on Auto include dependent assets.**

Enable **Auto include dependent assets** beneath the asset list. Required dependencies are selected automatically, and the status shows how many dependencies are included.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084153275/original/VQOqD8VG9l7TaIsWWdeh6kZfPtjtF0kbBQ.png?1792978928)

**Step 4: Review the dependencies.**

Click **View dependencies** to focus the list on dependent assets. Hover over an information icon to see which asset type requires an item. Click **Show all assets** to return to the full list.

**Step 5: Review conflicts and complete the load.**

Click **Proceed to check conflicts** to review potential conflicts before loading. Review any choices to replace or retain existing destination assets, then complete the confirmation steps. Standard Snapshot conflict handling allows you to override an existing asset or skip the conflicting Snapshot asset.

The screen also provides **Proceed without conflict check**. Dependency inclusion and conflict checking are separate controls: including dependencies does not replace reviewing how the load may affect existing assets.

**Step 6: Verify the destination assets.**

After loading, inspect the transferred Workflows and Email Templates. For Workflows that send email, review the **Send Email** actions, confirm the template connections and content, and send a test email before activating the automation.

### 

### **Review Automatically Included Assets in Version History**

Version History helps you inspect what a Snapshot version contains.

1. Go to **Agency View > Account Snapshots > My Snapshots**.
2. Click the Snapshot name to open its asset viewer.
3. Open the **Version History** tab.
4. Select a version to open its details.

Look for assets marked **Auto included**. Hover over the dependency indicator to see which asset types required them. A dependency can be required by more than one asset type, such as both **Email Builder Templates** and **Workflow**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084153304/original/TQqOYDntDDvn3W1SwyD6HpHp0DDFI-AGCw.png?1792978999)

---

## **Important Notes and Limitations**

**Automatic dependency detection has limited asset-type coverage.**  
The initial coverage is Workflows and Email Templates. Review supporting assets manually for other asset types rather than assuming every relationship will be detected.

**Automatic inclusion can be disabled during loading.**  
When **Auto include dependent assets** is off, dependencies can remain unselected. Review the warning count and affected items before proceeding. Leaving a required asset out may result in an incomplete configuration in the destination.

**Unresolved dependencies are skipped.**  
If HighLevel cannot find or resolve a referenced dependency, that item is left out without blocking the remaining Snapshot processing. However, the asset that requires it may still need correction before it can function as intended.

**A successful load is not a substitute for testing.**  
Review the destination configuration before using it with live contacts. For workflow emails, verify the imported email content and template mapping rather than assuming that completing the load confirms the automation is ready.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I still need to select every related asset manually?**

For supported selected Workflows and Email Templates, available dependencies are included automatically when you create or refresh a Snapshot. During loading, turn on **Auto include dependent assets** to select those dependencies automatically.

Continue reviewing related assets for categories outside the initial dependency-detection coverage.

**Q: Why are some assets checked even though I did not select them?**

They were selected automatically because another selected asset requires them. Hover over the information icon to see the dependency explanation.

**Q: What does “dependencies not included” mean?**

It means detected dependencies are not included in your current load selection. Click **View dependencies** to inspect them, then enable **Auto include dependent assets** or review and select the required items manually.

**Q: Why does the Snapshot include more assets than I selected?**

Supported assets can reference other assets. HighLevel includes those dependencies in addition to your direct selections, so the final asset count can be higher. Review **Auto included** labels in Version History to identify the additional items.

**Q: What happens when a required dependency cannot be found?**

HighLevel skips the unresolved dependency and continues processing the remaining assets. Check the source asset’s references and correct the missing dependency before relying on the affected Workflow or Email Template.

**Q: How do I capture new dependencies in an existing Snapshot?**

Refresh the Snapshot with the relevant Workflows or Email Templates selected. The refresh rechecks their dependencies. Then review the updated Snapshot and use the appropriate load or push-update process to distribute the changes. Source-account edits do not automatically update an existing Snapshot.

**Q: Does including dependencies remove the need for conflict checking?**

No. Dependency inclusion determines which supporting assets are selected. Conflict checking helps you review whether a selected Snapshot asset should replace or be skipped in favor of an existing destination asset.

---

## **Related Articles**

- **[Creating New Snapshots in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48000982512)** — Create a Snapshot from a source sub-account and select its assets.
- **[Refresh or Update Snapshots](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48000982583)** — Capture source-account changes and prepare updated assets for distribution.
- **[Load Snapshots Into Existing Sub-Account](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48000982582)** — Load selected assets, review conflicts, and confirm the import.
- **[Load Multiple Sub-Accounts to a Snapshot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007638)**— Use the centralized load flow to select multiple destination sub-accounts.
- **[Snapshot Version Management](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006497)**— Review Snapshot versions and their asset changes.
- **[Snapshot Workflow Email Action – Enhanced Flow](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005856)** — Understand workflow-email template connections and verify transferred email actions.

title_en: AI Studio - Pricing
source_md:
AI Studio can build everything from a single landing page to complete, multi-page web experiences with forms, booking flows, and connected domains. Because each request differs in scope, the work AI Studio performs — the number of prompts, reasoning steps, generated assets, and connection actions — varies from one project to the next.

This article explains how AI Studio projects are structured, what happens during a build session, and what influences the amount of work involved, using real-world examples.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Understanding AI Studio Build Sessions](#understanding)
- [AI Studio Pricing Overview](#pricing)
- [Yoga Lead-Capture Landing Page](#ex1)
- [Image-Forward Editorial Fashion Landing Page](#ex2)
- [7-Page Travel Website with a CMS](#ex3)
- [What Affects AI Studio Usage?](#affects)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq)
- [Related Articles](#related)

---

## **Understanding AI Studio Build Sessions**

An AI Studio project consists of one or more conversational turns where the AI plans, reasons, generates content and visuals, renders a live preview, and performs supported actions such as connecting a form or calendar. Each session is measured by the work performed rather than simply the number of prompts submitted.

A typical build session may include:

- Understanding your request
- Asking follow-up questions when the request is broad
- Using a reference URL, screenshot, or uploaded images for direction
- Planning single-page or multi-page structure
- Generating layout, copy, and visuals
- Rendering a live, editable preview
- Creating a new version on each change
- Connecting supported components such as forms and calendars
- Publishing to a preview or custom domain

More complex projects — more pages, more refinements, connected components — generally involve more processing than a single-page draft.

---

## **AI Studio Pricing Overview**

AI Studio uses usage-based pricing, with included usage determined by the user's access type and AI Employee subscription. Agency users receive AI Studio usage at no additional cost, subject to fair use, while sub-account users can access AI Studio through an AI Employee subscription or pay-per-use billing.

### **AI Studio Usage by User Type and Plan**

| User Type / Plan | Included Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Agency Admins & Users ($97, $297 & $497 agency plans) | Free, subject to fair use\* |
| Sub-Account Users (without an AI Employee plan) | Not included; Pay-per-use |
| AI Employee Starter ($20/month) | Standard Usage\* |
| AI Employee Growth ($50/month) | High Usage\* |
| AI Employee Unlimited ($97/month) | Unlimited Usage\* |

```
*Fair Use Policy: Free, standard, high and unlimited usage is subject to HighLevel's Terms of Service, including excessive-use restrictions. If usage is excessive, abusive, or negatively affects platform performance, HighLevel may throttle, limit, require service upgrades, or terminate access with or without notice.
```

**Usage Limits:** AI Studio usage is measured in rolling five-hour windows, with additional usage protections. Included allowances vary by plan. When an allowance is reached, additional usage may be billed at pay-per-use rates if Extra Usage is enabled. Otherwise, access may pause until the applicable allowance resets.

**Pay-Per-Use Pricing:** AI Studio charges are based on the AI models, tokens, resources, and actions used during a session. Costs vary depending on project complexity, generated content, and the work performed.

Factors that influence AI Studio usage include:

- Number of reasoning and planning steps
- Number of pages generated
- Content and copy generation
- AI-generated images and other media
- Reference URL or image analysis
- Form and calendar connections
- Iterative refinements and version history
- Publishing and custom domain setup

```
Want to estimate your usage? Use the AI Plan Calculator to see what your included AI Studio usage looks like.
```

```
Important: AI Studio Cloud Hosting is billed separately from AI Studio generation usage. Nano hosting is free, while Micro and higher cloud tiers have additional charges, regardless of the AI Employee subscription. For additional pricing details, see AI Studio Cloud Pricing.
```

---

## **Yoga Lead-Capture Landing Page**

This example shows AI Studio building a polished single-page lead-capture site from a short prompt — generating imagery, a themed design system, and a validated lead form, then offering to connect it to the CRM.

### 

### **Overview**

AI Studio built a single-page yoga lead-capture landing page, "Sahaja," with a hero, benefits grid, class styles, weekly schedule, instructor bio, testimonials, and a validated lead form. It was themed with a sage-green palette and Fraunces/Inter typography, then prompted the user to connect the form to the CRM.

**User Request**

Create a landing page to capture leads for my yoga classes

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077342794/original/e7Er19OFNA0MLt_f69GXDpoEVlBoZHu4KQ.jpg?1785502169)

*The generated Sahaja yoga landing page with a "Find your balance" hero and free-trial call to action.*

### 

### **How AI Studio Processed the Task**

AI Studio:

- Generated sunrise yoga imagery and set up the design system in parallel
- Set up the sage-green design tokens and Fraunces/Inter fonts
- Built a shared site header and the landing page (hero, benefits, class styles, schedule, bio, testimonials)
- Built a validated lead-capture form (name, email, phone, class interest, notes) with a success state
- Verified the build was clean
- Prompted the user to connect the form to the CRM

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077342924/original/pjF6AX1hLeLP71NWpjaK8j_h2I46JcbX_g.jpeg?1785502250)

*The build session steps — generating imagery, setting up the design system, and building the page and lead form (14 tools used).*

### **What Was Built**

- Hero with sunrise yoga imagery and a free-trial call to action
- Benefits grid and four signature class styles
- Weekly schedule and instructor bio
- Student testimonials
- Validated lead-capture form (name, email, phone, class interest, notes) with a success state
- Sage-green palette with Fraunces/Inter typography

### 

### **Session Details**

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| User Messages | 1 |
| Tools Used | 14 |
| Rendering | AI-generated images, "Connect to CRM" card |
| Platform Actions | Lead form connection prompted (captured client-side pending connection) |
| Final Result | Yoga lead-capture landing page, ready to connect and publish |
| Total Session Cost | **$0.60** |

---

## **Image-Forward Editorial Fashion Landing Page**

This example shows how AI Studio builds a highly designed, animation-rich landing page from a detailed prompt — installing a dependency, generating a full set of imagery, and applying custom typography and motion.

### 

### **Overview**

AI Studio built a luxury editorial fashion landing page, "Maison Noir," with a full-bleed parallax hero, alternating image/text collection sections, a full-width masonry gallery, and smooth hover animations — all from a single detailed prompt.

**User Request**

Create a visually striking, image-forward landing page for a fashion brand. Full-bleed hero image, bold typography, parallax scroll, alternating image/text sections, a full-width gallery grid, and smooth hover animations. Premium, editorial feel with generous whitespace and a cohesive color palette.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077343007/original/Hat38FTx6l9DQ7MgwpFyfy-DCuKOLJs4WA.jpeg?1785502316)

*The generated "The Art of Undressing the Dark" editorial hero with parallax and Cormorant Garamond display type.*

### 

### **How AI Studio Processed the Task**

AI Studio:

- Chose a Noir & Gold luxury direction with Cormorant display + Karla body typography
- Installed `framer-motion` for scroll and hover animations
- Generated the full set of hero and collection imagery in parallel
- Set up design tokens with the Noir & Gold palette and editorial typography
- Built the page — hero with parallax, alternating collection sections, gallery grid, and footer
- Created and iteratively refined the page files

### **What Was Built**

- Full-bleed parallax hero with scroll-driven image scaling and a fading headline
- Bold Cormorant Garamond display typography paired with Karla body text
- Noir & Gold palette via semantic design tokens in `src/index.css`
- Three alternating image/text collection sections with parallax image drift and hover zoom
- Full-width masonry gallery grid with hover-reveal captions and staggered entrance animations

### 

### **Session Details**

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| User Messages | 1 |
| Tools Used | 29 |
| Dependencies | framer-motion installed |
| Rendering | Multiple AI-generated images, parallax and hover animations |
| Final Result | Luxury editorial fashion landing page, ready to publish |
| Total Session Cost | **$1.30** |

---

## **7-Page Travel Website with a CMS**

This example shows AI Studio building a larger, multi-page site with editable content collections, a contact form, and shared navigation — the kind of structured project that involves the most planning and page generation.

### 

### **Overview**

AI Studio built a complete 7-page website, "Bharat Voyages," for a travel business in India — with shared nav and footer, a CMS for blog posts and tours, responsive design, SEO metadata, and a contact form ready to connect to the CRM.

**User Request**

Build a 7-page website with a CMS for a travel business in India. Home, About, Services, Blog (CMS collection), Portfolio/Projects (CMS collection), Pricing, and Contact (with form). Shared nav and footer, responsive design, editable content collections for blog posts and projects, and SEO-friendly structure.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077343183/original/NXEg8jyi0wUyRdWsHbs2qiUo42hpkdcLEA.jpeg?1785502362)

*The generated Bharat Voyages home page with shared nav, hero, and stats band — plus the "Connect to CRM" prompt for the contact form.*

### **How AI Studio Processed the Task**

AI Studio:

- Planned a 7-page structure with shared navigation and footer
- Generated content and imagery across the pages
- Built editable CMS content collections for blog posts and tours
- Applied responsive design and SEO metadata
- Built a contact form and prompted to connect it to the CRM

### 

### **Pages Created**

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Hero, highlights, and primary calls to action |
| About | Company story and credibility |
| Services | Overview of travel offerings |
| Blog | Editable CMS collection of posts |
| Portfolio / Projects | Editable CMS collection of tours |
| Pricing | Package and pricing details |
| Contact | Contact form (connectable to CRM) |

### 

### **Session Details**

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| User Messages | 1 |
| Tools Used | 40 |
| Output | 7-page site with CMS collections and contact form |
| Rendering | Generated content and imagery, "Connect to CRM" card |
| Platform Actions | Contact form connection prompted |
| Final Result | Complete 7-page travel website, ready to publish |
| Total Session Cost | **$1.10** |

---

## **What Affects AI Studio Usage?**

AI Studio usage is based on the work performed during a session rather than the number of prompts alone. Sessions become more resource-intensive as additional reasoning, generation, or connection actions are required. Factors that increase overall work include:

- Multi-page structures and larger projects
- Follow-up questions and multiple refinements
- AI-generated images and other media
- Reference URL and image analysis
- Form and calendar connections
- Custom domain setup and publishing
- Version history from repeated changes

Based on the examples above:

- **AI-generated imagery** is often the largest single driver — image-heavy pages can cost more than sites with more pages but less generated media.
- **Page count alone** is not a reliable predictor of cost; a structured 7-page site can cost less than a single image-forward landing page.
- **Text, layout, and CMS structure** generally involve less processing than generating visuals.

---

## **AI Studio Usage and Spending Notifications**

AI Studio displays usage notification banners to help users monitor consumption and spending before they reach their limits. These banners are enabled automatically for users who have access to AI Studio, so no additional setup is required.

### 

### **Subscription Usage Notifications**

Subscription users receive notifications as their AI Studio usage increases:

- **70% usage:** Usage alert
- **85% usage:** Warning
- **Approaching or reaching 100%:** Critical and usage exhaustion notifications

Depending on billing permissions, the banner can provide actions to adjust usage limits or request an increase from the Agency Admin.

### **Pay-Per-Use Spending Notifications**

Pay-per-use users receive a spending notification for every **$50 spent on AI Studio**. These notifications help users monitor ongoing usage and costs as spending increases.

For detailed information about configuring spending limits, requesting additional usage, and managing limit-increase requests, see [AI Usage Limits.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007813)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How much does AI Studio cost?**

AI Studio is included at no additional cost for agency users on all HighLevel agency plans, subject to fair use. Sub-account users can access AI Studio through an AI Employee Starter ($20/month), Growth ($50/month), or Unlimited ($97/month) subscription, or through pay-per-use billing. The Starter plan is available exclusively to agencies on the $497/month plan.

**Q: Does every prompt do the same amount of work?**

No. The work varies with the complexity of the request — the number of pages, refinements, generated assets, and connection actions involved.

**Q: Does image generation involve more work than text?**

Generally, yes. Generating images or other visual assets typically requires more processing than generating text alone.

**Q: Are forms and calendars connected automatically?**

No. AI Studio builds the form or booking layout first, then connects it after you ask it to or click Connect. Submissions and bookings flow into your sub-account only after that step.

**Q: Can AI Studio recreate a site exactly from a URL?**

A reference URL or image should be treated as inspiration for structure, layout, and style rather than an exact one-to-one copy.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [AI Studio in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007587-ai-studio-in-highlevel)
- [Connect Forms and Calendars in AI Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007599-connect-forms-and-calendars-in-ai-studio)
- [Code Editor in AI Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007652-code-editor-in-ai-studio)
- [Advanced SEO Support in AI Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007691-advanced-seo-support-in-ai-studio)
- [AI Studio Cloud Pricing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000009207)

title_en: Global Search V2
source_md:
Platform Navigation

# Global Search V2

Search across every product, page, and record in HighLevel from a single unified interface with keyboard shortcuts, voice commands, and lightning-fast backend performance.

What You'll Learn

Global Search V2 provides a unified search experience across HighLevel, indexing 530+ platform routes and 8 core products including contacts, opportunities, calendars, workflows, and more. With backend-powered search, keyboard-first navigation, and voice command support, you can find any record or page in seconds without hunting through nested menus.

This article covers the key features of Global Search V2, how to enable and use the search interface, available search modes and shortcuts, and answers common questions about product coverage and performance.

Labs Feature

Global Search V2 is available under HighLevel Labs. Enable it under **Labs > Subaccounts > "Global Search V2"** to access the feature. Labs features are early-access capabilities that may receive updates based on user feedback.

## What is Global Search V2?

Global Search V2 is a unified search interface that allows you to find any record, page, or route in HighLevel from a single entry point. It indexes 530+ platform routes across both agency and location levels, and searches across 8 core products including contacts, opportunities, products, calendars, funnels, workflows, social planner, and conversations.

The search runs on the backend with parallel product queries, enforcing access control based on user roles, assigned-data-only permissions, feature flags, and deprecated features. This eliminates client-side latency and provides a lightning-fast search experience similar to Mac Spotlight or Windows Search.

Global Search V2 replaces the need to hunt through nested menus or remember where specific features are located. Access it instantly from the search bar in the left sidebar or press **Cmd/Ctrl + K** from anywhere in HighLevel to start searching.

When Global Search does not find a matching result, users with Ask AI access can send the same query to Ask AI without starting over. The first Ask AI response appears inside Global Search, and users can continue the interaction in Ask AI when they need a more detailed conversation.

## Key Benefits

Global Search V2 transforms platform navigation from a time-consuming process into an instant action. The unified search interface reduces friction, eliminates confusion about feature locations, and scales performance as the product catalog grows.

**Universal Platform Coverage** — Search across 530+ routes and 8 products from a single interface, with more products being onboarded continuously to provide complete platform coverage.

**Backend-Powered Speed** — Server-side search runs product queries in parallel with no client-side latency stacking, delivering results in a single round trip regardless of how many products are searched.

**Smart Fuzzy Matching** — Spelling mistakes are handled automatically, and typing a section name surfaces every sub-page under it without requiring exact text matches.

**Permission-Aware Results** — Search results are automatically filtered by user roles, assigned-data-only permissions, feature flags, and deprecated features, ensuring you only see what you have access to.

**Keyboard-First Navigation** — Full arrow-key and Enter navigation, Cmd/Ctrl+K to open, and Cmd/Ctrl+1..9 to switch search scopes provide a fast, hands-on-keyboard workflow.

**Voice Command Support** — Use voice dictation with commands like "open", "tab", and shortcuts for hands-free navigation and accessibility.

## The Search Interface

The Global Search V2 interface opens as a centered modal overlay with a clean, focused design. The search bar appears at the top with four action icons, followed by product filter pills and grouped results below.

Component 1

Search Bar and Action Icons

The search bar displays dynamic placeholder text based on your selected filter, such as "Search", "Search for Conversations...", or "Search apps...". Four action icons appear to the right of the search input: a microphone icon for voice commands, a magnifying glass for standard search, a navigation/routes icon, and a help icon for assistance.

Component 2

Product Filter Pills

Below the search bar, a row of pill-shaped filters displays your search scope options. The "All" pill searches across all products and routes, while individual product pills (Contacts, Opportunities, Products, Calendars, Funnels, Workflows, Social Planner, Conversations) narrow results to specific product types. The active filter is highlighted in blue.

Component 3

Grouped Search Results

Results appear in grouped sections such as PAGES, CONTACTS, PRODUCTS, FUNNELS, with result counts displayed next to each section header (e.g., "PAGES 3", "FUNNELS 5"). Each result shows the record or page name, breadcrumb navigation path, and relevant metadata. A "See all" link appears for sections with more results than displayed.

Component 4

Search Apps View

When you click into the search bar without typing, a "Search apps..." view appears showing all 8 product icons in a grid layout: Contacts, Opportunities, Products, Calendars, Funnels, Workflows, Social Planner, and Conversations. Click any icon to filter your search to that specific product.

Component 5

Keyboard Shortcuts Footer

At the bottom of the search modal, a keyboard shortcuts reference displays available commands: Navigate (arrow keys), Tab, Switch tab (Cmd/Ctrl+number), Open (Enter), and ESC to Dismiss. The label "Global Search" appears in the bottom right corner.

**COMPONENT 6**

**Ask AI No-Results Experience**

When Global Search does not find a matching result, users with Ask AI access can send their existing search query directly to Ask AI. This provides a path forward when the information cannot be found as a Global Search result.

Select the Ask AI option to send the current query to Ask AI. The first response appears directly inside the Global Search modal, allowing you to review the answer without leaving your search.

If you need to continue the conversation, select Continue in Ask AI\*\*. The query and conversation context carry into the full Ask AI experience so you can continue without starting again.

Access Point

Global Search V2 is triggered from the search bar located in the left sidebar of HighLevel, displaying the keyboard shortcut "⌘K" next to it. Click the search bar or press Cmd/Ctrl+K from anywhere in the platform to open the search interface instantly.

## Search Modes and Filters

Global Search V2 provides multiple search modes to match different workflows. You can perform a global search across all products and routes, narrow the scope to a single product, or focus on navigation-only searches.

Mode 1

All Scope

The default "All" mode searches across every enabled product and all platform routes simultaneously. This provides a comprehensive sweep of HighLevel, returning both records (contacts, opportunities, funnels, etc.) and navigation pages that match your query. Results are grouped by category with counts displayed.

Mode 2

Product-Specific Filters

Click any of the 8 product filter pills (Contacts, Opportunities, Products, Calendars, Funnels, Workflows, Social Planner, Conversations) to narrow your search to that specific product. The search bar placeholder updates to reflect your selection, such as "Search for Conversations..." when the Conversations filter is active. This mode is useful when you know the product type but not the specific record.

Mode 3

Search Apps View

When you first open Global Search or clear your query, the interface displays a "Search apps..." view with all 8 product icons arranged in a grid. Click any icon to instantly filter your search to that product category, making it easy to browse by product type before entering specific search terms.

Switching Modes

Use keyboard shortcuts Cmd/Ctrl+1 through Cmd/Ctrl+9 to switch between search scopes quickly without leaving the search interface. The active filter pill is highlighted in blue, and the search placeholder text updates to match your selection.

## Keyboard Shortcuts and Voice Commands

Global Search V2 is designed for keyboard-first navigation with full arrow-key and Enter support, plus voice command capabilities for accessibility and hands-free workflows. A keyboard shortcuts reference is displayed at the bottom of the search interface for quick reference.

Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Cmd/Ctrl + K | Open Global Search from anywhere in HighLevel |
| Arrow Keys | Navigate up and down through search results |
| Enter | Select the highlighted result and navigate to that page or record |
| Tab | Move between search interface elements |
| Cmd/Ctrl + 1..9 | Switch between search scopes (All, specific Apps, Navigation) |
| Esc | Close the Global Search interface |

Voice Commands

Global Search V2 supports voice dictation with command shortcuts for hands-free navigation. Click the microphone icon in the search bar to activate voice commands:

**"open [page name]"** — Navigate directly to a platform page by voice

**"tab [product name]"** — Switch to a specific product filter using voice

**Command Shortcuts** — Use voice to trigger keyboard shortcuts for faster navigation

Accessibility

Global Search V2 includes screen-reader announcements for state changes and command execution, ensuring full accessibility for users who rely on assistive technologies. The keyboard shortcuts footer provides a persistent visual reference for available commands.

Speed and Scale

Backend-Powered Performance

Global Search V2 eliminates client-side latency with parallel backend queries, debounced typing, and cancellable requests — delivering results in a single round trip no matter how many products are searched.

## How to Enable and Use Global Search V2

Global Search V2 is available under HighLevel Labs. Once enabled, you can invoke the search interface using the keyboard shortcut, clicking the search bar in the left sidebar, or using voice commands.

Enabling Global Search V2

Step 1

Navigate to Labs Settings and Enable Global Search V2

From your HighLevel account, go to **Labs > Subaccounts** to access the Labs feature settings. Locate **"Global Search V2"** in the Labs features list and toggle it to the enabled position. Changes take effect immediately.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077348979/original/DxdifN9pOtd1kHs1pZFnusGZar9SEC-q3g.png?1785504987)

Step 2

Access the Search Interface

Click the search bar in the left sidebar (next to the ⌘K shortcut label), or press **Cmd/Ctrl + K** from anywhere in HighLevel at the subaccount level to open the Global Search interface.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077349407/original/xtdqDDgsUbqN1B5tQUXBd0kZEY1Jzy_ubw.png?1785505175)

Using Global Search V2

Step 3

Enter Your Search Query

Type the name of a contact, opportunity, page, or feature you want to find. Global Search uses fuzzy matching, so spelling mistakes are automatically handled. You can also click the microphone icon to use voice commands.

Step 4

Review and Navigate Results

Results appear grouped by type (PAGES, CONTACTS, PRODUCTS, FUNNELS, etc.) with result counts displayed. Use arrow keys to navigate through results, and press **Enter** to open the selected item. Results are automatically filtered by your permissions and access level.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077349532/original/8BZXenuDkuRTJihHEtsCyg2dAOcmuhXwGw.png?1785505243)

Step 5

Filter by Product or Browse Apps

Click any of the product filter pills to narrow results to a single product (Contacts, Opportunities, Calendars, etc.), or click the search bar without typing to view the "Search apps..." grid showing all 8 product icons. Press **Cmd/Ctrl + 1..9** to switch scopes quickly using keyboard shortcuts.

Tip

If you type a section name (e.g., "Settings"), Global Search automatically surfaces all sub-pages under that section, making it easy to discover nested features without navigating through multiple menu levels. Breadcrumb paths show the full navigation hierarchy for each result.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Which products are currently included in Global Search V2?

Global Search V2 currently searches across 8 core products: contacts, opportunities, products, calendars, funnels, workflows, social planner, and conversations. Additional HighLevel products are being onboarded continuously to provide complete platform coverage.

Q: How do I enable Global Search V2?

Navigate to **Labs > Subaccounts** and enable the **"Global Search V2"** feature. Once enabled, click the search bar in the left sidebar (next to the ⌘K label) or press **Cmd/Ctrl + K** from anywhere at the subaccount level to access the search interface.

Q: Does Global Search V2 respect user permissions and role-based access?

Yes. Global Search enforces access control on the backend, filtering results by user roles, assigned-data-only permissions, feature flags, and deprecated features. You will only see records and pages you have permission to access.

Q: Can I search for platform pages as well as data records?

Yes. Global Search V2 indexes 530+ sidebar routes covering both agency and location levels, plus data records from 8 products. You can search for any navigable page in HighLevel, and results display with breadcrumb navigation paths showing the full menu hierarchy.

Q: What keyboard shortcuts are available in Global Search V2?

Press **Cmd/Ctrl + K** to open Global Search. Use arrow keys to navigate results and **Enter** to select. Press **Cmd/Ctrl + 1..9** to switch search scopes, **Tab** to move between elements, and **Esc** to close the search interface. A keyboard shortcuts reference is displayed at the bottom of the search modal.

Q: Does Global Search V2 handle spelling mistakes?

Yes. Global Search uses fuzzy matching to handle spelling mistakes automatically. You don't need to type exact names or routes — the search will return relevant results even with approximate text.

Q: Can I filter search results to a single product?

Yes. Click any of the product filter pills (Contacts, Opportunities, Calendars, Funnels, Workflows, Social Planner, Products, Conversations) to narrow results to that specific product. You can also view all product icons in a grid by clicking the search bar, or use **Cmd/Ctrl + number** shortcuts to switch filters quickly.

Q: Are voice commands supported in Global Search V2?

Yes. Global Search V2 supports voice dictation with commands like "open [page name]" and "tab [product name]" for hands-free navigation. Click the microphone icon in the search bar to activate voice commands. Screen-reader announcements are also included for accessibility.

Q: Where is the Global Search trigger located?

The Global Search trigger is located in the left sidebar of HighLevel, displaying as a search bar with the keyboard shortcut "⌘K" next to it. Click the search bar or press **Cmd/Ctrl + K** from anywhere in the platform to open the search interface instantly.

title_en: Redirection links in Countdown Timer
source_md:
Countdown Timer redirection links help you control where contacts go based on whether a timer is still active or has expired. By combining Active and Expired Links with a timer's redirection link, you can keep buttons, images, and other calls-to-action aligned with the offer's current availability. This is useful for limited-time offers, registration deadlines, appointment promotions, and other campaigns where access should change automatically after expiration.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Countdown Timer Redirection Links?](#What-are-Countdown-Timer-Redirection-Links?)
- [Key Benefits of Countdown Timer Redirection Links](#Key-Benefits-of-Countdown-Timer-Redirection-Links)
- [How Active, Expired, and Redirection Links Work](#How-Active,-Expired,-and-Redirection-Links-Work)
- [Copy Link, Redirection Link, and Copy Code](#Copy-Link,-Redirection-Link,-and-Copy-Code)
- [Where You Can Use Redirection Links](#Where-You-Can-Use-Redirection-Links)
- [Using Redirection Links with Dynamic Countdown Timers](#Using-Redirection-Links-with-Dynamic-Countdown-Timers)
- [Using Redirection Links with Recurring Countdown Timers](#Using-Redirection-Links-with-Recurring-Countdown-Timers)
- [How to Set Up Countdown Timer Redirection](#How-to-Set-Up-Countdown-Timer-Redirection)
- [Testing Countdown Timer Redirection](#Testing-Countdown-Timer-Redirection)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are Countdown Timer Redirection Links?**

Countdown Timer Redirection Links provide a conditional destination based on the current state of a countdown. Instead of manually changing campaign links after an offer expires, HighLevel can evaluate the timer and route the contact to the appropriate Active or Expired destination.

Three link concepts work together:

- **Active Link:** The destination contacts should reach while the countdown is still active.
- **Expired Link:** The destination contacts should reach after the timer has expired.
- **Redirection Link:** The conditional link that checks the timer's current state and sends the contact to either the Active or Expired Link.

For example, a promotional email can use a Redirection Link on its **Claim Offer** button. While the timer is active, the button sends the contact to the offer page. After expiration, the same button can route the contact to an expired-offer or waitlist page.

---

## **Key Benefits of Countdown Timer Redirection Links**

Redirection Links help keep campaign destinations aligned with countdown availability without requiring you to manually replace links when a timer expires.

- **Automatic routing:** Contacts are directed to the appropriate destination based on whether the timer is active or expired.
- **Consistent campaign experience:** Buttons, images, and text links can follow the same availability rules as the countdown.
- **Reduced manual updates:** The same Redirection Link can continue working before and after expiration without manually replacing the CTA URL.
- **Better expiration handling:** Contacts who interact after the deadline can be sent to a waitlist, expired-offer page, alternate promotion, or another relevant destination.
- **Flexible placement:** Redirection Links can be used with supported calls-to-action where timer-aware routing is needed.

---

## **How Active, Expired, and Redirection Links Work**

Active and Expired Links define the destinations associated with the timer, while the Redirection Link determines which destination a contact should reach. Understanding this relationship helps prevent contacts from reaching expired offers through campaign CTAs.

**Active Link**

The **Active Link** is the destination used while the countdown is still running.

Common Active Link destinations include:

- Limited-time offer pages
- Registration pages
- Checkout pages
- Booking pages
- Promotional funnel steps

For example, if a registration offer closes at the end of the timer, the Active Link could point to the registration page.

**Expired Link**

The **Expired Link** is the destination used after the countdown has reached its expiration state.

Common Expired Link destinations include:

- Offer expired pages
- Waitlist pages
- Alternate promotion pages
- General information pages
- Next-event registration pages

Using an Expired Link prevents contacts who return after the deadline from being directed to an offer that is no longer available.

**Redirection Link**

The **Redirection Link** acts as the conditional URL between the contact and your configured destinations.

When a contact clicks the Redirection Link:

1. HighLevel checks the associated timer state.
2. If the timer is active, the contact is routed to the Active Link.
3. If the timer has expired, the contact is routed to the Expired Link.

The Redirection Link itself can remain the same even though the final destination changes based on the timer state.

---

## **Copy Link, Redirection Link, and Copy Code**

HighLevel provides several timer-related sharing options that serve different purposes. Choosing the correct option depends on whether you want to control navigation or display the countdown itself.

**Redirection Link**

Use a Redirection Link when a button, image, or text CTA should send contacts to different destinations depending on the timer's current state.

Examples include:

- A **Claim Offer** button in an email
- A linked promotional image
- A text link such as **Register Now**
- A CTA associated with a time-sensitive campaign

**Copy Link**

Depending on the timer type and where the timer is being used, HighLevel may provide a link action associated with the timer.

The available link options can vary by timer type and placement. When working with a Dynamic Timer inside an email, use the timer settings available in the Email Builder to obtain the appropriate redirection link.

**Copy Code**

**Copy Code** is used to embed or display the countdown timer itself on supported external websites or platforms.

Copy Code and Redirection Links serve different purposes:

- **Copy Code:** Displays the countdown.
- **Redirection Link:** Controls where contacts go when they click a CTA based on the countdown state.

Dynamic Timers can require additional implementation values when embedded outside HighLevel. Refer to the dedicated Copy Code documentation before implementing them externally.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082137513/original/aq0KDhx0jMMLgxY5oqkkYZO6kmJaHN5JVA.png?1790700493)

---

## **Where You Can Use Redirection Links**

Redirection Links are most useful anywhere a call-to-action should respect the same deadline as the associated countdown. The implementation can differ depending on whether the timer is being used in an email, funnel, website, or another supported channel.

**Emails**

Redirection Links can be applied to email calls-to-action such as:

- Buttons
- Images
- Linked text

A common workflow is to place a countdown timer in the email and use the timer's Redirection Link on the primary CTA.

For example:

- Timer active → **Shop Now** sends the contact to the sale page.
- Timer expired → the same **Shop Now** button sends the contact to an expired-offer page.

**Funnels and Websites**

Funnels and websites can use Countdown Timer elements directly on the page. Timer expiration behavior can then be configured as part of the page experience.

When coordinating an email and destination page, use the same timer configuration where supported so the deadline shown in the email and on the destination page remains aligned.

The timer displayed on the page and a CTA Redirection Link serve related but different purposes:

- The **timer** displays or tracks the countdown state.
- The **Redirection Link** determines the appropriate destination when a contact clicks a linked CTA.

For complete page-specific configuration, refer to the Countdown Timers in Funnels documentation.

**External Platforms**

If a countdown needs to be displayed outside HighLevel, use the timer's **Copy Code** feature where supported.

If the external campaign also needs timer-aware CTA routing, make sure the appropriate Redirection Link is used separately from the embed code.

---

## **Using Redirection Links with Dynamic Countdown Timers**

Dynamic Timers create contact-specific countdown experiences, so their link behavior must remain associated with the individual timer state. This is especially important when the timer starts based on an email interaction.

When using a Dynamic Timer in an email:

1. Add the Dynamic Timer to the email.
2. Open the timer settings in the Email Builder.
3. Copy the available Redirection Link.
4. Apply that link to the appropriate button, image, or text CTA.
5. Test the active and expired destinations before sending the campaign.

Dynamic Timer Redirection Links should not be confused with the **Copy Code** option used to embed Dynamic Timers externally.

---

## **Using Redirection Links with Recurring Countdown Timers**

Recurring Timers can cycle between active countdown periods and wait periods. This creates additional expiration behavior that should be considered when configuring destinations and testing campaign links.

During a Recurring Timer's wait state, contacts may be treated as being in an expired state until the next countdown cycle begins.

For this reason:

- Configure an appropriate Expired Link.
- Test the timer during both active and wait states.
- Confirm that contacts are routed to the expected destination before using the campaign publicly.

For complete wait-state behavior, refer to the dedicated Recurring [Timer Wait Time documentation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005838).

---

## **How to Set Up Countdown Timer Redirection**

Proper setup ensures that campaign CTAs continue to lead contacts to the correct destination both before and after the countdown expires. Configure both destination states and test the generated Redirection Link before launching the campaign.

1. Navigate to **Marketing > Countdown Timers**.
2. Create a new timer or open an existing timer.
3. Configure the timer type, duration, expiration behavior, and other applicable timer settings.
4. Enter the **Active Link**.

   Use the URL contacts should access while the timer remains active.

   Example:  
     
   `https://yourdomain.com/offer`
5. Enter the **Expired Link**.

   Use the URL contacts should access after the timer expires.

   Example:  
     
   `https://yourdomain.com/offer-expired`  
     
   `![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082137544/original/M4DzLcLJNz2lbzJU7LLFGrsA8cWb4hCJRQ.png?1790700536)`
6. Save the timer.
7. Add the timer to the appropriate email, funnel, website, or supported campaign.
8. Copy the timer's available **Redirection Link** from the appropriate timer or builder settings.
9. Apply the Redirection Link to the relevant CTA.

   This may include:

   - Button
   - Image
   - Text link
   - Other supported clickable elements
10. Test the CTA while the timer is active.

    Confirm that it routes to the Active Link.
11. Test the expired state.

    Confirm that the same CTA routes to the Expired Link after the countdown expires.

---

## **Testing Countdown Timer Redirection**

Testing both timer states helps prevent contacts from reaching unavailable offers or incorrect destination pages. A timer that displays correctly can still create a poor campaign experience if its associated Active or Expired destination is misconfigured.

Before publishing or sending a campaign, verify:

- The Active Link opens the intended live offer or destination.
- The Expired Link opens the correct post-expiration destination.
- The Redirection Link is used on the intended CTA.
- Buttons, images, and text links using the Redirection Link route correctly.
- The timer and destination page use consistent expiration behavior.
- Dynamic Timer behavior is tested with the intended trigger.
- Recurring Timer behavior is tested during both active and wait states.
- External implementations use Copy Code separately from Redirection Link configuration where applicable.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

### 

**Q: What is the difference between an Active Link and a Redirection Link?**

The Active Link is the destination contacts reach while the timer is active. The Redirection Link is the conditional URL contacts click. HighLevel checks the timer state and sends the contact to either the Active or Expired Link.

**Q: Does the Redirection Link change after the timer expires?**

The Redirection Link can remain the same. The destination it routes the contact to changes according to whether the associated timer is active or expired.

**Q: Can I use the same Redirection Link on multiple CTAs?**

Yes, the same Redirection Link can be used on multiple supported CTAs when those elements should follow the same timer state and destination rules.

**Q: Can I use a Redirection Link with a Dynamic Timer?**

Yes. When using a Dynamic Timer in an email, obtain the available Redirection Link through the timer settings in the Email Builder and apply it to the relevant CTA.

**Q: Is Copy Code the same as a Redirection Link?**

No. Copy Code is used to display or embed the countdown timer itself. A Redirection Link is used to route contacts to the Active or Expired destination based on the timer state.

**Q: What happens if a contact clicks after the timer expires?**

If the Expired Link is properly configured and the CTA uses the timer's Redirection Link, the contact is routed to the Expired destination.

**Q: What should I use as an Expired Link?**

Use a destination that remains useful after the original offer closes. Common examples include an expired-offer page, waitlist, alternate promotion, or upcoming-event page.

**Q: Do Recurring Timers behave differently after expiration?**

Recurring Timers can enter a wait state between countdown cycles. During that period, expired-state behavior may apply until the next active cycle begins.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started with Countdown Timer](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003100-getting-started-with-countdown-timer)
- [Using Countdown Timers in Emails](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003101-how-to-use-countdown-timer-in-emails-)
- [Sync Your Countdown Timer in Email and Funnels](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003102-sync-your-countdown-timer-in-email-and-funnels)
- [How to Use the Copy Code Feature in Countdown Timers](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003103-how-to-use-the-copy-code-feature-in-countdown-timers)
- [How to Use Countdown Timers in Funnels](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003122-how-to-use-countdown-timers-in-funnels-)
- [Guide: Dynamic Countdown Timer](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004385-guide-dynamic-countdown-timer)
