A Snapshot Share Link opens the recipient import experience directly. Sign in to the agency where you want the Snapshot stored before opening the link.

1. Sign in to the HighLevel agency where you want to import the Snapshot.
2. Open the **Snapshot Share Link** provided by the sender. You can paste it into a new browser tab if needed.
3. Review the Snapshot import pop-up.
4. Enter a custom Snapshot name if you want to rename it before importing.
5. Click **Import Now**.
6. Watch for the Snapshot to appear in your imported Snapshots list.
7. Wait until the greyed-out processing state clears and the Snapshot becomes available.

![Snapshot import pop-up with Snapshot naming and Import Now controls](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071794433/original/_TcGehhSTyMP6Ce-mnS7Gm1xlFcvh810Cg.png?1779279980)
![Imported Snapshots list showing a Snapshot in the greyed-out processing state](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071794510/original/Z9STIZhBAXLpIBgqwIVB63VfusmnL5cfJA.png?1779280031)

Method 2

### Import a Snapshot from Email

An email invitation launches the same general import experience while delivering access directly to the intended recipient.

1. Sign in to the HighLevel agency where the Snapshot should be imported.
2. Open the Snapshot invitation email.
3. Click the Snapshot import link in the email.
4. Review the Snapshot import pop-up.
5. Rename the Snapshot if needed.
6. Click **Import**.
7. Wait for processing to finish before loading the Snapshot into a sub-account.

![Snapshot invitation email containing a Snapshot import link](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071822070/original/V0Yo8P0R7BTka8EfVImswQPqqWpa1Bnrzg.png?1779290724)

## Load the Imported Snapshot Into a Sub-Account

An imported Snapshot remains at the agency level until you deliberately load it into a sub-account. Loading gives you control over the destination, selected assets, and any conflicts with assets that already exist in the sub-account.

**Protected assets can be loaded internally:** If the imported Snapshot contains protected assets, those assets can be selected and loaded into sub-accounts within the same agency. Loading them does not remove their protection.

Step 1

Open the Destination Sub-Account

From **Agency View**, locate the sub-account where you want to load the Snapshot. Open the sub-account action menu and select **Manage Client**.

![Agency sub-account list showing the action menu for the destination sub-account](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080791240/original/ZH-0zrpdbvaNafkINQVtWru29MUT0ktZeg.png?1789246310)
![Sub-account action menu showing Manage Client](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071796844/original/s8mSERi6DDizLkg3Bb_c9X-67e3Oy6jFuA.png?1779280978)

Step 2

Select Load Snapshot

Click **Actions**, then select **Load Snapshot**.

![Actions menu showing the Load Snapshot option](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071797037/original/BhMgfjVjco6zQqf4Zmdcl2hGkKTScz0-hg.png?1779281048)

Step 3

Choose the Imported Snapshot

Select the Snapshot you imported from the available Snapshot list.

![Load Snapshot dialog showing the Snapshot selection field](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071797198/original/ZwO0VK7C06xezVfe93oI1CdtJNxIBs5tOA.png?1779281121)

Step 4

Select the Assets to Load

Select the supported Snapshot assets you want to apply to the destination sub-account.

![Snapshot asset selection screen for loading assets into a sub-account](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080791243/original/_CgHPFYFJIYjDv0n00plhjAMGv59oQ4heA.png?1789246325)

Step 5

Review Conflicts and Confirm the Load

Review any detected conflicts and choose the appropriate action for existing assets. When everything is correct, confirm the Snapshot load.

![Snapshot load confirmation screen after asset and conflict review](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155071797395/original/QFEwFaHZw2zXaPahOxnbeAk_FhbaeYlPmQ.png?1779281235)

For additional details about selecting assets and resolving conflicts, see [Load Snapshots Into Existing Sub-Account](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982582-load-snapshots-into-existing-sub-account).

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I rename a Snapshot while importing it?

Yes. The import pop-up lets you enter a custom Snapshot name before completing the import.

Q: Why is my imported Snapshot greyed out?

The Snapshot is still processing. Wait for it to become active instead of starting another import or trying to load it immediately.

Q: What does the shield icon mean?

The shield indicates that the Snapshot contains protected assets. Those assets can be imported, loaded, and reused within your agency, but their protected status remains attached and restricts external redistribution.

Q: Can I load imported protected assets into more than one sub-account?

Yes. Protected assets can be reused across sub-accounts within the same receiving agency. Their protected status remains attached.

Q: Can I create or refresh another Snapshot using imported protected assets?

Yes. Protected assets can be included in internal Create and Refresh workflows within your agency. Reusing them does not remove their protection.

Q: Can I share imported protected assets with another agency?

No. Protected assets remain restricted when they would leave your agency. If a mixed Snapshot is shared externally, protected assets are excluded while eligible non-protected assets can continue.

Q: What should I do if my Snapshot Share Link has expired?

Request a new Snapshot Share Link from the person or agency that originally shared the Snapshot.

Q: Does importing a Snapshot automatically load it into a sub-account?

No. Importing stores the Snapshot in your agency library. You must separately load it into the intended sub-account before its selected assets are applied.

title_en: How to Manage Feature Permissions for Subaccounts
source_md:
Feature Permissions let agencies control which HighLevel tools and features their clients can see and use. The updated permission experience includes more than 80 controllable features and organizes them into clear groups, making it easier to find and manage access. Agencies can manage permissions for an individual subaccount or include them in SaaS plans.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Feature Permissions?](#What-are-Feature-Permissions?)
- [Key Benefits of Feature Permissions](#Key-Benefits-of-Feature-Permissions)
- [How Feature Permissions are Organized](#How-Feature-Permissions-are-Organized)
- [Understanding the Selected Feature Counts](#Understanding-the-Selected-Feature-Counts)
- [Search for a Feature](#Search-for-a-Feature)
- [Feature Permissions for Individual Subaccounts](#Feature-Permissions-for-Individual-Subaccounts)
- [Feature Permissions for SaaS Plans](#Feature-Permissions-for-SaaS-Plans)
- [Feature Permissions vs. User Permissions](#Feature-Permissions-vs.-User-Permissions)
- [What Happened to Existing Permissions?](#What-Happened-to-Existing-Permissions?)
- [How To Manage Feature Permissions](#How-To-Manage-Feature-Permissions)
- [Troubleshooting Feature Permissions](#Troubleshooting-Feature-Permissions)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are Feature Permissions?**

Feature Permissions control which parts of HighLevel are available inside a subaccount. They help agencies create a cleaner client experience by showing only the tools each client should have access to.

For example, an agency may want one client to use:

- AI Agents
- Calendars
- Opportunities
- Phone System

while another client may need a different set of features.

Instead of showing every HighLevel feature to every client, Feature Permissions let the agency choose what each subaccount can access.

The updated system includes **80+ controllable features**, compared with the smaller set of controls previously available.

---

## **Key Benefits of Feature Permissions**

The updated Feature Permissions experience gives agencies more control while making the settings easier to understand and manage. This is especially useful for agencies managing several clients or offering different SaaS plans.

- **More feature controls:** Manage access to more than 80 HighLevel features.
- **Better organization:** Features are grouped into Categories, Modules, and individual Features.
- **More detailed control:** Choose specific features instead of managing only large areas of the platform.
- **Easier feature discovery:** Search for a feature instead of browsing through a long list.
- **Cleaner client experience:** Clients see the features the agency has made available to them.
- **SaaS plan support:** Pro agencies can choose which features are included in their SaaS plans.
- **Existing access is preserved:** Existing subaccounts and SaaS plans were moved to the updated permission system without removing features they already had access to.

---

## **How Feature Permissions are Organized**

The new permission screen organizes features into three levels so agencies can find related settings more easily. Think of these levels as folders that move from a broad area of HighLevel down to a specific feature.

The three levels are:

**Category:** A large area of HighLevel.

**Module:** A group of related tools inside that category.

**Feature:** A specific tool or function that can be controlled.

For example:

- **Category:** CRM
- **Module:** CRM core
- **Feature:** Contacts & Conversations

The CRM category may also contain other features such as:

- Custom Objects
- Smartlists
- Tags
- Email System
- Opportunities
- Phone System

This structure makes it easier to find the exact feature you want to manage.

**Screenshot description:** Add the **Feature Permissions** screen showing the searchable feature list, the Category > Module > Feature structure, selected counts, **Enable All** controls, and individual feature checkboxes.

---

## **Understanding the Selected Feature Counts**

The numbers beside Categories and Modules help you quickly see how many features are currently enabled. This makes it easier to review permissions without opening every group.

For example:

- **AI Agents (6/6)** means all 6 available AI Agent features are selected.
- **CRM (1/7)** means 1 of the 7 available CRM features is selected.
- **Features (22/63 selected)** shows the total number of currently selected features in that permission setup.

These counts update as features are selected or removed.

---

## **Search for a Feature**

The search field helps agencies quickly find a feature without opening each Category and Module. This is useful when you already know which feature you want to enable or disable.

Use the **Search features** field at the top of the permission list and enter the name of the feature you are looking for.

For example, you can search for:

- Phone System
- Opportunities
- Smartlists
- Calendar
- AI Agents

The matching feature can then be reviewed and managed from the results.

---

## **Feature Permissions for Individual Subaccounts**

Subaccount-level permissions are useful when one client needs a different set of HighLevel features from your other clients. These settings control what is available inside that specific subaccount.

An agency can review and manage Feature Permissions while managing an individual client.

This allows you to:

- Review the features currently available to the subaccount.
- Find a feature using search.
- Open Categories and Modules to locate individual features.
- Enable or disable supported features for that client.
- Review the selected feature count.

Feature Permissions control what the **subaccount itself** can access.

They are different from individual user permissions, which control what a specific person inside that subaccount can access.

---

## **Feature Permissions for SaaS Plans**

SaaS plan permissions let Pro agencies decide which HighLevel features are included with a plan. This makes it easier to offer different feature packages without manually setting up every new client.

When creating or editing a SaaS plan, the agency can select the features included with that plan.

When a subaccount subscribes to the SaaS plan, the plan's Feature Permissions are applied to that subaccount.

For example, an agency could create:

- A basic plan with CRM and Calendar access.
- A higher plan with CRM, Calendar, Automation, and AI features.

The exact features available depend on what the agency selects for the plan.

```
Note: At least one feature must be selected before a SaaS plan can be saved.
```

---

## **Feature Permissions vs. User Permissions**

Feature Permissions and User Permissions control different levels of access. Understanding the difference helps prevent situations where a user permission is enabled but the feature is still unavailable.

**Feature Permissions** control what the entire subaccount can access.

**User Permissions** control what an individual user inside that subaccount can access.

For example:

1. The agency enables **Opportunities** for the subaccount.
2. The agency can then decide which users inside that subaccount are allowed to use Opportunities.

If the subaccount does not have access to Opportunities, giving an individual user permission to Opportunities does not give them access to the feature.

A user can therefore have the same or less access than the subaccount, but not more.

---

## **What Happened to Existing Permissions?**

Existing subaccounts and SaaS plans were moved to the updated Feature Permissions system automatically. The migration was designed to preserve existing access so clients would not unexpectedly lose features they were already using.

Agencies do not need to recreate all existing permission settings from the beginning.

After the update:

- Existing subaccounts keep the feature access they previously had.
- Existing SaaS plans keep the access that was already configured.
- Agencies can use the new permission screen to review and adjust access going forward.

---

## **How To Manage Feature Permissions**

Managing Feature Permissions starts with choosing whether you are updating one client or configuring the features included in a SaaS plan. The new organized permission list then makes it easier to find and select the appropriate features.

### 

### Manage Permissions for a Subaccount

1. Open the agency area where you manage the client.
2. Select the subaccount you want to update.
3. Open its Feature Permissions settings.
4. Use **Search features** or browse the Categories.
5. Expand a Category to view its Modules and Features.
6. Select or clear the supported features you want to manage.
7. Review the selected feature count.
8. Save your changes.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079888236/original/eagMIdahjE_ttz2wYAGGLWXDy8GTkVWjMA.png?1788343721)**

### 

### Manage Permissions for a SaaS Plan

1. Open the **SaaS Configurator**.
2. Create a new plan or open an existing plan.
3. Go to the feature selection area.
4. Search for a feature or open the appropriate Category.
5. Select the features that should be included in the plan.
6. Make sure at least one feature is selected.
7. Review the feature choices.
8. Save the SaaS plan.

When the SaaS plan is assigned to a subaccount, the plan's feature configuration is applied to that account.

---

## **Troubleshooting Feature Permissions**

Most permission issues happen because the feature is unavailable at the subaccount level or because an individual user's permissions are more limited. Checking both levels can help identify why a client cannot access something.

**A client cannot see a feature**

Check whether the feature is enabled in the subaccount's Feature Permissions.

**A user cannot access a feature even though the subaccount has it**

Check that user's individual permissions. A subaccount can have access to a feature while a specific user is restricted from it.

**I cannot find a feature**

Use the **Search features** field. If the feature still does not appear, it may not currently have a configurable permission.

**The selected number is lower than expected**

Open the Category or Module and review the individual selected features.

**A permission appears unavailable**

Some permission controls may not be available in every area of HighLevel at the same time. Review the current settings shown in your account before making changes.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What does 1/7 mean beside a Category?**  
A: It means 1 of the 7 available features in that Category is currently selected.

**Q: Can I search for a specific feature?**  
A: Yes. Use the **Search features** field at the top of the Feature Permissions list.

**Q: Are Feature Permissions the same as User Permissions?**  
A: No. Feature Permissions control what the subaccount can access. User Permissions control what an individual user

can access inside that subaccount.

**Q: Can a user access a feature that is disabled for the subaccount?**  
A: No. User permissions cannot provide access beyond what is available to the subaccount.

**Q: Can Feature Permissions be configured in SaaS plans?**  
A: Yes. Pro agencies can select which supported features are included with each SaaS plan.

**Q: What happens when a SaaS plan is assigned to a subaccount?**  
A: The Feature Permissions configured for that SaaS plan are applied to the subaccount.

**Q: Did existing clients lose access when the new permission system was introduced?**  
A: No. Existing subaccounts and SaaS plans were moved to the new system while preserving the feature access they already had.

**Q: Does disabling a feature delete the client's existing data?**  
A: Feature Permissions control access to supported features. The article does not assume that changing access deletes existing client data; review the specific product's documentation before making decisions involving stored data.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [SaaS User Level Permissions Vs Sub-Account Level Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001184431-saas-user-level-permissions-vs-sub-account-level-permissions)
- [Getting Started with the SaaS Configurator](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008015-getting-started-with-the-saas-configurator)
- [Manage Agency User Roles and Permissions in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002543)
- [Convert Existing Sub-Accounts to SaaS Mode in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001188055-convert-existing-sub-account-to-saas-mode-subscription-plan)

###

title_en: How to Connect and Use Ask AI Through Calls and Texts
source_md:
Ask AI Phone Dispatch lets you call or text your Ask AI copilot without opening the HighLevel app. You can ask questions, manage supported business tasks, and continue conversations across phone calls and text messages. Connect your US phone number, verify it by SMS, and create a six-digit call PIN to secure phone access. This guide covers setting up Phone Dispatch, interacting with Ask AI, and reviewing your conversations in HighLevel.

---

# **What is Ask AI Phone Dispatch?**

Ask AI Phone Dispatch lets you access your existing Ask AI copilot through regular phone calls and text messages. Once you connect your personal US phone number, you receive a dedicated Ask AI number that you can call or text to ask questions and request supported tasks.

Phone Dispatch uses the same Ask AI capabilities available through the HighLevel web workspace and other Dispatch channels. You can retrieve business information, manage supported CRM activities, create content, or delegate work through natural-language requests.

Calls and text messages share conversation context. You can begin a request over the phone, follow up by text, or switch back to a call without starting the conversation over.

---

## **Key Benefits of Ask AI Phone Dispatch**

Phone Dispatch makes Ask AI accessible when you are away from your computer or unable to open the HighLevel app. It combines conversational assistance with the convenience of familiar calling and messaging.

- **Work while away from your screen:** Call or text Ask AI while traveling, between appointments, or away from your desk.

- **Manage business tasks remotely:** Look up contacts, add notes, update fields, move opportunity stages, and check upcoming appointments.

- **Delegate content creation:** Request blog drafts through a subagent or create reusable email templates with Email AI.

- **Keep important details in writing:** Ask questions during a call and request the key information by text for future reference.

- **Continue conversations across channels:** Switch between calls and texts while retaining the context of your request.

- **Share information through messages:** Send photos or files in a message for Ask AI to work with.

- **Start work with a quick text:** Submit requests without opening the HighLevel web workspace.

- **Stay connected without app data:** Access Ask AI through regular cellular calls or SMS without requiring an internet connection for the HighLevel app.

- **Review previous interactions:** Access phone and text conversations in HighLevel's Dispatch history.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Before connecting your phone, make sure you have access to a supported US number that can receive verification text messages. Phone Dispatch also applies number ownership and location restrictions to protect individual connections.

- **US numbers only:** Phone Dispatch currently supports US phone numbers with the +1 country code.
- **One number per location:** Only one phone number can be connected to the Phone Dispatch channel for a location at a time.
- **SMS verification required:** You must verify the phone number using a code sent by text.
- **Six-digit call PIN required:**Create a six-digit PIN during setup. The PIN helps verify your identity when making phone calls.
- **PIN recovery limitation:** Your call PIN cannot be recovered later. Choose a PIN you can remember.
- **User-specific connections:** A connected number belongs to the user who connected it. Other users cannot view or manage that user's connection.
- **Existing connections:** If your number is connected to another location or agency under your user, you can move it through the connection process.

---

## **How To Setup Ask AI Phone Dispatch**

Connecting your phone number allows Ask AI to recognize your number when you call or text the dedicated Ask AI number. Setup includes SMS verification and creating a call PIN to protect voice access.

### 

### **Step 1: Open Ask AI**

From your HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, click **Ask AI** in the left sidebar. Once the Ask AI workspace opens, select **Customize** to access your copilot settings.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105041/original/-Qa3CnwRczYV_qgaRV1lXKidltCAfz9i_A.png?1792802286)

### **Step 2: Go to Dispatch**

Under **Customize**, select **Dispatch** to view the channels you can connect to Ask AI. This is also where you can access your previous Dispatch conversations.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105043/original/znkPVBiyIkYmeWs6LkUxY-l3ApboMUbv-g.png?1792802303)

### **Step 3: Select the Phone Channel**

Under **Connected channels**, click **Phone** to open the Phone Dispatch settings. From here, you can start connecting your personal phone number to Ask AI.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105047/original/YAnwVtg2EDhqwil4ZhRgN1OuJuXT-DTJdg.png?1792802320)

### **Step 4: Start Connecting Your Phone**

Review the information about supported US phone numbers and the one-number-per-location limit. Click **Connect Phone** to begin setting up your connection.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105058/original/31qjBW9zymtPnTOqDw1ozCxhaba4RlreSw.png?1792802349)

### 

### **Step 5: Enter Your Phone Number**

In **Your phone number**, enter your US mobile number without the country code, since **US +1** is already selected. Click **Continue** to receive a verification code by text.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105061/original/U5Aowp8nrV1_1RQb3eIbV7smhdOED9_L3Q.png?1792802383)

### **Step 6: Verify Your Phone Number**

Check your text messages for the verification code and enter it in the **Verification code** field. Click **Verify** to confirm your number and continue to PIN setup.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105065/original/JfbuYGDKdHZIVQ68jetnrKXMrfz6hHi-JQ.png?1792802423)

### **Step 7: Create Your Call PIN**

Enter a six-digit PIN in **6-digit PIN** and enter it again in **Confirm PIN**. Click **Set PIN** to save it, and make sure you remember your PIN because it cannot be recovered later.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105071/original/6dh-0tjtHdi4tWQe56NWmYSAEll_bMGVNg.png?1792802449)

### 

### **Step 8: Copy Your Ask AI Number**

Once your setup is complete, you'll see **Phone connected** along with your dedicated number under **ASK AI NUMBER**. Click **Copy** to save the number, then use it to call or text Ask AI from your connected phone.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084105077/original/DPouTPOYuuLFYYX2uhFh-TtedRswNaE27Q.png?1792802480)

---

## **Use Ask AI Through Calls and Texts**

Once your phone is connected, you can call or text Ask AI to ask questions, manage business tasks, and get information without opening HighLevel. Both channels share the same conversation context, so you can switch between calling and texting without starting over.

### **Call Ask AI**

Calling Ask AI lets you speak your requests when typing isn't convenient. You can check appointments, look up contact information, or ask Ask AI to send important details by text.

1. Open your phone's calling app and dial your dedicated **Ask AI number**.
2. When prompted, say your six-digit **call PIN** to verify your identity.
3. Tell Ask AI what you need help with, just as you would in the HighLevel web app.
4. If you want to keep the information, ask Ask AI to send the details by text.

For example, you can say:

- "What appointments do I have today?"
- "Find the contact details for my next appointment."
- "Summarize my new leads."
- "Text me the details from this conversation."

### **Text Ask AI and Send Media**

Texting Ask AI makes it easy to handle quick requests when you can't make a call or open the web app. You can also send photos or files when your request requires additional information.

1. Open your phone's messaging app and start a conversation with your dedicated **Ask AI number**.
2. Type your question or task request, then send the message.
3. Continue the conversation by replying to Ask AI's messages.
4. When needed, attach a photo or file to provide more information for Ask AI to work with.

For example, you can text:

- "Add a note to Sarah's contact about our meeting."
- "Move the opportunity to the next stage."
- "What appointments do I have tomorrow?"
- "Create a follow-up email template for new leads."
- "Draft a blog post about appointment reminders."

### 

### **Switch Between Calls and Texts**

Phone Dispatch keeps your call and text conversations connected, making it easier to continue working when your situation changes. You can start a request on a call and follow up by text, or begin with a text and continue over the phone.

For example:

1. Call Ask AI and ask about your upcoming appointments.
2. During the call, ask Ask AI to text you the appointment details.
3. Open the text message to review the information.
4. Reply with a follow-up question or another task.

Ask AI retains the conversation context, so you don't need to repeat your original request.

---

## **Review Phone Dispatch Conversations in HighLevel**

Your Phone Dispatch conversations are saved in HighLevel, giving you a place to revisit previous calls and text exchanges. The Dispatch history supports searching, sorting, and pagination to help you find earlier interactions.

1. From your HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, click **Ask AI** in the left sidebar.
2. In the Ask AI workspace, select **Customize**.
3. Under **Customize**, click **Dispatch**.
4. Click **View Dispatch Sessions** to access your conversation history.
5. Review your saved Dispatch conversations and use the available history controls to find earlier interactions.

---

## **Move Your Connected Phone Number**

If your phone number is already connected to Ask AI under another location or agency, you can move that connection to your current location. Phone Dispatch recognizes connections owned by you and provides a confirmation before transferring the number.

1. From the destination HighLevel **Sub-Account** view, click **Ask AI** in the left sidebar.
2. Select **Customize**, then click **Dispatch**.
3. Under **Connected channels**, select **Phone**.
4. Click **Connect Phone**.
5. Enter your previously connected number in **Your phone number**, then click **Continue**.
6. If the number is already connected under your user, review the transfer confirmation and confirm the move.

```
Important: You can transfer a number connected under your own user, but you cannot take over a number connected by someone else. If another user owns the connection, HighLevel displays an Unauthorized message instead of offering a transfer.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Is the SMS verification code the same as my call PIN?**

No. The SMS verification code confirms ownership of your phone number during setup. Your six-digit call PIN is created separately and helps verify your identity during phone calls.

**Q: Can I ask Ask AI general questions without creating a task?**

Yes. You can ask questions, request information, or have a conversation without assigning a specific business task.

**Q: Can I use Phone Dispatch to get product or account support answers?**

Yes. When you ask a product or account support question, Ask AI can route your request to Support AI within the same conversation.

**Q: Can I schedule recurring tasks through Phone Dispatch?**

Yes. You can ask Ask AI to create recurring work through calls or texts. For example, you can request, "Every Monday at 9 AM, summarize new leads."

**Q: Can I use my custom Ask AI Skills through text messages?**

Yes. Custom Skills configured for your copilot can also be used through Phone Dispatch text conversations.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Ask AI Assistant](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005327)
- [How to Use Ask AI Dispatch on WhatsApp](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008779)
- [Ask AI Skills and Connectors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008434-ask-ai-skills-and-connectors)
- [How to Use Scheduled Tasks in Ask AI to Automate Prompts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007966-how-to-use-scheduled-tasks-in-ask-ai-to-automate-prompts)
- [Create Email Templates with Ask AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008500-create-email-templates-with-ask-ai)

---

title_en: Mail Loop Detected - Resolve Email Routing Conflicts
source_md:
EMAIL DELIVERABILITY

Mail Loop Detection Issues: Complete Troubleshooting Guide

Diagnose circular routing loops, fix the root cause, and get your sending back to normal safely.

What You'll Learn

Your email gets trapped in an endless routing cycle between mail servers, creating an infinite delivery attempt cycle. Mail servers detect this pattern and reject the message to prevent system overload. This prevents delivery and can impact your sender reputation if not resolved quickly.

## What's Happening?

Your email gets trapped in an endless routing cycle between mail servers, creating an infinite delivery attempt cycle. Mail servers detect this pattern and reject the message to prevent system overload. This prevents delivery and can impact your sender reputation if not resolved quickly.

Mail loop detection occurs when email forwarding rules, MX record configurations, or automated responses create circular routing patterns. Unlike other delivery issues, mail loops require immediate attention as they can quickly escalate and affect your entire sending infrastructure.

## Quick Diagnosis: Identifying Mail Loop Issues

Look for these bounce messages that indicate mail loop problems:

Common Loop Detection Messages

- "The message was rejected because it was caught in a routing loop between mail servers."

## Understanding Mail Loop Causes

Common Loop Scenarios

Email Forwarding Loops

- Email A forwards to Email B, which forwards back to Email A
- Catch-all addresses that forward to themselves
- Multiple forwarding rules creating circular references
- Auto-responders replying to automated messages

DNS and MX Record Issues

- Duplicate or conflicting MX entries
- Incorrect priority ordering in MX records
- Misconfigured mail server routing
- DNS propagation conflicts

Platform-Specific Considerations

Workflow-Related Loops

- Workflows triggering each other in circular patterns
- Email-based triggers creating infinite responses
- Auto-responders conflicting with external systems
- Conversation forwarding creating routing conflicts

Domain Configuration Issues

- Incomplete domain setup causing routing problems
- Authentication conflicts with forwarding rules
- Multiple email services competing for the same domain
- Cached routing information causing persistent loops

## Step-by-Step Mail Loop Resolution

Step 1

Immediate Diagnosis

**Check your domain configuration:**

1. **Navigate to Email Services**
   - Go to **Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domains and IP**.
   - Check for any warning indicators or incomplete setup steps.
   - Verify domain authentication status.
2. **Review recent changes**
   - Check if you've recently modified email forwarding rules.
   - Review any new workflow implementations.
   - Look for changes in conversation email integration.
3. **Examine bounce reports**
   - Go to **Marketing → Emails → Reports**.
   - Look for patterns in bounce messages.
   - Identify affected domains or email addresses.

Step 2

External Diagnostic Assessment

**For domain configuration issues:**

MX Record Analysis Tools

- **MXToolbox.com** — comprehensive email server testing
- **DNSChecker.org** — global DNS propagation verification
- **WhatsmyDNS.net** — DNS lookup verification
- **IntoDNS.com** — complete DNS health check

**For email header analysis:**

- **Collect email headers**
  - From bounced emails, copy complete headers.
  - Look for all "Received:" lines showing routing path.
  - Document repeated server names or IP addresses.
- **Use header analysis tools**
  - MXToolbox Email Header Analyzer
  - Google Admin Toolbox Message Header
  - Microsoft Message Header Analyzer

Step 3

Configuration Review

**Domain authentication check:**

1. Navigate to **Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain & IP → [Your Domain] → Authentication**.
2. Verify the SPF record.
3. Ensure the DMARC policy isn't causing rejection and re-routing.

**Workflow and automation review:**

1. **Check automation workflows**
   - Go to **Automation → Workflows**.
   - Look for workflows triggering each other in circular patterns.
   - Review email-based triggers and responses.
   - Identify any workflows that might create reply loops.
2. **Review email templates**
   - Navigate to **Marketing → Emails → Templates**.
   - Check auto-responder settings.
   - Review any automated email responses.
3. **Examine conversation settings**
   - Go to **Conversations → Settings → Email Integration**.
   - Check email forwarding configurations.
   - Review any routing conflicts.

Step 4

External Infrastructure Resolution

**Eliminate forwarding loops:**

- **Domain registrar/hosting provider review**
  - Log into your domain management panel.
  - Review all email forwarding rules and aliases.
  - Remove circular forwarding configurations.
  - Disable catch-all settings that forward to themselves.
- **Auto-responder management**
  - Disable auto-responders that reply to automated messages.
  - Configure proper filtering to prevent reply loops.
  - Set up appropriate sender exclusions.

**DNS record optimization:**

- **MX record cleanup**
  - Remove duplicate or conflicting MX entries.
  - Ensure proper priority ordering (lower numbers = higher priority).
  - Verify all MX records point to valid mail servers.
  - Wait 24–48 hours for DNS propagation.

## Advanced Resolution Techniques

Domain Reconfiguration

**When standard fixes don't work:**

1. Navigate to **Settings → Email Services → Sending Domains**.
2. Consider removing and re-adding your domain to reset cached routing.
3. Ensure all DNS records are properly configured before re-adding.
4. Test with small volume after reconfiguration.

Campaign Management During Resolution

- **Pause affected campaigns**
  - Go to **Marketing → Campaigns → [Campaign Name] → Pause**.
  - Temporarily halt campaigns experiencing loop issues.
  - Prevent further reputation damage.
- **Document evidence**
  - Collect bounce messages and error logs.
  - Save email headers showing loop patterns.
  - Track affected domains and volumes.

Testing and Validation Process

**Small-scale testing:**

1. Use **Marketing → Emails → Send Test Email**.
2. Send to various providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo).
3. Monitor email headers for proper routing paths.
4. Verify no loop indicators in delivery reports.

**Gradual campaign resumption:**

- Start with small segments of highly engaged contacts.
- Monitor delivery metrics closely.
- Gradually increase volume while watching for loop recurrence.
- Document successful delivery patterns.

## Prevention and Best Practices

Email Infrastructure Management

- **Avoid complex forwarding chains:** Keep email routing simple and direct.
- **Regular DNS audits:** Review MX records quarterly.
- **Test before implementing:** Always test forwarding rules with small volumes.
- **Document configurations:** Maintain records of all email routing setups.

Platform Recommendations

- **Use dedicated sending domains:** Separate marketing from operational email.
- **Monitor automation workflows:** Regular review for circular triggers.
- **Proper unsubscribe handling:** Ensure processes don't create reply loops.
- **Regular health checks:** Use the platform's monitoring features.

Early Warning System

- **Monitor bounce patterns:** Watch for sudden increases without campaign changes.
- **Track delivery times:** Unusual delays may indicate routing issues.
- **Review error messages:** Look for "too many hops" patterns.
- **Recipient feedback:** Monitor complaints about duplicate messages.

## Recovery Timeline and Expectations

Immediate Phase · 0–24 Hours

- **Pause affected campaigns:** Stop loop-generating sends immediately.
- **Document evidence:** Collect bounce messages and headers.
- **Identify root cause:** Determine forwarding or DNS issues.
- **Begin remediation:** Remove circular forwarding rules.

Technical Resolution · 1–3 Days

- **DNS propagation:** Allow time for MX record changes.
- **System cache clearing:** Wait for routing information updates.
- **Reconfiguration:** If domain reset is required.
- **External system updates:** Coordinate with hosting providers.

Validation and Recovery · 3–7 Days

- **Small-scale testing:** Verify loop resolution.
- **Gradual volume increase:** Monitor for recurring issues.
- **Performance stabilization:** Return to normal delivery rates.
- **Reputation monitoring:** Ensure no lasting impact.

## Monitoring and Maintenance

Regular Monitoring Schedule

Daily Monitoring

- Check bounce rates in **Reports → Email Performance → Delivery Metrics**.
- Review any new error message patterns.
- Monitor delivery time consistency.

Weekly Reviews

- Audit email automation workflows for efficiency.
- Review conversation email integration settings.
- Check for any new forwarding configurations.

Monthly Maintenance

- Comprehensive DNS record review.
- Email forwarding configuration audit.
- Domain authentication verification.

Key Performance Indicators

- **Bounce rate:** Should remain below 2% for healthy delivery.
- **Delivery time:** Monitor for delays indicating routing issues.
- **Error message patterns:** Track recurring loop-related errors.
- **Campaign completion rates:** Ensure consistent delivery performance.

## Working with Support

When to Contact Support

- **Persistent loop issues:** When standard resolution doesn't work.
- **Domain reconfiguration needs:** For complex setup requirements.
- **Workflow optimization:** Advanced automation troubleshooting.
- **Performance analysis:** Detailed delivery metric interpretation.

Information to Provide Support

- **Specific bounce messages:** Complete error text and headers.
- **Timeline information:** When loops started occurring.
- **Configuration details:** Recent changes to domains or workflows.
- **Affected volumes:** Scale and scope of the issue.
- **Resolution attempts:** What you've already tried.

## Success Indicators

You'll know your mail loop issue is resolved when you see:

- **Bounce rates return to normal:** Under 2% for healthy delivery.
- **No loop error messages:** Elimination of "too many hops" errors.
- **Normal delivery times:** Under 5 minutes for most providers.
- **Successful domain delivery:** Previously affected domains accepting mail.
- **Stable performance metrics:** Consistent delivery and engagement rates.

## Still Having Issues?

If you continue to experience mail loop challenges:

1. **Double-check all forwarding rules:** Ensure no circular references remain.
2. **Verify DNS propagation:** Allow a full 48 hours for changes.
3. **Review workflows:** Check for automation conflicts.
4. **Contact support:** Leverage platform expertise.
5. **Consider professional consultation:** For complex infrastructure issues.

Remember

Mail loops are technical issues that require systematic resolution. Focus on eliminating circular routing patterns, maintaining clean DNS configurations, and monitoring your automation workflows for potential conflicts.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if this is a mail loop versus a normal bounce?

Look at the bounce message itself. Normal bounces reference a specific reason like an invalid address or full mailbox. Loop-related bounces reference routing, "too many hops," or being "caught in a loop between mail servers."

Q: Can removing and re-adding my domain cause data loss?

Removing and re-adding a domain resets its cached routing and authentication status, but it doesn't delete your campaigns, contacts, or historical data. You will need to reconfigure DNS records and wait for re-verification.

Q: Will pausing my campaigns during resolution hurt my sender reputation?

No, pausing is protective, not harmful. Continuing to send into an active loop causes far more reputation damage than a short pause while you fix the underlying forwarding or DNS issue.

Q: How long should I wait after fixing DNS before resuming full volume?

Give DNS changes 24–48 hours to propagate, then validate with small-scale test sends before ramping back up. Jumping straight to full volume right after a DNS change risks masking a loop that hasn't fully cleared.

Q: Can a single misconfigured auto-responder cause a mail loop?

Yes. An auto-responder that replies to automated or bounce messages is one of the most common causes of a loop, since each automated reply can trigger another automated reply in return.

Q: Should I contact my domain host or support first?

Start with your own diagnosis using the steps in this guide. If the cause traces back to forwarding rules or DNS at your domain host, contact them directly; if it traces back to workflows or domain configuration, reach out to support.

title_en: Create Pages in the Page Builder
source_md:
Funnels & Websites

# Create Pages in the HighLevel Page Builder

Build multi-page funnels and websites without leaving the editor—create, organize, and switch between pages directly from the builder canvas.

What You'll Learn

This guide shows you how to create new pages, reorder page sequences, and quickly switch between pages—all from inside the HighLevel Page Builder—so you can build complete funnels and websites faster with less context-switching.

You'll learn how to use the pages drawer, page selector popover, drag-and-drop reordering, and search tools to stay focused on design and conversion rather than navigation overhead.

## What is New Page Creation from Page Builder?

New Page Creation from Page Builder is a Funnels & Websites enhancement that lets you create, configure, and organize pages without leaving the HighLevel Page Builder. Instead of navigating back to the funnel or website settings to add or reorder pages, you can perform all page management tasks directly from the pages drawer and a page selector popover inside the editor.

This streamlined workflow is available for both funnels and websites, and pairs with existing builder improvements—like enhanced drag-and-drop layout and modern navigation menus—to make multi-page experiences faster to build and easier to manage.

The feature includes four key tools: an "Add New Page" button in the pages drawer, a page selector popover on the action bar for quick switching, drag-and-drop page reordering, and a search bar for locating pages in large projects.

## Key Benefits

New Page Creation from Page Builder removes friction from multi-page builds and ongoing maintenance by keeping all page management tools inside the editor.

**Faster multi-page builds** — Create new funnel steps or website pages right where you're designing, instead of backing out to the settings dashboard.

**Less context-switching** — Stay inside the builder canvas while managing page names, paths, and order, which helps you focus on layout and conversion rather than navigation overhead.

**Intuitive drag-and-drop page order** — Reorder pages with the same drag-and-drop behaviors you already use elsewhere in HighLevel, making it easy to align page order with your navigation or funnel flow.

**Quick page switching** — Jump between pages from a compact page selector popover, ideal for working back and forth on headers, footers, or universal sections.

**Better scalability for large funnels and websites** — Use search directly in the pages drawer to quickly locate the right page when you're working with dozens of steps or content-heavy sites.

## Add New Page from Pages Drawer

The "Add New Page" option in the pages drawer is the primary way to create pages inline while you design. It keeps page creation, naming, and path configuration tightly coupled to the editing experience so you can build out full funnels and sites in one flow.

Step 1

Open your funnel or website in the builder

Go to **Sites → Funnels** or **Sites → Websites**, then click **Edit** on any page to open the Page Builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081948715/original/kroOnhY5lr5X2v4-0L1TkWbJd8iIlKfwBA.png?1790537471)

Step 2

Open the pages drawer

In the builder, open the **Pages** drawer (typically accessible from the left or side navigation, depending on your layout).

You'll see a list of all pages or steps in the current funnel or website.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809302/original/BUWt5LHYOqxbriKbxxx3TulaCQ2iukwDsQ.png?1786025418)

Step 3

Click "Add New Page"

At the top or bottom of the pages list, click **Add New Page**. This opens a modal form so you can configure the new page without exiting the builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809365/original/vuepBNxIrbugl38IOPGM4Qr9WJZ8ghoLzw.png?1786025470)

  

Step 4

Configure the new page

**Page Name** – Enter a clear, descriptive name (e.g., "Pricing", "Thank You", "Webinar Confirmation").

**URL Path / Slug** – Define the path visitors will use (e.g., /pricing, /thank-you). Keep it short, readable, and relevant.

If the path conflicts with an existing page in that funnel or website, adjust the path to keep URLs unique.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809692/original/h2olIuQk_joofQPaDFThIrI3XS4sQoH0bQ.png?1786025629)

Step 5

Create the page

The new page appears immediately in the pages drawer list and becomes available for editing in the builder.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809617/original/vQqJNAkHG8mWsdgIY1Tpni-49ngO1YtF2Q.png?1786025590)

Step 6

Start designing

Select the new page in the drawer to switch the canvas to that page and begin adding sections, rows, and elements.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809784/original/rdqDSD_GmxCIHp3_UxASAA0FB1vJB4trNw.png?1786025693)

Tip

Use consistent naming across funnels and websites (e.g., "Home," "About," "Services," "Contact") so it's easier to search and manage pages later.

## Page Selector Popover on Action Bar

The page selector popover lives in the secondary action bar and provides a compact, at-a-glance view of all pages. It's ideal when you want to switch pages quickly without opening the full drawer. This tool helps you keep your workspace clean—especially on smaller screens—while still giving you rapid access to navigation, landing pages, and other key steps.

Step 1

Locate the page selector

In the builder's secondary action bar (usually at the top), look for the current page name or a page dropdown icon.

Step 2

Open the popover

Click the page name or dropdown to open the page selector popover.

You'll see a list of all pages in the current funnel or website, often mirroring the order defined in your drawer.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077809898/original/EY7wXDxs8t95W046iIevTUgXa4EDJ5bAsA.png?1786025768)

Step 3

Switch between pages

Click any page in the list to instantly switch the canvas to that page.

This is especially helpful for jumping between shared components like navigation menus or footers that appear across multiple pages.

Step 4

Add a new page via inline form

Inside the popover, look for an inline new page form or an **Add New Page** option.

Enter the **Page Name** and **URL Path** directly within the popover.

Save to add the page to the funnel or website and to the list in both the popover and the pages drawer.

Step 5

Close the popover

Click outside the popover or hit the close icon to continue designing on the selected page.

Workflow Example

When building a three-step funnel (Opt-in → Sales → Thank You), keep the popover open so you can quickly bounce between steps as you adjust headlines, navigation labels, or universal sections.

## Drag & Drop Page Reordering

Drag-and-drop page reordering lets you organize page order while working in the Page Builder. Website pages can also be reordered directly from the Pages grid without opening the builder.

Where you can reorder pages

- **Pages drawer** – Reorder pages while working in the Page Builder.
- **Page selector popover** – Make quick page-order adjustments while staying focused on the builder canvas.
- **Website Pages grid** – Reorder website page cards directly from the Pages area. The new order saves automatically when you drop the page into position, with no confirmation step.

Step 1

Open the pages drawer or page selector popover

Use whichever view you prefer for page management.

Step 2

Click and hold the page you want to move

Hover over the page entry until you see a drag handle (e.g., three horizontal lines) or the cursor indicates you can drag.

Step 3

Drag to the new position

Drag the page up or down the list.

Release the mouse when it's at the correct position.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077810123/original/mo6biQo_4W4XGdOdYtJgSoipyeHIwfxWwg.gif?1786025926)

Step 4

Confirm in-builder reordering when prompted

When reordering from the **Pages drawer** or **page selector popover**, HighLevel may show a confirmation modal for sequences that rely on a specific order, such as webinar funnels.

Carefully review the warning and confirm only if you're sure reordering won't affect your intended flow.

Step 5

Verify navigation

If you use a Navigation Menu element that links to pages, verify that your menu still reflects the correct order and destinations after reordering.

Important

Reordering changes page order, not URLs. The URL paths you set earlier remain the same unless you edit them separately. This helps preserve existing links and SEO while still letting you refine the visitor journey.

## Search in Pages Drawer

The search bar in the pages drawer is designed for users managing large funnels or content-rich websites. It allows you to quickly locate specific pages based on name (and, in many cases, URL path), so you're not scrolling endlessly to find the one you need.

Step 1

Open the pages drawer

In the builder, open the **Pages** drawer to view the page list.

Step 2

Locate the search bar

At the top of the drawer, find the **Search** input.

Step 3

Type your query

Enter part of the page name (e.g., "pricing", "webinar", "thank") or a keyword from the URL path.

The list filters in real time to show only pages that match your search query.

Step 4

Select the page

Click the desired page from the filtered list to switch the canvas to that page.

Clear the search field to return to the full list.

Best practices for searchability

- Use clear, consistent naming when you create pages (e.g., "Webinar – Registration," "Webinar – Live Room," "Webinar – Replay").
- If you reuse funnel patterns across multiple client accounts, adopt a standard naming convention so anyone on your team can quickly find the right page.

Ready to Build?

Set Up Your Multi-Page Workflow

Follow the step-by-step guide below to start creating pages entirely from the builder

## How to Set Up New Page Creation from Page Builder

New Page Creation from Page Builder is enabled by default in the Funnels & Websites Page Builder—there's no toggle to activate. What matters most is understanding how to incorporate it into your everyday build workflow so you get the biggest efficiency gains.

Step 1

Open or create a funnel or website

Navigate to **Sites → Funnels** or **Sites → Websites** in your sub-account.

Open an existing funnel or website or create a new one, then click **Edit** on any step or page to launch the builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081948717/original/flLaoSPedMfm6DQqfoXYwyjCANrmXFB_UQ.png?1790537493)

Step 2

Plan your page structure

Decide the pages you need (e.g., Home, About, Services, Pricing, Blog, Contact or Opt-in, Sales Page, Order Form, Upsell, Thank You).

Having a clear list makes it easier to create pages in one pass.

Step 3

Create all required pages from the pages drawer

Open the **Pages** drawer.

Click **Add New Page** and configure the **Page Name** and **URL Path** for each page in your plan.

Repeat until all required pages exist in the funnel or website.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081948722/original/AhEASDXKJCXlARGN14Hq0WpNMd8AGSi_Sg.png?1790537511)

Step 4

Organize page order via drag and drop

From the pages drawer or page selector popover, drag and drop pages into the correct sequence.

Confirm any modals that appear, especially in webinar funnels, only when you're sure of the new order.

Step 5

Switch pages quickly while designing

Use the page selector popover to move between pages as you:

- Reuse navigation menus that link to multiple pages.
- Maintain consistent branding (colors, fonts, sections).
- Apply universal or global sections across pages (e.g., header, footer).

Step 6

Use search for large builds

For big projects (membership funnels, webinar ecosystems, large websites), rely on the search bar in the pages drawer to jump straight to the page you need instead of scrolling.

Step 7

Publish and test the full flow

After designing, preview key journeys (e.g., from opt-in to thank you) and verify:

- Navigation menus route to the correct pages.
- Page order aligns with your conversion path.
- URLs and internal links (buttons, menus, QR codes) point to the correct destinations.

title_en: Where and How to Configure the Missed Call Text Back Feature
source_md:
Phone System · Voice

Missed Call Text Back — Overview & Setup

Automatically text back every missed caller — and now, send from an eligible number even when the number they called can’t send SMS.

Overview

A missed call can be a missed opportunity. HighLevel’s Missed Call Text Back feature automatically sends a text message to callers you weren’t able to reach, so every inbound call gets acknowledged right away — even after hours.

In this article, we’ll walk through what the feature does, how to set it up, how voicemail settings work alongside it, and how HighLevel now picks the best eligible number to send your follow-up from.

What’s New

Your missed call text back now has a better chance of reaching the customer. If the number they called can’t send SMS, HighLevel automatically selects an eligible sending number instead of letting the follow-up fail. See [Smarter Sending Number Selection](#smarter-number-selection).

Important

Missed Call Text Back triggers an SMS notification for **every** missed call — even if the same caller tries multiple times within a brief timeframe.

To avoid sending multiple messages for repeated missed calls, we recommend you [create and customize the existing recipe in Workflows](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZwvCPUxgMaM) and personalize it to your preference (for example, add a 20 +/− minute Wait step, or filter using tags such as 1st call, 2nd call, and so on).

## What is Missed Call Text Back?

Missed Call Text Back is a feature that automatically sends a text message to a caller when their inbound call is missed. It helps your business acknowledge the missed call right away, set expectations, and encourage the caller to continue the conversation by text while your team is unavailable.

This feature is especially helpful for businesses that receive after-hours calls, handle a high volume of inbound calls, or want a faster first response without relying on a manual callback process.

Why This Matters

When someone calls your business and you can’t answer, that first follow-up can be the difference between a booked appointment and a lost lead. An automatic text keeps the conversation alive without anyone lifting a finger.

## Key Benefits of Missed Call Text Back

**Faster follow-up** — send an automatic text to missed callers right away so they know their call was noticed.

**Better customer experience** — a quick response reassures callers and gives them another way to continue the conversation.

**More personalization** — use merge fields to include details like the contact name or business name in your message.

**Simple setup** — enable the feature, customize the message, send a test, and save your changes.

**Improved lead response** — keep potential leads engaged when your team is unavailable to answer.

**Higher delivery success** — HighLevel automatically picks an eligible sending number so more follow-ups actually go out.

Setup Guide

Turn on Missed Call Text Back in five steps

Open Settings, find the feature under Phone System, enable it, write your message, and send a test.

## How to Configure the Missed Call Text Back Feature

Step 1

Open the Settings

In your sub-account, click **Settings** in the bottom-left corner.

![Settings option in the bottom-left corner of the sub-account](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066734906/original/OjFHNIoeULj0h8e-0ZPWraTyv3Akzr7Zhw.png?1773264995)

Step 2

Navigate to Missed Call Text Back

Follow this path inside Settings:

- In the left-side menu, click **Phone System**.
- In the top navigation, click **Voice**.
- Under Voice, open **Voicemail & Missed Call Text Back**.
- In the side panel, click **Missed Call Text Back**.

![Voicemail and Missed Call Text Back settings under Phone System > Voice](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066734967/original/hCHydUVEIyYEVu_BVFFDM246xJXztOXPSw.png?1773265066)

Step 3

Enable the feature

Select the checkbox to **Enable Missed Call Text Back** to turn the feature on. Then click **Customize** to tailor the message that goes out when someone misses you.

![Enable Missed Call Text Back checkbox with the Customize button](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066735467/original/4EWpJaWoQ9luC5sgv6_WANHjVeaO3_e4jA.png?1773266017)

Step 4

Customize the message

Clicking **Customize** opens a pop-up where you can craft your automated response. In the **Enter message** field, type the content you want sent when a call is missed.

You can also use the custom value tag icon to insert dynamic placeholders such as the contact’s name. Keep in mind that these only work if the system already recognizes the contact from a prior interaction.

![Customize message pop-up with the Enter message field and custom value tag icon](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066735521/original/pMhp0ohGahjc31N7CeMboNaTo8iHB28GJg.jpeg?1773266117)

Step 5

Send a test message

Below the message editor you’ll find a field where you can send a test message. Select the number you’d like to use to preview how the message will appear to customers.

After reviewing, click **Save** to finalize your settings and activate the updated Missed Call Text Back configuration.

![Test message field and Save button in the Missed Call Text Back settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066735539/original/r7OeTZfb0lEhUEmClUY-X3M8JnQH4dPtvA.png?1773266177)

You’re All Set

Missed Call Text Back is now live. The next time an inbound call goes unanswered past your ring timeout, the caller receives your message automatically.

## Voicemail Settings

Voicemail settings shape what happens when an inbound call is not answered. These options let you control how long the phone rings before voicemail triggers, and optionally replace the default voicemail greeting with a custom recording.

Setting 1

Adjust the incoming call timeout

This option sets how long the phone should ring before the missed call text back triggers. Use the slider to choose a timeout duration — 10 to 20 seconds is typically recommended.

![Incoming call timeout slider in voicemail settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066036199/original/NTcwyGYzj0J8NJgwbl1AhEdPpRwY4k4xBA.png?1772475723)

Setting 2 · Optional

Upload a voicemail audio file

You can add a custom voicemail message here if you’d like. Upload a pre-recorded file in mp3, wav, or a similar format. This plays instead of the carrier’s generic voicemail greeting.

![Upload voicemail audio file option in voicemail settings](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155066036213/original/375vNtucIblJVv2XLsfRPNTC-B-cJAWcJw.png?1772475746)

Note

The call timeout you set here determines when a call counts as “missed.” A very long timeout delays the text back; a very short one may cut off callers who would have answered.

## Smarter Sending Number Selection

A missed call can be a missed opportunity — and your follow-up text shouldn’t fail simply because the number your customer called can’t send SMS.

What Changed

**Previously:** Missed Call Text Back always tried to send the follow-up SMS from the same number your customer called. Some numbers are designed primarily to receive calls, or may not currently be eligible to send SMS — so your text back could fail even when another messaging-ready number was available in your account.

**Now:** HighLevel automatically chooses an eligible sending number, helping more of your missed call follow-ups reach your customers while staying aligned with messaging requirements.

### How the sending number is chosen

When a customer calls and you miss them, we’ll still try to text them back from **the number they called first**, as long as that number can send SMS. If it can’t, the system automatically looks for the next best option in this order:

| Priority | Number used to send the text back |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | The number the customer called — if it is eligible to send SMS |
| 2 | A number you’ve **successfully messaged this contact from before** |
| 3 | Your **default outbound number** |
| 4 | Another **eligible messaging number** available in the location |

Where This Helps Most

This is especially useful when calls come through **number pools, call tracking numbers, unverified toll-free numbers, or other numbers that aren’t eligible to send SMS**. Instead of attempting the text from a number that can’t send, we use an eligible number when one is available.

### What will you notice?

Most of the time, nothing changes — the missed caller simply receives your follow-up as expected.

Heads Up

In some cases the **SMS may come from a different number than the one they originally called**. That’s intentional — we choose a number that can actually send the message rather than letting an important follow-up fail.

### Why it matters

With smarter number selection, you can:

**Reach more missed callers** instead of losing the follow-up because one number can’t send SMS.

**Keep follow-ups automatic** without manually managing which number should be used.

**Stay aligned with messaging requirements** such as A2P and toll-free verification.

**Respond to potential leads sooner** and keep conversations moving even when you miss the initial call.

The Payoff

In short: if you have an eligible number available, we’ll automatically use it to give your missed call text a better chance of reaching the customer.

Good to Know

- Answered calls continue to work as before and will not trigger a text back.
- If **Missed Call Text Back** is disabled in your Phone System settings, no message will be sent.
- Your contacts’ communication preferences and DND settings continue to be respected.
- If there is no eligible number available, you’ll see the failed attempt in the conversation along with the reason, giving you clear visibility into what happened.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What number is used to send the missed call text back message?

We first try the number the customer called, as long as it’s eligible to send SMS. If it isn’t, HighLevel automatically falls back to a number you’ve successfully messaged this contact from before, then your default outbound number, then any other eligible messaging number in the location. See [Smarter Sending Number Selection](#smarter-number-selection) for the full order.

Q: Why did my missed call text come from a different number?

That’s expected behavior. The number the caller dialed most likely can’t send SMS — for example a number pool number, a call tracking number, or an unverified toll-free number — so we used an eligible number instead of letting the follow-up fail.

Q: What happens if no eligible sending number is available?

The attempt is logged in the contact’s conversation along with the reason it failed, so you have clear visibility. To fix it, make sure at least one number in the location is verified and eligible to send SMS (**A2P 10DLC** registration for local numbers, or toll-free verification for toll-free numbers).

Q: Do Missed Call Text Back messages count toward messaging limits?

Yes. These SMS messages count toward your phone messaging usage limits.

Q: Will a text be sent if the contact is on DND?

No. Your contacts’ communication preferences and DND settings are always respected, regardless of which sending number would have been selected.

Q: Do I need to change any settings to get smarter number selection?

No. There’s nothing to enable. As long as Missed Call Text Back is turned on in **Settings → Phone System → Voice**, the improved number selection applies automatically.

Q: Can I use WhatsApp instead of SMS for missed call follow-up?

Not with the SMS-based Missed Call Text Back feature. If you want to message missed callers through WhatsApp instead, use the separate [Missed Call WhatsApp Back](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002417) feature in HighLevel.

Q: Does Missed Call Text Back work for after-hours calls?

Yes. This feature is especially useful for after-hours missed calls because it automatically acknowledges the caller and gives them a way to continue the conversation by text even when your team is unavailable.

Q: Will an answered call still trigger a text back?

No. Only calls that go unanswered past your incoming call timeout are treated as missed. Answered calls never trigger a text back.
