Folder management lets you keep your agent organization aligned with changing teams, campaigns, and business needs. You can move agents into folders and update folder details without changing how the agent itself is configured.

### **Move an Agent to a Folder**

Moving an agent helps keep related Conversation AI agents grouped together and easier to locate.

1. From AI Agents > Conversation AI > Agents List, locate the agent you want to move.
2. Click the agent's three-dot menu.
3. Select the option to move the agent to a folder.
4. Choose the destination folder. Confirm the move.

### **Edit or Rename a Folder**

Updating a folder name allows your organization structure to evolve without requiring you to recreate the folder.

1. Locate the folder in the Agents List. Click the folder's three-dot menu. Select the edit option.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083554571/original/XD8Oq6yhQt173bSRAj52AR8eCchL33mNHw.png?1792183550)
2. Update the folder name or associated agents as needed.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083554554/original/JrcQh-XLs4cce8zs7Du0856Jwe3ZGaLLwg.png?1792183505)
3. Save your changes.

---

### **Delete a Folder**

### 

Delete folders that are no longer needed to keep the Agents List focused on your current organization structure.

1. Locate the folder you want to remove. Click the folder's three-dot menu.
2. Select Delete. Confirm the action when prompted.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083554599/original/Wr2vbwJVsiUCdiBewqoXcdDRIhAZxvtIqA.png?1792183598)

---

## **Browse Agents Inside a Folder**

Opening a folder gives you a focused view of only the Conversation AI agents associated with that group. This makes it easier to work with a particular department or use case without browsing unrelated agents.

When you open a folder, you can:

- View the agents assigned to that folder.
- Search within the folder.
- Switch between available list layouts.
- Use Add Agents to associate additional agents with the folder.
- Use the breadcrumb navigation to return to the main Agents List.

**Table View**

Table view provides a compact, information-dense layout for reviewing agents and folders. It is useful when you want to compare several agents quickly across details such as status, type, assigned channels, and recent updates.

The table can display information such as:

- Agent name
- Status
- Agent type
- Assigned channels
- Last updated information
- Folder entries

Use the view controls at the top of the Agents List to switch between Table and Grid views.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083554655/original/RziJz2J4MAp9SYPm8438IolrB2zjugRTpw.png?1792183748)

**Grid View**

Grid view provides a more visual way to browse folders and agents. Folder cards summarize the agents inside them, while agent cards surface important information such as status, agent type, and configured channels.

Grid view can help when you want to:

- Scan folders visually.
- See which agents belong to each folder.
- Compare agent status at a glance.
- Review configured channels without opening the agent.
- Identify agents that show Not configured for channel deployment.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083554660/original/T9ALcSYVGrZLHSmcQ5fh2Q-nh55vs2y_4w.png?1792183763)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do folders change how a Conversation AI agent responds?**No folder behavior in the supplied release indicates that folders change agent logic or deployment. Folders are used to organize and browse agents.

**Q: Where do I create folders for Conversation AI agents?**Go to AI Agents > Conversation AI > Agents List, then select Create folder.

**Q: Can I add existing agents when I create a folder?**Yes. The release supports selecting existing agents while creating a folder.

**Q: Can I add more agents after a folder has already been created?**Yes. You can move agents into a folder from the agent menu, and the folder view includes an Add Agents option.

**Q: Does Grid view change the way my agents are configured?**No. Grid view changes how agents and folders are displayed in the Agents List.

**Q: What does “Not configured” mean on an agent card?**It indicates that the agent does not currently show a configured channel assignment in the Agents List.

**Q: Can I configure an agent's channels directly from the Agents List?**The Agents List displays channel information, but channel deployment and routing are configured from the individual agent's deployment settings. HighLevel Support Portal

**Q: Can one Conversation AI agent belong to multiple folders?**The supplied Conversation AI release information does not specify this behavior. Voice AI has separate documented folder behavior, but that should not be assumed to apply to Conversation AI. HighLevel Support Portal

**Q: What happens to agents if I delete a Conversation AI folder?**The release confirms that folders can be deleted but does not document what happens to the agents inside them. Confirm this behavior before adding a definitive answer to the published article.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Create and Set Up a Conversation AI Bot in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Manage Conversation AI Bot Channels and Routing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008266?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Guide to Understanding Conversation AI Bot in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001335?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Guided Form Based Setup for Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005382-guided-form-based-setup-for-conversation-ai?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI Flow Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006515?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Conversation AI Advanced Settings Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004415-advanced-settings-overview-conversation-ai?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Recommendations and Best Practices for Maintaining a Positive Caller Reputation
source_md:
Maintaining consumer trust in the voice communication channel is critical. Consumers expect to receive wanted and personalized communications while being protected from spam and unwanted calls.

This guide provides recommendations and best practices for maintaining a positive caller reputation and links to additional HighLevel resources for caller authentication, identification, and reputation management.

---

## **Why Does Caller Reputation Matter?**

Throughout the industry, there are continued efforts to reduce unwanted calls to consumers. These efforts can sometimes lead to legitimate business calls being screened, blocked, or marked as spam.

Following good calling practices and using HighLevel’s caller trust and reputation tools can help reduce the likelihood of your calls being flagged and improve caller recognition.

If your calls are already being marked as spam, see [Why are my Calls marked as Spam, and How can I avoid it?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001231665-why-are-my-calls-marked-as-spam-and-how-can-i-avoid-it-lc-phone-).

For an overview of the tools HighLevel provides for caller authentication, caller identification, and reputation management, see [Branded Calling: Improve Your Phone Number Reputation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008284-branded-calling-improve-your-phone-number-reputation).

---

## **Trust Center**

LC Phone provides the Trust Center to help businesses establish trust within the telephony ecosystem.

HighLevel provides several tools that support different aspects of caller trust and phone number reputation:

- [SHAKEN/STIR](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006429-what-is-shaken-stir-) authenticates caller ID information and helps carriers verify that you are authorized to use the phone number displayed on an outbound call.
- [CNAM](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006430-what-is-cnam-) associates a U.S. phone number with a registered business or personal name. The receiving carrier and device ultimately determine whether the registered name is displayed.
- [Voice Integrity](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005566-improve-your-phone-number-s-reputation-with-voice-integrity) submits eligible U.S. phone numbers to caller-ID analytics providers for reputation review when legitimate numbers are incorrectly receiving spam or nuisance labels.

For a broader explanation of how these tools work together, see [Branded Calling: Improve Your Phone Number Reputation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008284-branded-calling-improve-your-phone-number-reputation).

---

## **Telemarketing and Advertising Requirements & Best Practices**

If LC Phone Voice Services are used to place telemarketing or advertising voice calls, applicable industry best practices and rules governing telemarketing calls must be followed to reduce the risk of disciplinary action by CPaaS providers, carriers, or third-party analytics providers.

If special circumstances justify deviation from these guidelines, such as a recruiting website with multiple positions or debt collection, document your practices appropriately.

**1. Compliance with TSR, TCPA, and Truth-in-Caller ID Requirements for U.S. Calls**

a. Consent

Unless an exception applies, calls covered by the TCPA must have consent from the call recipient. The level of consent required depends on whether the call is classified as informational or telemarketing.

- For telemarketing calls, prior express written consent may be required.
- For informational calls, prior express consent may be required.

Businesses are responsible for understanding and complying with the laws and regulations applicable to their use case.

**b. Time Restrictions**

Callers should comply with applicable calling-hour restrictions based on the recipient’s local time. Some states or jurisdictions may impose additional restrictions.

Keep in mind that a phone number’s area code may not accurately indicate the recipient’s current location.

**c. Repeated Calls**

Do not repeatedly or continuously call a person with the intent to annoy, abuse, or harass them.

Calling frequency should be appropriate for the use case and should respect the recipient’s preferences and applicable requirements.

**d. Call Content**

Additional disclosures may apply when accepting sales orders, charitable contributions, or marketing certain regulated products or services.

e. Reassigned Numbers

Where applicable, calling lists should be reviewed for reassigned numbers to reduce the likelihood of contacting someone who did not provide consent.

**2. Best Practices When Placing a Call**

- When calling the same number repeatedly, use the same caller ID whenever appropriate.
- Associate a descriptive Caller ID Name with your outbound number. See [What is CNAM?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006430-what-is-cnam-) for requirements and setup instructions.
- Clearly announce the caller or business name at the beginning of the call.
- Be prepared to explain how the recipient’s consent to receive the call was obtained.  
    
  Example:  
  “Hi, this is Gloria with AAA Insurance. You requested that we contact you regarding an auto insurance quote. Is Conrad available?”
- Allow sufficient time for the recipient to answer the call and avoid silent calls.

**3. Managing Customer Concerns When Calls Are Answered**

- Address questions or concerns about the nature of the call before continuing.
- Be prepared to provide a website URL or phone number where the recipient can find more information about your business.
- If the recipient states that they did not consent, are no longer interested, or wish to revoke consent, honor the request and update your calling list accordingly.
- When leaving voicemail, clearly identify your business and provide appropriate callback information.

---

## **Positive Caller Reputation Basic Do’s and Don’ts**

- Comply with applicable Do Not Call requirements and other calling regulations relevant to your business.
- Keep your calling lists up to date and remove phone numbers that no longer connect.
- Avoid repeatedly calling unassigned or disconnected numbers.
- Provide contact information recipients can use to reach your business or report concerns.
- Avoid suspicious calling patterns such as inappropriate neighbor calling, where the caller ID closely matches the recipient’s area code and prefix. These patterns are commonly associated with unwanted calls and may affect caller reputation.
- Use accurate caller identification and maintain consistent calling behavior.

For additional guidance on factors that may contribute to spam labeling, see [Why are my Calls marked as Spam, and How can I avoid it?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001231665-why-are-my-calls-marked-as-spam-and-how-can-i-avoid-it-lc-phone-).

---

## **Be Consistent in Your Phone Number Usage**

Avoid using the same phone number for unrelated purposes, such as marketing campaigns, surveys, and support callbacks.

Aligning the context and purpose of calls made from a specific phone number can help establish consistent calling patterns.

For more information about maintaining caller reputation, see [Branded Calling: Improve Your Phone Number Reputation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008284-branded-calling-improve-your-phone-number-reputation).

---

## **Be Consistent in Your Outbound Call Volume**

- If your use case allows it, maintain relatively consistent calling volume and avoid unusual spikes.
- Gradually ramp up new campaign call volume instead of immediately moving from little or no activity to high volume.
- Avoid calling recipients excessively or outside appropriate calling hours.
- Respect recipient preferences regarding how often and through which channels they want to be contacted.

Consistent and permission-based calling behavior can help distinguish legitimate business communication from patterns associated with unwanted calls.

---

## **What to Do If Your Number Is Marked as Spam**

If you follow recommended calling practices but your legitimate U.S. phone number is still being marked as Spam Likely, review the available reputation-remediation options.

Voice Integrity

If your business meets the applicable requirements, [Voice Integrity](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005566-improve-your-phone-number-s-reputation-with-voice-integrity) allows eligible U.S. phone numbers to be submitted to supported caller-ID analytics providers for reputation review.

Free Caller Registry

If you cannot use the documented Voice Integrity process, review [Remediate 'Spam Likely' on your Caller ID using Free Caller Registry](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005891-remediate-spam-likely-on-your-caller-id-using-free-caller-registry).

For a complete explanation of spam labeling and the available remediation options, see [Why are my Calls marked as Spam, and How can I avoid it?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001231665-why-are-my-calls-marked-as-spam-and-how-can-i-avoid-it-lc-phone-).

---

title_en: Version History in Workflow AI Builder
source_md:
Workflow Automation

# Version History in Workflow AI Builder

Track and restore every AI-generated workflow iteration with artifact cards that preserve your entire build history.

What You'll Learn

The Workflow AI Builder tracks every iteration it creates. Each AI build or edit produces an artifact card in the chat, allowing you to restore any previous version in one click.

This article explains how artifact cards work, how to restore versions, and how version history integrates with the existing Version History tab to create a unified timeline of all workflow changes.

## What is Version History in AI Builder?

Version History in AI Builder preserves every iteration the AI Assistant creates when building or editing workflows. Each change generates an artifact card that appears inline in the chat conversation, creating a complete timeline of all AI-generated modifications.

These artifact cards allow you to restore any previous version with a single click, eliminating the need to manually rebuild workflows when an AI edit removes a trigger, overwrites an action configuration, or makes unwanted changes. All iterations remain accessible and restorable, creating a bidirectional and non-destructive version control system.

The feature integrates with the existing Version History tab, creating a unified timeline where AI-generated versions and manual edits appear together as a single source of truth for version numbering.

## Key Benefits

Version History in AI Builder transforms how you work with AI-generated workflows by providing safety, flexibility, and confidence when experimenting with changes.

**One-Click Recovery** — Restore any previous iteration instantly when an AI edit removes triggers, overwrites action configurations, or makes unwanted changes. No manual rebuilding required.

**Seamless Workflow** — Restore versions without leaving the AI Assistant or breaking your conversation flow. Continue working immediately after reverting changes.

**Safe Experimentation** — Try bold edits and aggressive changes with confidence. Compare results, then roll back instantly if the iteration misses the mark.

**Non-Destructive Versioning** — Restoring older iterations preserves newer ones. Jump back and forth freely between versions without destroying any iteration.

**Complete Transparency** — Visual indicators show which version currently matches your canvas, and which versions remain unsaved when auto-save is disabled.

## How Artifact Cards Work

Artifact cards provide visual representation and control for each AI-generated workflow iteration. Understanding their components helps you navigate version history efficiently.

Component 1

Artifact Card Generation

Every build or edit from the AI Assistant produces an artifact card that appears inline in the chat, positioned exactly where the change occurred in your conversation. This creates a chronological timeline of all AI-generated modifications.

Component 2

Current Version Indicator

The artifact card matching your current canvas displays a purple border. This visual marker ensures you always know which iteration you are viewing, even when multiple versions exist in the chat history.

Component 3

Restore Controls

Each artifact card includes a three-dot menu with "Restore this version" as an option. Selecting this option reverts your canvas to that iteration instantly. The purple border moves to the restored card, and the previously current card gains restore controls.

Component 4

Bidirectional Navigation

Restoring an older iteration keeps newer versions restorable. You can jump back and forth between any iterations without destroying them. No version is ever permanently deleted through the restore process.

[Screenshot: Artifact cards in chat showing purple border on current version and three-dot menu with restore option on previous versions]

Workflow Tip

Experiment Without Fear

Version history lets you try aggressive AI edits with complete safety. Test bold changes, compare results, and revert instantly if needed.

## How to Use Version History in AI Builder

Follow these steps to track, compare, and restore AI-generated workflow iterations using artifact cards.

Step 1

Prompt the AI Assistant

Open the Workflow AI Builder and prompt the AI Assistant to build or edit your workflow. The AI generates the workflow based on your prompt.

Step 2

View the First Artifact Card

An artifact card appears in the chat immediately after the AI completes the build. This card displays a purple border, indicating it matches your current canvas.

Step 3

Make Additional Changes

Prompt the AI to make another change to your workflow. The AI generates a new iteration and creates a second artifact card in the chat.

Step 4

Track Current Version

The purple border moves to the newest artifact card. The previous card no longer shows the purple border but remains visible in your chat history.

Step 5

Restore a Previous Version

Click the three-dot menu on any older artifact card and select "Restore this version." The canvas reverts to that iteration instantly. The purple border moves to the restored card.

Pro Tip

You can restore versions multiple times in any order. Newer iterations remain accessible even after restoring older ones, allowing you to compare different approaches freely.

## Understanding Unsaved Indicators

When auto-save is disabled for your location, artifact cards display an "Unsaved" pill to indicate which versions have not been saved manually. This indicator helps you track which iterations exist only in memory.

The unsaved indicator only appears when auto-save is turned off. When auto-save is enabled, all iterations are saved automatically and the indicator never appears on artifact cards.

Important

If you see an "Unsaved" pill on an artifact card, manually save the workflow before navigating away to preserve that iteration. Unsaved versions will be lost if you leave the workflow without saving.

[Screenshot: Artifact card showing "Unsaved" pill when auto-save is disabled]

## Integration with Version History Tab

Artifact cards in the AI Builder sync with the Version History tab, creating a unified timeline where AI-generated versions and manual edits appear together. The Version History tab remains the single source of truth for version numbering.

Each artifact card includes a "Show in version history" option in its three-dot menu. Selecting this option opens the Version History tab and highlights the corresponding entry, allowing you to view the full context of both AI and manual changes.

Unified Timeline

All workflow versions—whether created by the AI Assistant or manual edits—appear in chronological order in the Version History tab. This provides complete visibility into your workflow's evolution.

[Screenshot: Version History tab showing both AI-generated and manual versions in unified timeline]

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens to newer versions when I restore an older iteration?

Newer versions remain fully accessible and restorable. Restoring an older iteration does not delete or destroy any newer versions. You can jump back and forth between any iterations without losing work.

Q: Do artifact cards appear for manual edits I make to the workflow?

No. Artifact cards only appear for builds and edits generated by the AI Assistant. Manual edits you make directly to the workflow canvas do not create artifact cards in the chat, but they do appear in the Version History tab.

Q: How do I know which version is currently on my canvas?

The artifact card matching your current canvas displays a purple border. This visual indicator updates automatically whenever you restore a different version or the AI generates a new iteration.

Q: What does the "Unsaved" pill mean on an artifact card?

The "Unsaved" pill appears when auto-save is disabled for your location and indicates the version has not been saved manually. You must save the workflow manually to preserve that iteration. This indicator never appears when auto-save is enabled.

Q: Can I restore a version from the Version History tab instead of using artifact cards?

Yes. The Version History tab displays all workflow versions, including AI-generated iterations. You can restore any version from the Version History tab using the standard restore controls. The artifact card's "Show in version history" option takes you directly to that version in the tab.

Q: How many artifact cards can appear in a single AI Builder conversation?

There is no limit to the number of artifact cards that can appear in a conversation. Every AI build or edit generates a new card, creating a complete timeline of all AI-generated changes for that workflow.

Q: Do I need to manually save after restoring a version?

Only if auto-save is disabled for your location. When auto-save is enabled, restored versions are saved automatically. When auto-save is disabled, you must save manually to preserve the restored version.

Q: Can I delete artifact cards from the chat history?

No. Artifact cards are permanent parts of the conversation history and cannot be deleted. They provide a complete record of all AI-generated iterations for reference and restoration.

title_en: How to Duplicate & Copy Pipelines to Sub-Account(s)
source_md:
This article explains how to duplicate an existing pipeline within a sub-account or copy it to other sub-accounts in HighLevel. This feature helps replicate pipeline structures without manually rebuilding them.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Duplicate & Copy Pipelines to Sub-Account(s)?](#What-is-Duplicate-&-Copy-Pipelines-to-Sub-Account(s)?)
- [Key Benefits of Duplicate & Copy Pipelines to Sub-Account(s)](#Key-Benefits-of-Duplicate-&-Copy-Pipelines-to-Sub-Account(s))
- [Duplicate vs Copy to Sub-Accounts](#Duplicate-vs-Copy-to-Sub-Accounts)
- [Permissions Required](#Permissions-Required)
- [What Does and Doesn't Get Copied](#What-Does-and-Doesn't-Get-Copied)
- [How to Duplicate a Pipeline in the Same Sub-account](#How-to-Duplicate-a-Pipeline-in-the-Same-Sub-account)
- [How to Copy a Pipeline to Other Sub-Accounts](#How-to-Copy-a-Pipeline-to-Other-Sub-Accounts)
- [Best Practices](#Best-Practices)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Duplicate & Copy Pipelines to Sub-Account(s)?**

Duplicate Pipelines and Copy Pipelines to Sub-Accounts help you reuse an existing opportunity pipeline instead of rebuilding it manually. This makes it easier to standardize sales processes, save setup time, and keep pipeline structures consistent across accounts. Teams can use duplication to create a version of a pipeline in the same sub-account, or use copy to send a pipeline to one or more sub-accounts.

Managing similar sales pipelines across multiple sub-accounts often requires repetitive manual setup. With this feature, agency admins can quickly copy pipelines to other sub-accounts, and users with the right access can duplicate pipelines within the same sub-account. This saves time and helps maintain consistency across accounts.

---

## **Key Benefits of Duplicate & Copy Pipelines to Sub-Account(s)**

- **Faster setup:** Reuse an existing pipeline instead of creating stages one by one.
- **Improved consistency:** Keep sales processes aligned across sub-accounts.
- **Simpler onboarding:** Roll out proven pipeline structures to new sub-accounts more quickly.
- **Less manual work:** Eliminate repetitive configuration when managing multiple accounts.
- **Safer testing:** Duplicate a pipeline in the same sub-account to test changes before wider use.

---

## **Duplicate vs Copy to Sub-Accounts**

Understanding the difference between these two actions helps you choose the right workflow for your goal. One option is designed for reuse inside the same sub-account, while the other is designed for distribution across multiple sub-accounts.

- **Duplicate:** Creates a copy of an existing pipeline inside the same sub-account.
- **Copy to sub-accounts:** Sends a copy of the pipeline to one or more different sub-accounts.
- **Use Duplicate when:** You want to test a variation, create a similar pipeline, or avoid rebuilding stages in the same account.
- **Use Copy to sub-accounts when:** You want to standardize pipeline structures across client or location accounts.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/YoGJ761c4jPQVFWtR6UQ+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+18.17.37.png)

---

## **Permissions Required**

Access to duplicate or copy pipelines depends on the user's role and pipeline permissions. Reviewing these requirements first can help explain why a user may not see one or both actions in the pipeline menu.

- **Duplicate pipeline:** Available to users with **Edit access** to that pipeline.
- **Copy to sub-accounts:** Available to **Agency Admins only**.

---

## **What Does and Doesn't Get Copied**

Knowing what transfers with the pipeline helps set the right expectations before you duplicate or copy it. This is especially important when working across sub-accounts, where some settings do not move with the pipeline.

When you **duplicate a pipeline within the same sub-account**, the following are copied:

- Pipeline stages
- Pipeline permissions
- Colored smart tags
- Chart visibility settings

When you **copy a pipeline to other sub-accounts**, the following are copied:

- Pipeline stages
- Chart visibility settings

The following items are **not copied**:

- Records
- Automations
- Reports
- Custom fields

When copying to other sub-accounts, the following are also **not copied**:

- Pipeline permissions
- Colored smart tags

---

## **How to Duplicate a Pipeline in the Same Sub-account**

Duplicating a pipeline **creates a copy** **within** the **same sub-account**.

1. Go to **Opportunities** > **Pipelines**
2. Find the pipeline you want to duplicate and click the **three-dot menu** on the right and select **Duplicate**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/mJPEKAEkS8TZRmLCvkzP+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+18.55.02.png)
3. A **Duplicate Pipeline** window will appear.
4. Update the **Pipeline Name:**Enter a new name for the duplicated pipeline. A default name will appear with “(copy)” added.
5. **Set pipeline display colors:** Choose how stage colors appear across your pipeline views.
6. **Modify Pipeline Stages:**Rearrange, rename, add/remove stages.
7. **Choose show in report options:** Select whether each stage should appear in your default dashboard. Disabling all stages hides the pipeline from the dashboard.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/UhgM6olratSUK2ZujeTr+/GIF+Recording+2026-04-14+at+19.42.09.gif)
8. The following **elements** **will** **be** **copied** **automatically**:  
     
   - Pipeline stages
   - Chart visibility settings
   - Smart tag colors
   - Pipeline permissions
9. The following **will NOT be copied**:  
     
   - Opportunity records
   - Automations
   - Reports
   - Custom fields
10. Click **Duplicate** to create the new pipeline.  
      
    ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/S6sxzNLbXJ4duiNxQZ4t+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+19.44.50.png)
11. The duplicated pipeline will appear in the pipeline list. You can now edit the pipeline or start using it immediately.  
      
    ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/VJgNxxngEUikwjjXjRyK+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+19.45.20.png)

---

## **How to Copy a Pipeline to Other Sub-Accounts**

This feature allows **Agency Admins** to copy a pipeline to multiple sub-accounts at once.

1. Go to **Opportunities > Pipelines.**
2. Find the pipeline you want to copy and open the **three-dot menu**and select **Copy to sub-accounts**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/RQaSWpniymmX66xsJ20A+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+19.49.53.png)
3. In the **Copy to Sub-Accounts** window, enter the following details.
4. **Pipeline Name:**You can keep the same name or change it.
5. **Select Sub-Account(s):**Choose one or more sub-accounts where the pipeline should be created.
6. Click **Copy**and the pipeline will be created in each selected sub-account.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/bEYV4PLvhhUQS8HCGPeT+/Screen+Shot+2026-04-14+at+19.52.39.png)

---

## **Best Practices**

A few simple habits can make pipeline duplication and distribution easier to manage at scale. These recommendations help reduce confusion, improve organization, and make future updates easier.

- Rename duplicated pipelines immediately so they are easy to distinguish from the original.
- Use duplication to test pipeline variations before rolling them out more broadly.
- Standardize your preferred pipeline templates before copying them to other sub-accounts.
- Review which settings do and do not copy so you can complete any needed setup afterward.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I duplicate a pipeline inside the same sub-account?**

Yes. Use the **Duplicate** option from the three-dot menu next to the pipeline.

**Q: Can I copy a pipeline to more than one sub-account at the same time?**  
Yes. You can select multiple destination sub-accounts in a single copy action.

**Q: Who can copy pipelines to other sub-accounts?**  
Only **Agency Admins** can use the **Copy to sub-accounts** option.

**Q: Who can duplicate a pipeline?**  
Any user with **Edit access** to that pipeline can duplicate it.

**Q: Are opportunity records copied with the pipeline?**  
No. Records are not copied.

**Q: Are automations, reports, or custom fields copied?**  
No. Automations, reports, and custom fields are not copied.

**Q: Do smart tags copy with the pipeline?**  
Smart tag colors are copied when duplicating within the same sub-account, but they are not copied to other sub-accounts.

**Q: Do pipeline permissions copy with the pipeline?**  
Pipeline permissions are copied when duplicating within the same sub-account, but they are not copied to other sub-accounts.

**Q: Why do I not see the Copy to sub-accounts option?**  
That option is available to **Agency Admins only**.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Understanding Pipelines](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000001982)
- [Step-by-Step Guide: Creating Pipelines](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000001985)
- [How to Manage Pipeline Permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006523)
- [How to Color-Code Opportunity Pipelines (Smart Tags)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006642)

title_en: How to Setup Conversation SLAs
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/sQye\_iw7gxs?&wmode=opaque)

Conversation SLAs (Service Level Agreements) help teams maintain consistent response times and ensure no customer message is missed. This article shows how to setup and track SLAs for Conversations in HighLevel. 

> To access this feature, enable **"CRM Redesign - Conversations + Contact Detail Page (Upgrade)"** from Labs. SLA is supported only on the new Conversations page.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is a Conversation SLA?](#What-is-a-Conversation-SLA?)
- [Key Benefits of Conversation SLAs](#Key-Benefits-of-Conversation-SLAs)
- [How to Set Up Conversation SLAs](#How-to-Set-Up-Conversation-SLAs)
- [Understanding SLA Timers in Conversations](#Understanding-SLA-Timers-in-Conversations)
- [Filter and Sort by SLA](#Filter-and-Sort-by-SLA)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is a Conversation SLA?**

A Conversation SLA (Service-Level Agreement) is a response-time goal that counts down on each incoming thread inside HighLevel’s Conversations inbox. Timers start when a new customer message arrives and then turn grey (on-track), orange (due soon), or red (overdue) as the deadline approaches, giving agents a real-time visual cue to reply before the SLA is breached.

---

## **Key Benefits of Conversation SLAs**

- **Faster replies:**Teams always know how much time is left to answer.
- **Smarter prioritization:** Color-coded timers surface the most urgent threads first.
- **Channel flexibility:** Create one universal SLA or unique targets for Email, SMS, Facebook, WhatsApp, TikTok and more.
- **Accountability & reporting:** managers can filter, sort, and report on “Longest SLA Overdue” and “Next SLA Target” to spot coaching opportunities.

---

## **How to Set Up Conversation SLAs**

### **Step 1:** Navigate to SLA Settings

1. Click on **Conversations** module from your sub-account.
2. At the top panel, click on the**Settings** tab.
3. Click on the **SLA Settings** toggle to turn it on.
4. This will allow you to define how response time targets should apply across channels and how timers appear inside the inbox.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056272232/original/FP-IBsgSg9hDzf7iVIMaaiVRjvX-l9EPOw.jpeg?1760716664)

### **Step 2:** Choose How SLAs Apply Across Channels

1. Under **“How should SLAs apply across channels?”**, choose one of the following options:  
     
   - **Common SLA:** Apply the same SLA rule to all channels.  
     *Example:* All conversations—regardless of whether they come from Email, SMS, Facebook or TikTok—must be replied to within 1 hour.
   - **Channel-Specific SLA:** Define different response time targets for each channel.  
     *Example:* SMS replies must be sent within 15 minutes, while Email replies can take up to 2 hours.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064012601/original/y_EPiwyieZm55koUgIROCjhJp9yGWShKXw.png?1770047806)

### **Step 3:** Define SLA Timings

1. Set your preferred time limits to manage response expectations:  
     
   - **Due Soon:** The warning time before an SLA breach. When a conversation enters this window, the timer turns **orange**.
   - **Overdue:** The maximum time allowed to respond before the SLA is considered missed. Once breached, the timer turns **red**.

### **Step 4:** Choose How Workflow and AI Messages Affect SLAs

1. In this section, you can decide whether messages sent automatically—through **workflows** should count as valid replies for your SLA timers. This gives you flexibility to decide if automated responses should stop the countdown, or if only human replies should be considered.
2. Select how you’d like workflow or automation messages to affect SLAs:  
     
   - **Count all automation messages as valid responses** – The SLA timer stops whenever a workflow sends a message.
   - **Don’t count automation messages as valid responses** – The timer continues running until a team member replies.
   - **Count messages only from specific workflows** – Choose certain workflows that can stop the timer, while others won’t.

#### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064013095/original/CKpEPhwCP8Rq1XcPiBCCsX00yp52aGoaOg.png?1770047998)

### **Step 5:** Choose How AI Agent Messages Affect SLAs

1. Decide how replies from your AI Agent should impact SLAs:  
     
   - **Count AI replies as valid responses** – The SLA timer will stop when the AI Agent responds. *(Default)*
   - **Don’t count AI replies as valid responses**– The timer continues until a human agent replies.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056272231/original/_x8H6_kSRuPEKMkviYI0ix8xT0a9QmI3Ow.jpeg?1760716664)

### **Step 6:** Save and Apply Settings

1. Once you’ve configured your preferences, click **Save**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056272230/original/HOZCSURngiUlOSWNU0VNH4z5GSwq9YomRg.jpeg?1760716664)
2. From this point on, all new incoming customer messages will automatically have SLA timers applied based on your setup. Existing conversations will continue to follow the SLA rules that were active before the change.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056272229/original/ArbKPwiroq3oHgpHvB5-yLKF_AuYo4Dm-w.jpeg?1760716664)

---

## **Understanding SLA Timers in Conversations**

When a new customer message is received, an SLA timer appears in  the **Conversation list panel** (left side of the inbox). These timers visually indicate how much time is left to respond and change color based on their current state. The timer disappears once an agent replies or manually marks the conversation as read.

| **State** | **Color** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Active** | Grey | SLA is on track and within the allowed time. |
| **Due Soon** | Orange | The SLA is approaching the response deadline. |
| **Overdue** | Red | The SLA time has been exceeded. |

---

### **Filter and Sort by SLA**

To make it easier for agents to manage workloads, Conversations includes SLA-based filters and sorting options.

- **Filter by SLA Status:** View only Active, Due Soon, or Overdue conversations.
- **Sort by SLA:** Organize conversations by Longest Overdue or Next SLA Target.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056272225/original/KKT08BzlWtP-Lxd4P3rB7JqkC-6NH2GBjQ.png?1760716663)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Will SLAs apply to existing conversations after I enable them?**  
No. SLAs only apply to new incoming messages created after the feature is enabled. Existing conversations will continue without SLA tracking.

**Q: What happens if I disable SLAs?**  
If SLAs are disabled, existing conversations will continue to follow their current SLA timers, but new messages will no longer have SLAs applied. You can re-enable SLAs anytime from the SLA Settings tab.

**Q: Do automated or AI replies stop the SLA timer?**  
Only if configured to do so. By default, workflow messages do not stop the timer  and AI messages stop the timer. You can adjust these options under “How Workflow and AI Messages Affect SLAs.”

**Q: Does SLA tracking consider business hours?**  
Currently, SLAs are based on calendar hours. Business hours configuration will be introduced in a future update.

**Q: Can I have different SLAs for each channel?**  
Yes. You can set a **Common SLA** for all channels or define **Channel-Specific SLAs** to set different response targets for each communication channel.

**Q: How will agents know if a conversation is overdue?**  
SLA timers inside Conversations change color to show status — **Grey (Active)**, **Orange (Due Soon)**, and **Red (Overdue)**.

**Q: Do SLAs apply to internal chats or comments?**  
No. SLAs apply only to customer conversations, not to internal team messages or comments.

**Q: Can I create reports or workflow triggers using SLAs?**  
Not yet. SLA-based workflow triggers and performance reporting will be available in upcoming phases.

**Q: If I modify my SLA settings, will they apply to all conversations?**  
No. Modified SLAs apply only to new incoming messages. Ongoing conversations will continue using the SLA rules active when they began.

**Q: If a contact sends multiple messages, how is the SLA timer calculated?**  
The SLA timer runs based on the oldest customer message in the conversation. This ensures the response time reflects how long the contact has been waiting, even if they send multiple follow-up messages.

---
